model_response:
**Chosen Method:** iDISCO+
**Chosen Labeling:** [Cx40 / Hcn4 + Alexa Fluor (secondary, e.g., Alexa Fluor 647), Cntn2 + Alexa Fluor (secondary, e.g., Alexa Fluor 568), DAPI]

**Justification:**
iDISCO+ is selected because it is optimized for whole-organ immunolabeling with organic solvent-based clearing (methanol dehydration + dibenzyl ether as RI-matching medium), which effectively delipidates dense myocardial tissue and removes heme/hemoglobin background via H₂O₂ bleaching—critical for a blood-rich heart. The methanol series enables deep antibody penetration into the compact ventricular wall. For Purkinje fiber labeling, a dual-antibody strategy is used: **Cx40** (gap junction protein highly enriched in Purkinje fibers and absent in working cardiomyocytes) as the primary Purkinje network marker, and **Cntn2** (Contactin-2, a cell-adhesion molecule specifically expressed in the cardiac conduction system including Purkinje fibers) as a co-label to confirm conduction system identity and improve network continuity visualization. Together they provide complementary, high-specificity labeling of the Purkinje fiber network. **DAPI** is added as a nuclear counterstain to provide anatomical reference of the ventricular wall layers (endocardium, myocardium, epicardium). Alexa Fluor dyes (647 and 568) are chosen for their photostability and compatibility with iDISCO+ organic solvents when used with secondary antibodies. This combination enables 3D reconstruction of the complete Purkinje network architecture, branching density, regional coverage, and spatial relationship to ventricular anatomy at whole-heart scale, imaged by light-sheet fluorescence microscopy (LSFM).

---

**Protocol Steps:**

**1 Pre-treatment and Heme Removal (Bleaching)**
1.1 Wash fixed whole mouse heart (10% neutral buffered formalin or 4% PFA fixed, post-fixed) with 1× PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 × 10 min)
1.2 Dehydrate in 20% (vol/vol) methanol in H₂O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
1.3 Dehydrate in 40% (vol/vol) methanol in H₂O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
1.4 Dehydrate in 60% (vol/vol) methanol in H₂O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
1.5 Dehydrate in 80% (vol/vol) methanol in H₂O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
1.6 Dehydrate in 100% methanol (anhydrous). (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
1.7 Dehydrate in 100% methanol (anhydrous), second change. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
1.8 Bleach with chilled 5% H₂O₂ in 100% methanol (1 vol 30% H₂O₂ : 5 vol MeOH) to remove heme pigment and reduce autofluorescence. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 16 hours, overnight, with gentle agitation)
1.9 Rehydrate in 80% (vol/vol) methanol in H₂O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
1.10 Rehydrate in 60% (vol/vol) methanol in H₂O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
1.11 Rehydrate in 40% (vol/vol) methanol in H₂O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
1.12 Rehydrate in 20% (vol/vol) methanol in H₂O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
1.13 Rehydrate in 1× PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
1.14 Wash in PBS/0.2% Triton X-100 (PTx0.2). (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 × 1 hour)

**2 Permeabilization and Blocking**
2.1 Incubate in permeabilization solution: PBS containing 0.2% Triton X-100, 20% DMSO, 0.3 M glycine. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours, with gentle shaking)
2.2 Incubate in blocking solution: PBS containing 0.2% Triton X-100, 10% DMSO, 6% normal donkey serum (NDS). (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 48 hours, with gentle shaking)

**3 Primary Antibody Immunolabeling**
3.1 Prepare primary antibody solution in PTwH (PBS + 0.2% Tween-20 + 10 µg/mL heparin) + 5% DMSO + 3% NDS:
- Anti-Cx40 (rabbit polyclonal or monoclonal, e.g., Abcam ab11370 or equivalent), dilution 1:200
- Anti-Cntn2 (goat polyclonal, e.g., R&D Systems AF4439 or equivalent), dilution 1:200
(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days, with gentle rocking; for a ~10 mm heart, extended incubation ensures deep penetration into compact myocardium)
3.2 Wash in PTwH (PBS + 0.2% Tween-20 + 10 µg/mL heparin). (Temperature: RT, Time: 5 × 1 hour, then overnight wash at RT with gentle agitation)

**4 Secondary Antibody Immunolabeling and Nuclear Counterstain**
4.1 Prepare secondary antibody solution in PTwH + 3% NDS:
- Donkey anti-rabbit Alexa Fluor 647 (Thermo Fisher A31573 or equivalent), dilution 1:400 (labels Cx40)
- Donkey anti-goat Alexa Fluor 568 (Thermo Fisher A11057 or equivalent), dilution 1:400 (labels Cntn2)
- DAPI, 1 µg/mL final concentration (nuclear counterstain for anatomical reference)
(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 5 days, with gentle rocking; protected from light)
4.2 Wash in PTwH. (Temperature: RT, Time: 5 × 1 hour, then overnight wash at RT with gentle agitation, protected from light)

**5 Dehydration for Clearing**
5.1 Dehydrate in 20% (vol/vol) methanol in H₂O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour, protected from light)
5.2 Dehydrate in 40% (vol/vol) methanol in H₂O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour, protected from light)
5.3 Dehydrate in 60% (vol/vol) methanol in H₂O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour, protected from light)
5.4 Dehydrate in 80% (vol/vol) methanol in H₂O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour, protected from light)
5.5 Dehydrate in 100% methanol (anhydrous), first change. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour, protected from light)
5.6 Dehydrate in 100% methanol (anhydrous), second change. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour, protected from light)

**6 Delipidation with Dichloromethane (DCM)**
6.1 Incubate in 66% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) / 33% methanol to initiate delipidation. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours, in fume hood, with gentle agitation, protected from light)
6.2 Incubate in 100% DCM, first change, to complete delipidation. (Temperature: RT, Time: 15 min, in fume hood)
6.3 Incubate in 100% DCM, second change. (Temperature: RT, Time: 15 min, in fume hood; tissue should sink to bottom of vial, indicating complete delipidation)

**7 Refractive Index Matching with Dibenzyl Ether (DBE)**
7.1 Transfer tissue to 100% dibenzyl ether (DBE, Sigma-Aldrich 108014, RI ≈ 1.562) for final optical clearing and RI matching. (Temperature: RT, Time: 4–6 hours or until tissue is fully transparent, without shaking, protected from light; replace DBE once after 2 hours if tissue is not yet fully clear)
7.2 Store cleared heart in fresh 100% DBE in a sealed glass vial until imaging. (Temperature: RT or 4 ℃, protected from light; stable for weeks to months)

**8 Mounting and Imaging Preparation**
8.1 Mount cleared heart in a custom glass chamber or FEP tube filled with 100% DBE (RI ≈ 1.562) compatible with the light-sheet objective (e.g., LSFM with DBE-compatible long-working-distance objective, 4× or 10× for whole-heart overview; 25× for Purkinje fiber detail). (Temperature: RT, Time: allow 30 min equilibration before imaging)
8.2 Acquire 3D image stacks using light-sheet fluorescence microscopy (LSFM):
- Channel 1: 405 nm excitation / 450 nm emission → DAPI (nuclear/anatomical reference)
- Channel 2: 561 nm excitation / 600 nm emission → Alexa Fluor 568 (Cntn2, Purkinje fibers)
- Channel 3: 638 nm excitation / 680 nm emission → Alexa Fluor 647 (Cx40, Purkinje fibers)
Step size: 2–5 µm for whole-heart overview; 1 µm for high-resolution regional analysis. (Temperature: RT, Time: per imaging session)
8.3 Process acquired 3D datasets using Imaris, Fiji/ImageJ (BigStitcher, 3D Viewer), or Arivis Vision4D for network tracing, branching analysis, regional coverage quantification, and co-registration with ventricular anatomy. (Temperature: RT, Time: as required)

**Chosen Method:** iDISCO+
**Chosen Labeling:** [Cntn2 + Alexa Fluor 647, Cx40 / Hcn4 + Alexa Fluor 546, DAPI]

**Justification:**
iDISCO+ is selected because: (1) it achieves excellent deep-tissue antibody penetration in large, dense organs such as the intact mouse heart (~10×8×8 mm) through organic-solvent-based delipidation, which is critical for labeling structures buried in the ventricular wall and septum; (2) it preserves antigenicity sufficiently for immunolabeling of membrane-associated proteins (Cntn2/Contactin-2 and Cx40); (3) the final refractive-index matching medium (DBE, RI ≈ 1.56) is compatible with light-sheet fluorescence microscopy (LSFM), enabling whole-organ 3-D reconstruction of the conduction network. Cntn2 (Contactin-2) is the canonical surface marker of the cardiac conduction system / Purkinje fiber network and is the gold-standard immunolabel for this cell population. Cx40 (Connexin 40, gene *Gja5*) is the gap-junction protein selectively enriched in the His-Purkinje system and atrioventricular conduction axis, making it the ideal second channel to confirm conduction-system identity and assess gap-junction continuity. Together, dual immunolabeling with Cntn2 (Ch1, Alexa Fluor 647, far-red) and Cx40/Hcn4 antibody (Ch2, Alexa Fluor 546, orange-red) provides two independent, conduction-system-specific signals for co-localization, branching-pattern, and signal-continuity analysis across the subendocardial layer, septum, apex, and free wall. DAPI is included as an auxiliary nuclear counterstain to delineate gross tissue architecture; it is used only as a structural reference and does not define conduction-system identity.

---

## Protocol Steps

### 1 Pre-clearing Fixation Verification and Tissue Preparation

1.1 Confirm that the intact mouse heart has been perfused transcardially with ice-cold PBS followed by 4% (wt/vol) paraformaldehyde (PFA) in 0.1 M PBS (pH 7.4) and post-fixed in 4% PFA at 4 °C for 24 hours. Trim residual connective tissue and great vessels to within ~2 mm of the heart base. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 24 hours post-fixation)

1.2 Wash the fixed heart in 1× PBS (3 × 10 mL) with gentle rocking to remove residual PFA. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 × 30 minutes)

---

### 2 Dehydration (Methanol Series)

2.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in ddH₂O with gentle rocking. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

2.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in ddH₂O with gentle rocking. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

2.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in ddH₂O with gentle rocking. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

2.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in ddH₂O with gentle rocking. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

2.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol (anhydrous) with gentle rocking. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

2.6 Repeat incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol (anhydrous) to ensure complete dehydration. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

---

### 3 Bleaching (H₂O₂ / Methanol)

3.1 Prepare fresh bleaching solution: 1 volume 30% H₂O₂ mixed with 5 volumes 100% methanol (final ~5% H₂O₂ in methanol, vol/vol). Pre-chill to 4 °C. Incubate the heart in this solution with gentle rocking to reduce autofluorescence from cardiac myoglobin and hemoglobin. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 16 hours)

3.2 Remove bleaching solution. Wash with 100% methanol (3 × 10 mL) with gentle rocking. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 × 30 minutes)

---

### 4 Rehydration (Methanol Series, Reverse)

4.1 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in ddH₂O with gentle rocking. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

4.2 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in ddH₂O with gentle rocking. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

4.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in ddH₂O with gentle rocking. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

4.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in ddH₂O with gentle rocking. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

4.5 Incubation with 1× PBS (pH 7.4) with gentle rocking. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

4.6 Repeat wash with fresh 1× PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

---

### 5 Permeabilization and Blocking

5.1 Incubation with permeabilization / blocking solution: 0.2% (wt/vol) gelatin, 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100, 0.01% (wt/vol) sodium azide in 1× PBS (PTxwH buffer) with gentle rocking. This step permeabilizes the dense cardiac tissue and blocks non-specific antibody binding. (Temperature: 37 °C, Time: 24 hours)

5.2 Replace with fresh PTxwH blocking solution and continue incubation. (Temperature: 37 °C, Time: 24 hours)

---

### 6 Primary Antibody Immunolabeling

6.1 Prepare primary antibody cocktail in PTxwH buffer:
- Anti-Cntn2 (Contactin-2) rabbit polyclonal antibody at 1:200 dilution (targeting Purkinje fiber network surface marker)
- Anti-Cx40 (Connexin 40 / *Gja5*) goat polyclonal antibody at 1:200 dilution (targeting gap-junction protein of the His-Purkinje axis)
Total volume: sufficient to fully submerge the heart (~500 µL–1 mL in a 1.5 mL tube or sealed chamber).

6.2 Incubate the heart in primary antibody cocktail with gentle rocking. (Temperature: 37 °C, Time: 48 hours)

6.3 Continue incubation with the same primary antibody cocktail (replace with fresh solution if volume has reduced). (Temperature: 37 °C, Time: 48 hours)

6.4 Wash with PTxwH buffer (5 × 10 mL) with gentle rocking to remove unbound primary antibodies. (Temperature: RT, Time: 5 × 1 hour)

6.5 Perform an extended overnight wash in PTxwH buffer with gentle rocking. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)

---

### 7 Secondary Antibody Immunolabeling

7.1 Prepare secondary antibody cocktail in PTxwH buffer:
- Donkey anti-rabbit IgG conjugated to Alexa Fluor 647 at 1:400 dilution (for Cntn2 detection, Ch1, excitation ~650 nm, emission ~668 nm)
- Donkey anti-goat IgG conjugated to Alexa Fluor 546 at 1:400 dilution (for Cx40 detection, Ch2, excitation ~556 nm, emission ~573 nm)
- DAPI at 5 µg/mL final concentration (auxiliary nuclear counterstain, Ch0, excitation ~360 nm, emission ~460 nm)
Protect from light throughout all subsequent steps.

7.2 Incubate the heart in secondary antibody / DAPI cocktail with gentle rocking, protected from light. (Temperature: 37 °C, Time: 48 hours)

7.3 Continue incubation with fresh secondary antibody / DAPI cocktail, protected from light. (Temperature: 37 °C, Time: 24 hours)

7.4 Wash with PTxwH buffer (5 × 10 mL) with gentle rocking, protected from light. (Temperature: RT, Time: 5 × 1 hour)

7.5 Perform an extended overnight wash in PTxwH buffer with gentle rocking, protected from light. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)

---

### 8 Second Dehydration (Methanol Series, Pre-clearing)

8.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in ddH₂O, protected from light. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

8.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in ddH₂O, protected from light. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

8.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in ddH₂O, protected from light. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

8.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in ddH₂O, protected from light. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

8.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol (anhydrous), protected from light. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

8.6 Repeat incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol (anhydrous), protected from light. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

---

### 9 Delipidation with Dichloromethane (DCM)

9.1 Incubation with 66% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) / 33% methanol (vol/vol) in a glass vial with gentle rocking, protected from light. Perform in a fume hood. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours)

9.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DCM (2 × 10 mL) in a glass vial with gentle rocking, protected from light. Perform in a fume hood. The heart should sink to the bottom of the vial when delipidation is complete. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 × 30 minutes)

---

### 10 Refractive Index Matching with Dibenzyl Ether (DBE)

10.1 Remove DCM completely by aspiration. Immediately transfer the heart to 100% (vol/vol) dibenzyl ether (DBE; Sigma-Aldrich, catalog 108014; RI ≈ 1.56) in a glass vial. Do not seal with rubber; use glass or PTFE caps. Incubate without shaking, protected from light, until the heart becomes fully transparent. (Temperature: RT, Time: 4 hours)

10.2 Replace with fresh 100% (vol/vol) DBE and continue incubation without shaking, protected from light, until imaging. The heart should appear optically clear. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours or until fully transparent)

---

### 11 Sample Mounting and Imaging Preparation

11.1 Transfer the DBE-cleared heart to a custom glass-bottom imaging chamber or a 1.5 mm borosilicate glass cuvette compatible with the light-sheet fluorescence microscope (LSFM) objective (e.g., 4× or 12× LSFM objective with working distance ≥ 10 mm). Fill the chamber with 100% DBE as the immersion / imaging medium. Seal to prevent evaporation. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes equilibration)

11.2 Orient the heart with the anterior surface facing the light sheet for initial acquisition of the subendocardial Purkinje network. Plan acquisition in three orientations (anterior, posterior, lateral) to achieve complete coverage of the subendocardial layer, interventricular septum, apex, and free wall. (Temperature: RT, Time: as required for mounting)

11.3 Acquire 3-D image stacks using the following channel settings:
- Ch0 (DAPI): 405 nm excitation laser, 420–460 nm emission filter (nuclear counterstain / structural reference only)
- Ch1 (Alexa Fluor 647 / Cntn2): 638 nm excitation laser, 660–720 nm emission filter (Purkinje fiber network)
- Ch2 (Alexa Fluor 546 / Cx40): 561 nm excitation laser, 570–620 nm emission filter (gap-junction conduction axis)
Recommended z-step: 2–5 µm; tile acquisition with ≥10% overlap for full-heart mosaic reconstruction. (Temperature: RT, Time: per imaging session)

11.4 For long-term storage prior to imaging, keep the cleared heart in 100% DBE in a sealed glass vial, protected from light. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: up to 4 weeks)

**Chosen Method:** iDISCO+
**Chosen Labeling:** [Cx40 / Hcn4 + Alexa Fluor 647, Cntn2 + Alexa Fluor 568, CD31 (PECAM1) + Alexa Fluor 488, DAPI]

**Justification:**
iDISCO+ is selected because it is optimized for whole-organ immunolabeling of dense tissues such as the intact mouse heart (~10×8×8 mm), employing methanol-based dehydration and dichloromethane (DCM)/dibenzyl ether (DBE) clearing that achieves high transparency and excellent antibody penetration via organic solvent permeabilization. The organic solvent backbone also preserves Alexa Fluor dye signals robustly. For Purkinje fiber identity, a dual-marker strategy using **Cx40** (gap junction protein highly enriched in the His-Purkinje conduction system) and **Cntn2** (contactin-2/TAG-1, a surface marker of the ventricular conduction system including Purkinje fibers) provides specific, orthogonal confirmation of conduction system identity and spatial trajectory. **CD31 (PECAM-1)** labels coronary vasculature as a three-dimensional anatomical reference frame to co-register Purkinje network position relative to subendocardial zones, interventricular septum, papillary muscles, and apex. **DAPI** (applied as a post-clearing nuclear counterstain compatible with iDISCO+ via a brief rehydration step before RI matching, or alternatively incorporated during the pre-clearing aqueous phase) provides myocardial cytoarchitecture reference. This multi-channel strategy ensures Purkinje fiber identity is established by specific conduction-system markers (Cx40, Cntn2) rather than generic structural labels, while CD31 and DAPI supply the anatomical coordinate system required for spatial mapping.

---

**Protocol Steps:**

**1 Sample Preparation and Pre-treatment**

1.1 Retrieve PFA-fixed, post-fixed intact mouse heart. Wash in 1× PBS to remove residual fixative. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 × 10 min)

1.2 Trim excess connective tissue and great vessel stumps to ≤2 mm above the atrioventricular groove to standardize sample geometry. Keep sample in 1× PBS on ice until next step. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: ≤30 min)

**2 Dehydration (Methanol Series)**

2.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in H₂O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

2.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in H₂O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

2.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in H₂O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

2.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in H₂O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

2.5 Incubation with 100% methanol (anhydrous). (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

2.6 Incubation with 100% methanol (anhydrous), second change. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

**3 Bleaching (H₂O₂ in Methanol)**

3.1 Incubation with chilled fresh 5% H₂O₂ in 100% methanol (1 volume 30% H₂O₂ : 5 volumes MeOH) to quench endogenous peroxidase and reduce autofluorescence from cardiac myoglobin and lipofuscin. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 16 hours, overnight)

**4 Rehydration**

4.1 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in H₂O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

4.2 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in H₂O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

4.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in H₂O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

4.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in H₂O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

4.5 Incubation with 1× PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

4.6 Incubation with 1× PBS, second change. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

**5 Permeabilization and Blocking**

5.1 Incubation with Permeabilization Solution [0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100, 20% (vol/vol) DMSO, 0.3 M glycine in 1× PBS]. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)

5.2 Incubation with Blocking Solution [0.2% (vol/vol) Tween-20, 10% (vol/vol) DMSO, 6% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum (NDS) in 1× PBS]. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 48 hours)

**6 Primary Antibody Incubation**

6.1 Prepare Primary Antibody Mix in PTwH+DMSO+NDS buffer [0.2% (vol/vol) Tween-20, 10 µg/mL heparin, 5% (vol/vol) DMSO, 3% (vol/vol) NDS in 1× PBS]:
- Anti-Cx40 (rabbit polyclonal, e.g., Abcam ab11370 or equivalent): 1:200 dilution
- Anti-Cntn2/TAG-1 (goat polyclonal, e.g., R&D Systems AF4439 or equivalent): 1:200 dilution
- Anti-CD31/PECAM-1 (rat monoclonal, e.g., BD Biosciences 550274 or equivalent): 1:300 dilution
Incubation with Primary Antibody Mix with gentle rocking. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days)

6.2 Wash with PTwH buffer [0.2% (vol/vol) Tween-20, 10 µg/mL heparin in 1× PBS], 5 changes. (Temperature: RT, Time: 5 × 1 hour, then overnight in final wash at RT)

**7 Secondary Antibody Incubation**

7.1 Prepare Secondary Antibody Mix in PTwH+DMSO+NDS buffer:
- Donkey anti-rabbit IgG conjugated to Alexa Fluor 647 (targeting Cx40): 1:400 dilution
- Donkey anti-goat IgG conjugated to Alexa Fluor 568 (targeting Cntn2): 1:400 dilution
- Donkey anti-rat IgG conjugated to Alexa Fluor 488 (targeting CD31): 1:400 dilution
Incubation with Secondary Antibody Mix with gentle rocking, protected from light. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 5 days)

7.2 Wash with PTwH buffer, 5 changes, protected from light. (Temperature: RT, Time: 5 × 1 hour, then overnight in final wash at RT)

**8 Nuclear Counterstain (DAPI)**

8.1 Incubation with DAPI solution [2 µg/mL DAPI in PTwH buffer], protected from light. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)

8.2 Wash with PTwH buffer, 3 changes, protected from light. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 × 30 min)

8.3 Wash with 1× PBS, 2 changes, to remove Tween-20 before dehydration. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 × 30 min)

**9 Second Dehydration (Methanol Series)**

9.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in H₂O, protected from light. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

9.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in H₂O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

9.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in H₂O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

9.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in H₂O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

9.5 Incubation with 100% methanol (anhydrous). (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

9.6 Incubation with 100% methanol (anhydrous), second change. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

**10 Delipidation with Dichloromethane (DCM)**

10.1 Incubation with 33% (vol/vol) DCM / 67% (vol/vol) methanol (1:2 DCM:MeOH) to initiate lipid extraction. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours)

10.2 Incubation with 100% DCM (Sigma-Aldrich 270997), two changes, to complete delipidation. Tissue should sink to bottom of vial when fully delipidated. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 × 30 min)

**11 Refractive Index Matching with Dibenzyl Ether (DBE)**

11.1 Transfer sample directly from DCM into 100% DBE (dibenzyl ether, Sigma-Aldrich 108014, RI ≈ 1.559) without intermediate steps. Incubation with 100% DBE, first change, without shaking, protected from light. (Temperature: RT, Time: 4 hours)

11.2 Incubation with fresh 100% DBE, second change, without shaking, protected from light. Tissue should appear fully transparent. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours, overnight)

**12 Sample Mounting and Storage Prior to Imaging**

12.1 Transfer cleared heart into a custom glass-bottom imaging chamber or a 5 mL glass vial filled with 100% DBE. Orient the heart with the apex pointing downward and the left ventricular free wall facing the objective to maximize subendocardial access. Seal with optical-grade glass coverslip using silicone sealant. (Temperature: RT, Time: allow 30 min for settling before imaging)

12.2 Store mounted sample in 100% DBE in sealed glass container, wrapped in aluminum foil to protect fluorophores, until light-sheet fluorescence microscopy (LSFM) or confocal imaging session. (Temperature: RT, Time: stable for up to 4 weeks; image within 1–2 weeks for optimal DAPI signal)

**Chosen Method:** iDISCO+
**Chosen Labeling:** [Alexa Fluor (anti-Cntn2 + Alexa Fluor 647), Alexa Fluor (anti-Cx40/Hcn4 + Alexa Fluor 568), DAPI]

**Justification:**
iDISCO+ is selected over CUBIC for the following reasons specific to this problem:
1. **Dense myocardial tissue & complete delipidation:** iDISCO+ uses methanol-based dehydration followed by DCM/DBE solvent clearing, which achieves far superior lipid extraction from compact, lipid-rich cardiac muscle compared to the aqueous CUBIC reagents. The previous CUBIC failure (incomplete clearing at RT/24 h) is directly addressed by the organic solvent backbone of iDISCO+.
2. **Heme removal:** The 5% H₂O₂/methanol bleaching step in iDISCO+ effectively eliminates hemoglobin-derived autofluorescence and heme pigment that would otherwise mask Purkinje fiber signals in the red/far-red channels—a critical advantage for the blood-rich heart.
3. **Antibody penetration into whole heart (~10 mm):** iDISCO+ employs methanol-based pre-treatment that permeabilizes membranes throughout the tissue, enabling deep antibody penetration with extended incubation at 37 °C, which is essential for reaching subendocardial Purkinje fibers in the interventricular septum and ventricular walls.
4. **Red/far-red channel compatibility:** DBE (refractive index ~1.562) provides excellent RI matching for light-sheet microscopy; Alexa Fluor 568 and Alexa Fluor 647 are both photostable in organic-solvent-cleared tissue and occupy spectrally distinct channels (red and far-red), minimizing cross-talk for dual-signal detection of Cntn2 (contactin-2, a Purkinje fiber marker) and Cx40/Hcn4 (gap junction/conduction system marker).
5. **3D network reconstruction:** The high transparency achieved by DBE and the long working distance afforded by RI = 1.56 matching are well-suited for light-sheet imaging and subsequent 3D tracing of the continuous Purkinje fiber network.
6. **Markers chosen:** Cntn2 (contactin-2) labels Purkinje fiber axons and their contacts; Cx40 (Connexin 40, listed as Cx40/Hcn4) labels gap junctions of the conduction system cells. Together they fulfill the dual-signal requirement. DAPI provides nuclear counterstain for anatomical reference (compatible with iDISCO+ when applied in aqueous immunostaining phase before dehydration, or omitted if nuclear signal is not needed in final DBE-cleared sample—here included in the aqueous staining phase).

---

## Protocol Steps

### 1 Pre-treatment & Dehydration

1.1 Wash fixed whole mouse heart (10 × 8 × 8 mm, post-fixed in 4% PFA/PBS) with 1× PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 × 30 min)

1.2 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in distilled water (dH₂O) with gentle shaking. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

1.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in dH₂O with gentle shaking. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

1.4 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in dH₂O with gentle shaking. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

1.5 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in dH₂O with gentle shaking. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

1.6 Incubation with 100% methanol (anhydrous) with gentle shaking. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

1.7 Repeat 100% methanol wash. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

---

### 2 Bleaching (Heme & Autofluorescence Removal)

2.1 Prepare fresh bleaching solution: 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in 100% methanol (1 volume 30% H₂O₂ : 5 volumes MeOH). Pre-chill to 4 °C.

2.2 Incubation with chilled 5% H₂O₂/methanol bleaching solution in a sealed tube, protected from light. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 16 hours)

2.3 Wash with 100% methanol × 2. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 min each)

---

### 3 Rehydration

3.1 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in dH₂O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

3.2 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in dH₂O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

3.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in dH₂O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

3.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in dH₂O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

3.5 Incubation with 1× PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 × 30 min)

---

### 4 Permeabilization & Blocking

4.1 Incubation with Permeabilization Solution [0.2% (wt/vol) gelatin, 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100, 0.01% (wt/vol) sodium azide in 1× PBS (PTxwH)]. (Temperature: 37 °C, Time: 2 × 1 hour)

4.2 Incubation with Blocking Solution [0.2% (wt/vol) gelatin, 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100, 10% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum, 0.01% (wt/vol) sodium azide in 1× PBS]. (Temperature: 37 °C, Time: 24 hours)

---

### 5 Primary Antibody Immunolabeling

5.1 Prepare primary antibody cocktail in PTxwH + 10% normal donkey serum:
- Anti-Cntn2 (contactin-2) antibody: 1:200 dilution
- Anti-Cx40 (Connexin 40 / Cx40/Hcn4) antibody: 1:200 dilution
(Use antibodies raised in different host species to enable dual secondary labeling, e.g., rabbit anti-Cntn2 and goat anti-Cx40.)

5.2 Incubation with primary antibody cocktail solution, with gentle rocking in a sealed tube. (Temperature: 37 °C, Time: 7 days)

5.3 Wash with PTxwH solution. (Temperature: 37 °C, Time: 5 × 1 hour, then overnight)

---

### 6 Secondary Antibody Immunolabeling & Nuclear Counterstain

6.1 Prepare secondary antibody cocktail in PTxwH + 10% normal donkey serum:
- Donkey anti-rabbit Alexa Fluor 647 (for Cntn2): 1:500 dilution
- Donkey anti-goat Alexa Fluor 568 (for Cx40): 1:500 dilution
- DAPI: 1 µg/mL

6.2 Incubation with secondary antibody + DAPI cocktail solution, protected from light, with gentle rocking. (Temperature: 37 °C, Time: 5 days)

6.3 Wash with PTxwH solution, protected from light. (Temperature: 37 °C, Time: 5 × 1 hour, then overnight)

6.4 Post-fix with 4% (wt/vol) PFA in 1× PBS to stabilize antibody-antigen complexes. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

6.5 Wash with 1× PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 × 30 min)

---

### 7 Dehydration (Pre-clearing)

7.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in dH₂O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

7.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in dH₂O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

7.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in dH₂O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

7.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in dH₂O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

7.5 Incubation with 100% methanol (anhydrous). (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

7.6 Repeat 100% methanol wash. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

---

### 8 Delipidation with DCM

8.1 Incubation with 33% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) in 100% methanol. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours)

8.2 Incubation with 100% DCM (two changes) to complete lipid extraction. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 × 30 min)

> ⚠ Perform all DCM steps in a chemical fume hood; use glass vials only.

---

### 9 Refractive Index Matching (Clearing in DBE)

9.1 Transfer sample from 100% DCM directly into 100% dibenzyl ether (DBE, Sigma-Aldrich 108014; RI ≈ 1.562) in a glass vial, protected from light, without shaking. (Temperature: RT, Time: 4 hours)

9.2 Replace with fresh 100% DBE and continue incubation until the heart is fully transparent (visually confirmed). (Temperature: RT, Time: 12–24 hours)

> Note: Complete transparency of the 10 mm heart typically requires 16–24 h total in DBE. The sample is stable in DBE at RT for weeks when sealed and protected from light.

---

### 10 Sample Mounting & Imaging Preparation

10.1 Transfer cleared heart into a glass-bottom imaging chamber or custom 3D-printed holder filled with 100% DBE (RI ≈ 1.562).

10.2 Orient the heart with the apex downward or in the desired imaging axis; immobilize with low-melting agarose dissolved in DBE (1% wt/vol) if needed, or use inert silicone putty to stabilize without touching the cleared tissue.

10.3 Fill the imaging chamber completely with fresh DBE to eliminate air bubbles; seal with a glass coverslip using silicone sealant compatible with organic solvents.

10.4 Allow the mounted sample to equilibrate and confirm full RI matching before imaging. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 min)

10.5 Image using a light-sheet fluorescence microscope (LSFM) equipped with a DBE-compatible objective (e.g., CLARITY/LSFM objective, NA 0.3–0.5, WD ≥ 10 mm) or a long-working-distance confocal objective immersed in DBE:
- Channel 1: DAPI (405 nm excitation / 420–470 nm emission) — nuclear reference
- Channel 2: Alexa Fluor 568 (561 nm excitation / 580–620 nm emission) — Cx40 conduction system cells
- Channel 3: Alexa Fluor 647 (638 nm excitation / 660–720 nm emission) — Cntn2 Purkinje fiber contacts

10.6 Acquire z-stacks with ≤ 2 µm z-step size throughout the full ventricular volume for complete 3D Purkinje network reconstruction. Export raw image stacks (TIFF or CZI) for downstream 3D rendering and network tracing (e.g., Imaris, Fiji/Simple Neurite Tracer, or Vaa3D).

**Chosen Method:** iDISCO+
**Chosen Labeling:** [Lectin + Alexa Fluor 647, Nephrin (NPHS1) + Alexa Fluor 568, DAPI]

**Justification:**
iDISCO+ is selected because it provides excellent whole-organ clearing for a tissue the size of a mouse kidney (~10 mm × 6 mm × 5 mm), achieves high transparency through organic solvent-based delipidation (methanol/DCM/DBE), and is highly compatible with immunolabeling of deep epitopes. The methanol dehydration step also permeabilizes the tissue thoroughly, enabling antibody penetration into the dense glomerular tuft. For the scientific goals:
- **Lectin (e.g., tomato lectin or IB4) conjugated to Alexa Fluor 647** labels the glomerular capillary endothelium and mesangial vasculature, delineating the capillary loops within each glomerular tuft — ideal for volumetric segmentation and counting.
- **Anti-Nephrin (NPHS1) + Alexa Fluor 568** labels podocytes at the filtration barrier, confirming glomerular identity, enabling morphological assessment of the slit diaphragm integrity in nephritis, and distinguishing glomeruli from other rounded structures.
- **DAPI** (applied pre-dehydration as a nuclear counterstain) provides cytoarchitectural context for cortex/medullary ray boundary identification and regional distribution mapping.
Together these three channels allow: (1) unambiguous identification and counting of all glomeruli across the whole kidney, (2) volumetric measurement of each glomerular tuft, (3) assessment of podocyte/filtration barrier changes in nephritis, and (4) 3D spatial mapping relative to cortex and medullary rays.

---

## Protocol Steps

### 0 Pre-clearing Preparation (Nuclear Staining with DAPI)
0.1 Wash fixed kidney in 1× PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 × 10 min)
0.2 Incubate in DAPI solution (5 µg/mL in 1× PBS with 0.1% Triton X-100) to label nuclei before dehydration. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)

model_response:
**Chosen Method:** iDISCO+
**Chosen Labeling:** [Nephrin (NPHS1) + Alexa Fluor 647, Podocin (NPHS2) + Alexa Fluor 546, DAPI]

**Justification:** iDISCO+ is selected because: (1) it achieves deep, uniform clearing of dense solid organs such as intact mouse kidney (~10×6×5 mm) via organic solvent-based delipidation, enabling whole-organ light-sheet imaging; (2) its methanol dehydration + dibenzyl ether (DBE) RI-matching pipeline is well-validated for immunolabeling of transmembrane proteins in kidney; (3) the detergent-free organic solvent environment preserves antigenicity of tight-junction/slit-diaphragm proteins when combined with the methanol-compatible fixation already performed; (4) whole-mount immunostaining with primary antibodies against Nephrin (NPHS1) and Podocin (NPHS2) — the two canonical slit-diaphragm transmembrane proteins — directly addresses the requirement to simultaneously visualize two key slit-diaphragm components across the entire kidney, enabling quantitative comparison of signal continuity, intensity, focal loss, and glomerular volume changes in nephritis. DAPI provides nuclear reference for glomerular segmentation. Lectin or CD31 are explicitly excluded as primary slit-diaphragm markers per the problem constraints.

---

**Protocol Steps:**

**1 Pre-clearing Washes (Post-fixation)**
1.1 Wash fixed intact kidney in 1× PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour × 3 washes)
1.2 Incubation in 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS (PTx0.2) to begin permeabilization. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour × 2 washes)

**2 Methanol Dehydration**
2.1 Incubation in 20% (vol/vol) methanol in H₂O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
2.2 Incubation in 40% (vol/vol) methanol in H₂O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
2.3 Incubation in 60% (vol/vol) methanol in H₂O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
2.4 Incubation in 80% (vol/vol) methanol in H₂O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
2.5 Incubation in 100% methanol. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
2.6 Incubation in 100% methanol (second change). (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

**3 Bleaching (H₂O₂ Treatment)**
3.1 Incubation in chilled fresh 5% H₂O₂ in methanol (1 volume 30% H₂O₂ : 5 volumes 100% MeOH). (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)

**4 Methanol Rehydration**
4.1 Incubation in 80% (vol/vol) methanol in H₂O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
4.2 Incubation in 60% (vol/vol) methanol in H₂O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
4.3 Incubation in 40% (vol/vol) methanol in H₂O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
4.4 Incubation in 20% (vol/vol) methanol in H₂O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
4.5 Incubation in 1× PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

**5 Permeabilization**
5.1 Incubation in permeabilization solution: 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100, 20% (vol/vol) DMSO, 0.3 M glycine in PBS (PTxs-DMSO/glycine). (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)

**6 Blocking**
6.1 Incubation in blocking solution: 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100, 10% (vol/vol) DMSO, 6% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum (NDS) in PBS. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)

**7 Primary Antibody Immunolabeling**
7.1 Incubation with primary antibody cocktail in PTwH (0.2% Tween-20 + 10 µg/mL heparin in PBS) + 5% DMSO + 3% NDS:
- Anti-Nephrin (NPHS1) rabbit polyclonal antibody, 1:200 dilution
- Anti-Podocin (NPHS2) guinea pig polyclonal antibody, 1:200 dilution
(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days, with gentle rocking)

**8 Post-Primary Antibody Washes**
8.1 Wash in PTwH (0.2% Tween-20 + 10 µg/mL heparin in PBS). (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
8.2 Wash in PTwH. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
8.3 Wash in PTwH. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
8.4 Wash in PTwH. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
8.5 Wash in PTwH. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
8.6 Overnight wash in PTwH. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)

**9 Secondary Antibody Immunolabeling + Nuclear Staining**
9.1 Incubation with secondary antibody cocktail in PTwH + 3% NDS:
- Donkey anti-rabbit IgG conjugated to Alexa Fluor 647, 1:400 dilution (for Nephrin/NPHS1 detection)
- Donkey anti-guinea pig IgG conjugated to Alexa Fluor 546, 1:400 dilution (for Podocin/NPHS2 detection)
- DAPI, 1 µg/mL final concentration (nuclear counterstain for glomerular segmentation)
(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 5 days, with gentle rocking, protected from light)

**10 Post-Secondary Antibody Washes**
10.1 Wash in PTwH. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour, protected from light)
10.2 Wash in PTwH. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour, protected from light)
10.3 Wash in PTwH. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour, protected from light)
10.4 Wash in PTwH. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour, protected from light)
10.5 Wash in PTwH. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour, protected from light)
10.6 Overnight wash in PTwH. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours, protected from light)

**11 Methanol Dehydration (Second Round, Pre-clearing)**
11.1 Incubation in 20% (vol/vol) methanol in H₂O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour, protected from light)
11.2 Incubation in 40% (vol/vol) methanol in H₂O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour, protected from light)
11.3 Incubation in 60% (vol/vol) methanol in H₂O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour, protected from light)
11.4 Incubation in 80% (vol/vol) methanol in H₂O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour, protected from light)
11.5 Incubation in 100% methanol. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour, protected from light)
11.6 Incubation in 100% methanol (second change). (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour, protected from light)

**12 Delipidation with DCM**
12.1 Incubation in 33% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) / 66% methanol. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours, protected from light)
12.2 Incubation in 100% DCM (two changes) to wash out methanol. (Temperature: RT, Time: 15 minutes × 2, protected from light)

**13 Refractive Index Matching with DBE**
13.1 Incubation in 100% dibenzyl ether (DBE, Sigma-Aldrich 108014) without shaking, until tissue is fully transparent and sinks to the bottom of the vial. (Temperature: RT, Time: 4–6 hours minimum; overnight recommended for complete RI matching, protected from light)

**14 Storage / Pre-imaging Preparation**
14.1 Store cleared kidney in 100% DBE in a sealed glass vial. (Temperature: RT, protected from light; stable for weeks to months)
14.2 Prior to light-sheet imaging, mount the cleared kidney in a glass capillary or imaging chamber filled with 100% DBE (RI ≈ 1.56), ensuring the kidney is fully submerged and oriented with the renal cortex accessible to the light sheet objective.
14.3 Acquire 3D image stacks using a light-sheet fluorescence microscope equipped with objectives compatible with DBE immersion (e.g., CLARITY/organic solvent-compatible objectives); use 405 nm (DAPI), 561 nm (Alexa Fluor 546 / Podocin-NPHS2), and 647 nm (Alexa Fluor 647 / Nephrin-NPHS1) laser lines. Tile the entire kidney volume with ≥10% overlap between tiles for seamless 3D reconstruction and whole-kidney glomerular analysis.

model_response:
**Chosen Method:** iDISCO+
**Chosen Labeling:** [Lectin+Alexa Fluor 647, Nephrin (NPHS1)+Alexa Fluor 568, Podocin (NPHS2)+Alexa Fluor 488, DAPI]

**Justification:** iDISCO+ is selected for the following reasons: (1) It achieves excellent clearing of dense, lipid-rich solid organs such as intact mouse kidney (~10×6×5 mm), enabling whole-organ 3D imaging compatible with light-sheet fluorescence microscopy (LSFM). (2) The methanol-based delipidation step efficiently removes lipids from the kidney's dense cortical and medullary parenchyma, yielding high transparency. (3) iDISCO+ is well-validated for immunolabeling of large intact tissues using organic solvent-compatible antibodies, and the permeabilization/blocking steps are optimized for deep antibody penetration. (4) DBE (dibenzyl ether) as the final RI-matching medium (RI ≈ 1.56) is compatible with long-term sample storage and LSFM objectives. For labeling: **Lectin (e.g., tomato lectin, Lycopersicon esculentum) conjugated to Alexa Fluor 647** is used as a vascular lumen marker via transcardial perfusion prior to fixation, labeling glomerular capillary endothelial surfaces directly and providing a high-quality capillary tuft channel. **Nephrin (NPHS1) + Alexa Fluor 568** marks the slit diaphragm-associated transmembrane protein at the podocyte foot process junction, directly reporting slit diaphragm structural integrity. **Podocin (NPHS2) + Alexa Fluor 488** marks the podocyte slit diaphragm scaffold protein, complementing Nephrin to delineate podocyte coverage and foot process distribution. **DAPI** provides nuclear counterstaining for glomerular cell identification and overall tissue architecture reference. This three-channel strategy (capillary lumen / slit diaphragm identity / podocyte scaffold + nuclei) enables quantitative 3D analysis of glomerular volume, capillary tuft morphology, podocyte signal coverage, and spatial heterogeneity of lesions across the whole kidney in a nephritis model.

---

**Protocol Steps:**

**0 Pre-clearing: Transcardial Lectin Perfusion & Fixation**

0.1 Prepare Lectin-Alexa Fluor 647 perfusion solution: dissolve Lycopersicon esculentum lectin conjugated to Alexa Fluor 647 at 0.1 mg/mL in sterile PBS (pH 7.4). (Temperature: RT, Time: prepare fresh)

0.2 Anesthetize mouse deeply; perform transcardial perfusion with 20 mL ice-cold PBS (pH 7.4) to flush blood, then immediately perfuse with 5 mL Lectin-Alexa Fluor 647 solution at ~1 mL/min to label vascular lumens including glomerular capillaries. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: ~5 min perfusion)

0.3 Follow immediately with transcardial perfusion of 20 mL ice-cold 4% paraformaldehyde (PFA) in PBS (pH 7.4) to fix the lectin in place and fix the tissue. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: ~10 min perfusion)

0.4 Dissect kidneys; post-fix by immersion in 4% PFA in PBS (pH 7.4). (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 24 hours)

0.5 Wash kidneys in PBS (pH 7.4) with gentle agitation. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 × 1 hour)

---

**1 Dehydration**

1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in distilled water (dH₂O) with gentle agitation on a rocking platform. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in dH₂O with gentle agitation. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in dH₂O with gentle agitation. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in dH₂O with gentle agitation. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

1.5 Incubation with 100% methanol (anhydrous) with gentle agitation. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

1.6 Repeat incubation with fresh 100% methanol (anhydrous) with gentle agitation. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

---

**2 Bleaching (Endogenous Peroxidase Quenching & Autofluorescence Reduction)**

2.1 Prepare chilled bleaching solution: 5% H₂O₂ in 100% methanol (1 volume 30% H₂O₂ : 5 volumes 100% MeOH, freshly prepared). Incubate kidneys fully submerged with gentle agitation. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)

---

**3 Rehydration**

3.1 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in dH₂O with gentle agitation. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

3.2 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in dH₂O with gentle agitation. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

3.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in dH₂O with gentle agitation. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

3.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in dH₂O with gentle agitation. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

3.5 Incubation with PBS (pH 7.4) with gentle agitation. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

3.6 Repeat incubation with fresh PBS (pH 7.4) with gentle agitation. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

---

**4 Permeabilization & Blocking**

4.1 Incubation with Permeabilization/Blocking solution: PBS containing 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100, 0.3 M glycine, 20% (vol/vol) DMSO, and 0.05% (wt/vol) sodium azide, with gentle agitation. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)

4.2 Incubation with Blocking solution: PBS containing 0.2% (vol/vol) Tween-20, 10% (vol/vol) DMSO, 6% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum (NDS), and 0.05% (wt/vol) sodium azide (PTwH/DMSO/NDS blocking buffer), with gentle agitation. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)

---

**5 Primary Antibody Immunolabeling**

5.1 Prepare primary antibody cocktail in PTwH/DMSO/NDS blocking buffer (PTwH: PBS + 0.2% Tween-20 + 10 µg/mL heparin; supplemented with 5% NDS and 3% DMSO):
- Anti-Nephrin (NPHS1) rabbit polyclonal antibody: 1:200 dilution
- Anti-Podocin (NPHS2) guinea pig polyclonal antibody: 1:200 dilution
(Note: Lectin-AF647 channel was established by perfusion in Step 0; no additional lectin antibody required.)
Incubate kidneys fully submerged with gentle agitation. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days)

5.2 Wash kidneys in PTwH (PBS + 0.2% Tween-20 + 10 µg/mL heparin) with gentle agitation, replacing wash solution every 2–3 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 5 × 2 hours, then overnight = ~24 hours total washing)

---

**6 Secondary Antibody Immunolabeling**

6.1 Prepare secondary antibody cocktail in PTwH/DMSO/NDS blocking buffer:
- Donkey anti-rabbit IgG conjugated to Alexa Fluor 568: 1:400 dilution (for Nephrin/NPHS1 detection)
- Donkey anti-guinea pig IgG conjugated to Alexa Fluor 488: 1:400 dilution (for Podocin/NPHS2 detection)
Incubate kidneys fully submerged with gentle agitation, protected from light. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 5 days)

6.2 Wash kidneys in PTwH with gentle agitation, replacing wash solution every 2–3 hours, protected from light. (Temperature: RT, Time: 5 × 2 hours, then overnight = ~24 hours total washing)

---

**7 Nuclear Counterstaining with DAPI**

7.1 Incubation with DAPI solution at 5 µg/mL in PTwH, protected from light, with gentle agitation. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)

7.2 Wash kidneys in PTwH to remove excess DAPI, protected from light. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 × 2 hours)

---

**8 Dehydration (Pre-clearing)**

8.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in dH₂O with gentle agitation, protected from light. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

8.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in dH₂O with gentle agitation, protected from light. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

8.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in dH₂O with gentle agitation, protected from light. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

8.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in dH₂O with gentle agitation, protected from light. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

8.5 Incubation with 100% methanol (anhydrous) with gentle agitation, protected from light. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

8.6 Repeat incubation with fresh 100% methanol (anhydrous) with gentle agitation, protected from light. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

---

**9 Delipidation**

9.1 Incubation with 33% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) in 100% methanol (1 volume DCM : 2 volumes MeOH) with gentle agitation, protected from light. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours)

9.2 Incubation with 100% DCM (anhydrous) to complete delipidation, with gentle agitation, protected from light. Tissue should sink to the bottom of the vial when clearing is complete. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 × 15 minutes)

---

**10 Refractive Index Matching**

10.1 Remove DCM completely by aspiration. Immediately transfer kidneys to 100% dibenzyl ether (DBE, Sigma-Aldrich 108014) without any aqueous wash. Incubate with gentle agitation, protected from light, until tissue is fully transparent (RI ≈ 1.56). (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours minimum; can be extended to overnight for complete transparency of whole kidney)

10.2 Replace with fresh 100% DBE and incubate without shaking for long-term storage and final RI equilibration, protected from light. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12–24 hours)

---

**11 Sample Mounting & Imaging Preparation**

11.1 Transfer cleared kidney in DBE to an appropriate imaging chamber (e.g., custom 3D-printed holder or glass-bottom dish sealed with silicone grease). Fill chamber completely with 100% DBE to eliminate air bubbles. Seal chamber to prevent DBE evaporation. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes equilibration before imaging)

11.2 Image using a light-sheet fluorescence microscope (LSFM) equipped with a long-working-distance, low-NA objective (e.g., 4× or 12× CLARITY/DBE-compatible objective) and appropriate laser lines:
- 405 nm laser → DAPI channel (nuclear counterstain, glomerular cell identification)
- 488 nm laser → Alexa Fluor 488 channel (Podocin/NPHS2, podocyte slit diaphragm scaffold)
- 561 nm laser → Alexa Fluor 568 channel (Nephrin/NPHS1, slit diaphragm identity)
- 638/647 nm laser → Alexa Fluor 647 channel (Lectin, glomerular capillary lumen)
Acquire whole-kidney tile scans with ≥10% overlap; Z-step: 2–5 µm for glomerular-resolution analysis. (Temperature: RT, Time: variable, typically 4–12 hours per whole kidney depending on resolution)

11.3 For long-term storage between imaging sessions, keep samples submerged in 100% DBE in sealed vials, protected from light. (Temperature: RT or 4 ℃, Time: up to several months)

**Chosen Method:** CUBIC

**Chosen Labeling:** [Nephrin (NPHS1) + Alexa Fluor (488), Podocin (NPHS2) + Alexa Fluor (647), DAPI]

**Justification:**
CUBIC（特别是优化后的CUBIC-R+/CUBIC-L延长处理方案）是针对完整小鼠肾脏等致密实质器官的首选水性透明方法。相比原始问题中仅室温24小时单次CUBIC-L处理，本方案采用37°C延长多轮CUBIC-L脱脂处理，可有效解决皮质/髓质透明不均一问题（肾髓质富含脂质和胶原，需更充分处理）。CUBIC全程水性环境对抗体表位保护优于有机溶剂法（如iDISCO+），适合Nephrin和Podocin两种足细胞裂孔隔膜跨膜蛋白的免疫荧光标记。CUBIC-R+（RI≈1.52）提供与光片显微镜匹配的折射率，适合全肾深层三维成像。标记策略：Nephrin（NPHS1）标记裂孔隔膜结构蛋白1（绿色通道），Podocin（NPHS2）标记裂孔隔膜结构蛋白2（远红通道），DAPI标记细胞核用于肾小球边界识别与体积定量，三通道组合可实现全肾肾小球计数、体积测量及滤过屏障双蛋白损伤评估。

---

**Protocol Steps:**

**1 样品预处理与渗透性增强**

1.1 将已完成4% PFA固定及后固定的完整小鼠肾脏（约10 mm × 6 mm × 5 mm）用PBS（0.01 M, pH 7.4）充分漂洗，每次10 mL。(Temperature: RT, Time: 3 × 20 min)

1.2 将肾脏转入含0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100的PBS溶液（10 mL）中振荡孵育，以增强后续试剂渗透性。(Temperature: 37 °C, Time: 12 hours)

1.3 用PBS漂洗样品。(Temperature: RT, Time: 3 × 20 min)

---

**2 脱脂透明处理（CUBIC-L 延长多轮处理）**

2.1 配制CUBIC-L工作液：10% (wt/vol) N-丁基二乙醇胺（N-butyldiethanolamine）+ 10% (wt/vol) Triton X-100，溶于超纯水，充分混匀至澄清。

2.2 第一轮CUBIC-L处理：将肾脏置于15 mL CUBIC-L工作液中，轻柔振荡孵育。(Temperature: 37 °C, Time: 48 hours)

2.3 更换新鲜CUBIC-L工作液（15 mL），进行第二轮处理，轻柔振荡孵育，直至样品呈半透明状（皮质与髓质透明度趋于一致）。(Temperature: 37 °C, Time: 48 hours)

2.4 若髓质区域仍不透明，更换新鲜CUBIC-L工作液（15 mL），进行第三轮处理。(Temperature: 37 °C, Time: 24–48 hours)

2.5 用PBS充分漂洗，去除残余CUBIC-L。(Temperature: RT, Time: 3 × 30 min)

---

**3 免疫荧光标记前封闭与渗透处理**

3.1 配制封闭液：5% (vol/vol) 正常驴血清（Normal Donkey Serum, NDS）+ 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 + 0.1% (wt/vol) 叠氮化钠（NaN₃）溶于PBS。

3.2 将透明化肾脏置于封闭液（10 mL）中孵育，以减少非特异性结合并进一步增强抗体渗透。(Temperature: 37 °C, Time: 24 hours)

---

**4 一抗孵育（Nephrin + Podocin 双标记）**

4.1 配制一抗工作液：抗Nephrin（NPHS1）兔多克隆抗体（1:200稀释）+ 抗Podocin（NPHS2）豚鼠多克隆抗体（1:200稀释），溶于含2% NDS + 0.5% Triton X-100 + 0.1% NaN₃的PBS中，终体积5 mL。

4.2 将肾脏置于一抗工作液中，轻柔振荡孵育。(Temperature: 37 °C, Time: 72 hours)

4.3 用含0.5% Triton X-100的PBS（PTwH：PBS + 0.2% Tween-20 + 0.1% Heparin，或直接用0.5% Triton X-100/PBS）充分漂洗，去除未结合一抗。(Temperature: RT, Time: 5 × 1 hour)

---

**5 二抗孵育（Alexa Fluor 荧光标记）**

5.1 配制二抗工作液：驴抗兔 Alexa Fluor 488（1:400稀释，针对Nephrin）+ 驴抗豚鼠 Alexa Fluor 647（1:400稀释，针对Podocin）+ DAPI（2 µg/mL，用于细胞核标记），溶于含2% NDS + 0.5% Triton X-100的PBS中，终体积5 mL，避光操作。

5.2 将肾脏置于二抗工作液中，轻柔振荡孵育，全程避光。(Temperature: 37 °C, Time: 48 hours)

5.3 用含0.5% Triton X-100的PBS充分漂洗，去除未结合二抗，全程避光。(Temperature: RT, Time: 5 × 1 hour)

5.4 用PBS再次漂洗。(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 × 30 min)

---

**6 折射率匹配（CUBIC-R+ 处理）**

6.1 配制CUBIC-R+工作液：45% (wt/vol) 蔗糖（Sucrose）+ 30% (wt/vol) 烟酰胺（Nicotinamide）+ 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100，溶于超纯水，充分溶解混匀，最终RI ≈ 1.52，避光保存。

6.2 第一步梯度RI匹配：将标记后肾脏置于50% CUBIC-R+（用PBS 1:1稀释，RI ≈ 1.46）中孵育，避光轻柔振荡。(Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)

6.3 第二步完全RI匹配：将肾脏转入100% CUBIC-R+工作液（5 mL）中孵育，避光轻柔振荡，直至样品完全透明且沉入溶液底部。(Temperature: RT, Time: 24–48 hours)

---

**7 样品保存与成像前处理**

7.1 将完全透明化的肾脏转入新鲜100% CUBIC-R+溶液中，置于适配光片显微镜（Light-Sheet Fluorescence Microscopy, LSFM）或共聚焦显微镜的样品槽/折射率匹配腔室中，避光静置平衡。(Temperature: RT, Time: 2–4 hours)

7.2 成像前确认样品折射率与成像介质（CUBIC-R+, RI ≈ 1.52）匹配，选用RI ≈ 1.52兼容的物镜（如LSFM专用浸液物镜）。

7.3 成像通道设置：DAPI（405 nm激发，用于细胞核/肾小球边界识别与体积定量）、Alexa Fluor 488（488 nm激发，Nephrin/NPHS1信号）、Alexa Fluor 647（638 nm激发，Podocin/NPHS2信号）；采集全肾Z-stack图像，层间距建议0.5–1 µm（皮质区）至2 µm（髓质区）。

7.4 短期保存：样品可在100% CUBIC-R+溶液中4 °C避光保存，建议成像后2周内完成分析。(Temperature: 4 °C, Time: ≤ 2 weeks)

**Chosen Method:** iDISCO+
**Chosen Labeling:** [CK19 (导管) + Alexa Fluor 647, CD31 (PECAM1) + Alexa Fluor 568, DAPI]

**Justification:** iDISCO+ is selected because it provides excellent whole-organ clearing for large, lipid-rich, blood-rich tissues such as intact mouse liver (~20×15×10 mm), achieving high transparency through organic solvent-based delipidation (methanol/DCM/DBE). Its immunolabeling-first workflow supports deep antibody penetration via methanol permeabilization and detergent-based blocking, which is critical for labeling the complex intrahepatic biliary tree throughout the full liver volume. CK19 (Cytokeratin 19) is the gold-standard marker for cholangiocytes and bile duct epithelium in mouse liver, enabling continuous visualization of bile duct trunks, branches, terminal ductules, and reactive ductular proliferation (ductular reaction) around injury zones. CD31 serves as a vascular/portal reference marker to delineate portal tracts and distinguish periportal from centrilobular regions, facilitating spatial comparison of branching density across hepatic zones. Alexa Fluor 647 (far-red) is assigned to CK19 as the primary target to maximize signal-to-noise in deep tissue; Alexa Fluor 568 (orange-red) is assigned to CD31 as the secondary reference channel. DAPI provides nuclear counterstaining for cytoarchitectural context. DBE (dibenzyl ether) as the final RI-matching medium (RI ≈ 1.56) is compatible with light-sheet fluorescence microscopy (LSFM), which is the optimal imaging modality for whole-lobe 3D reconstruction and network connectivity analysis at this scale.

---

**Protocol Steps:**

**1 Sample Preparation and Pre-treatment**

1.1 Retrieve fixed intact mouse liver (post-fixed in 4% PFA/PBS, stored at 4 °C). Rinse with 1× PBS to remove residual fixative. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 3 × 10 min)

1.2 Trim excess connective tissue and gallbladder; keep all hepatic lobes intact. Place liver in a 15 mL conical tube or mesh basket for subsequent incubations. (Temperature: RT, Time: 10 min)

**2 Dehydration (Methanol Series)**

2.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in ddH₂O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

2.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in ddH₂O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

2.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in ddH₂O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

2.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in ddH₂O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

2.5 Incubation with 100% methanol (anhydrous). (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

2.6 Incubation with 100% methanol (anhydrous), second change. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

**3 Bleaching (Heme Removal)**

3.1 Incubation with chilled fresh 5% H₂O₂ in 100% methanol (1 volume 30% H₂O₂ : 5 volumes MeOH) to remove heme pigment from blood-rich liver tissue. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 16 hours, protected from light)

**4 Rehydration (Methanol Series, Reverse)**

4.1 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in ddH₂O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

4.2 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in ddH₂O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

4.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in ddH₂O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

4.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in ddH₂O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

4.5 Incubation with 1× PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

**5 Permeabilization and Blocking**

5.1 Incubation with Permeabilization Solution [0.2% (wt/vol) gelatin, 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100, 0.01% (wt/vol) sodium azide in 1× PBS (PTxwH)]. (Temperature: 37 °C, Time: 24 hours, gentle shaking)

5.2 Incubation with Blocking Solution [0.2% (wt/vol) gelatin, 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100, 0.2% (vol/vol) heparin sodium (10 mg/mL stock), 5% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum, 0.01% (wt/vol) sodium azide in 1× PBS]. (Temperature: 37 °C, Time: 24 hours, gentle shaking)

**6 Primary Antibody Labeling**

6.1 Incubation with primary antibody cocktail in Blocking Solution:
- Anti-CK19 (rabbit monoclonal, e.g., Abcam ab52625), 1:200 dilution — bile duct epithelium primary target
- Anti-CD31/PECAM1 (rat monoclonal, e.g., BD Biosciences 550274), 1:150 dilution — portal vascular reference
(Temperature: 37 °C, Time: 7 days, gentle shaking, protected from light)

6.2 Wash with PTxwH Washing Solution [0.2% (wt/vol) gelatin, 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100, 0.2% (vol/vol) heparin sodium, 0.01% (wt/vol) sodium azide in 1× PBS]. (Temperature: 37 °C, Time: 5 × 1 hour, then overnight wash, gentle shaking)

**7 Secondary Antibody Labeling**

7.1 Incubation with secondary antibody cocktail in Blocking Solution:
- Donkey anti-rabbit Alexa Fluor 647 (e.g., Thermo Fisher A31573), 1:400 dilution — labels CK19
- Donkey anti-rat Alexa Fluor 568 (e.g., Thermo Fisher A78946), 1:400 dilution — labels CD31
(Temperature: 37 °C, Time: 5 days, gentle shaking, protected from light)

7.2 Wash with PTxwH Washing Solution. (Temperature: 37 °C, Time: 5 × 1 hour, then overnight wash, gentle shaking, protected from light)

**8 Nuclear Counterstaining (DAPI)**

8.1 Incubation with DAPI (4′,6-diamidino-2-phenylindole) at 5 µg/mL in 1× PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours, gentle shaking, protected from light)

8.2 Wash with 1× PBS to remove excess DAPI. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 × 30 min, gentle shaking)

**9 Post-fixation (Antibody Crosslinking)**

9.1 Incubation with 4% (wt/vol) PFA in 1× PBS to crosslink bound antibodies and preserve signal during organic solvent clearing. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour, gentle shaking)

9.2 Wash with 1× PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 × 20 min)

**10 Dehydration (Second Methanol Series, for Clearing)**

10.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in ddH₂O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

10.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in ddH₂O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

10.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in ddH₂O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

10.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in ddH₂O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

10.5 Incubation with 100% methanol (anhydrous). (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

10.6 Incubation with 100% methanol (anhydrous), second change. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

**11 Delipidation (DCM Treatment)**

11.1 Incubation with 33% (vol/vol) DCM (dichloromethane) / 67% methanol (vol/vol) mixture to initiate lipid extraction. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours, gentle shaking in fume hood)

11.2 Incubation with 100% DCM (dichloromethane, Sigma 270997) for complete delipidation of the large, lipid-rich liver tissue. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 × 30 min, gentle shaking in fume hood)

**12 Refractive Index Matching (DBE)**

12.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DBE (dibenzyl ether, Sigma 108014-1KG, RI ≈ 1.56) without shaking, in a glass vial sealed with Parafilm. Tissue will become fully transparent. (Temperature: RT, Time: 4 hours, then check clarity; extend to overnight if needed, protected from light)

12.2 Replace with fresh 100% DBE and confirm complete optical transparency of all hepatic lobes before imaging. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours minimum)

**13 Sample Storage and Imaging Preparation**

13.1 Transfer cleared liver to a glass imaging chamber (e.g., custom 3D-printed holder or glass cuvette) filled with 100% DBE. Orient liver to expose the desired lobe face for light-sheet objective access. Seal chamber to prevent DBE evaporation. (Temperature: RT, protected from light)

13.2 Image using a light-sheet fluorescence microscope (LSFM) equipped with a long-working-distance, low-NA objective (e.g., 4× or 12× CLARITY objective) compatible with DBE immersion (RI ≈ 1.56). Acquire z-stacks across full liver volume using:
- Channel 1: 405 nm excitation / 450 nm emission — DAPI (nuclear reference)
- Channel 2: 561 nm excitation / 590 nm emission — Alexa Fluor 568 / CD31 (portal vascular reference)
- Channel 3: 638 nm excitation / 680 nm emission — Alexa Fluor 647 / CK19 (bile duct epithelium, primary target)
(Temperature: RT, Time: per imaging session requirements)

13.3 For long-term storage, keep cleared samples in sealed glass vials filled with 100% DBE at RT, protected from light. Samples are stable for several months under these conditions. (Temperature: RT, protected from light)

**Chosen Method:** iDISCO+
**Chosen Labeling:** [CK19, CK7, CD31 + Alexa Fluor (647/568/488), DAPI]

**Justification:**
iDISCO+ is selected because: (1) it achieves deep, homogeneous clearing of large, lipid-rich, blood-rich organs such as intact mouse liver (~20×15×10 mm) via methanol-based delipidation combined with dibenzyl ether (DBE) RI matching; (2) its organic-solvent pipeline is fully compatible with whole-mount immunolabeling of intracellular cytoskeletal antigens (CK19, CK7) that require thorough permeabilization; (3) DBE (RI ≈ 1.56) provides excellent RI matching for light-sheet fluorescence microscopy (LSFM), the preferred modality for volumetric bile-duct network reconstruction. Labeling strategy: **CK19** (primary biliary epithelial marker, cholangiocyte-specific intermediate filament) and **CK7** (secondary biliary epithelial marker for cross-validation of bile-duct identity) are used as the two orthogonal cholangiocyte markers required by the scientific objective. **CD31** (PECAM-1) labels vascular endothelium to provide a negative-reference vascular channel, preventing misidentification of sinusoids/portal vessels as bile ducts. **DAPI** provides nuclear counterstain for tissue zoning and cytoarchitectural context. Alexa Fluor dyes (488, 568, 647) are chosen because they are bright, photostable, and well-separated spectrally for 3-channel simultaneous LSFM acquisition; they survive the iDISCO+ organic-solvent pipeline when conjugated to secondary antibodies added after rehydration.

---

## Protocol Steps

### 1 Pre-clearing Washes (Post-fixation Sample Entry)

1.1 Wash fixed intact liver in 1× PBS (phosphate-buffered saline, pH 7.4). (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 × 1 hour)

1.2 Wash in 1× PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 to begin surface permeabilization. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 × 1 hour)

---

### 2 Dehydration (Methanol Series)

2.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in H₂O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

2.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in H₂O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

2.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in H₂O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

2.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in H₂O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

2.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol (anhydrous). (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

2.6 Repeat 100% methanol incubation (second change). (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

---

### 3 Bleaching (Endogenous Pigment / Heme Removal)

3.1 Incubation with chilled fresh 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in 100% methanol (1 volume 30% H₂O₂ : 5 volumes MeOH) to quench heme and autofluorescence from blood-rich liver. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 16 hours, protected from light)

---

### 4 Rehydration

4.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

4.2 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in H₂O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

4.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in H₂O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

4.4 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in H₂O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

4.5 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in H₂O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

4.6 Incubation with 1× PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

---

### 5 Permeabilization

5.1 Incubation with Permeabilization Solution [1× PBS + 0.2% (wt/vol) gelatin + 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 + 0.01% (wt/vol) sodium azide + 0.02% (wt/vol) heparin sodium]. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours, gentle shaking)

---

### 6 Primary Antibody Immunolabeling

6.1 Prepare Primary Antibody Cocktail in Blocking/Labeling Solution [1× PBS + 0.2% (wt/vol) gelatin + 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 + 0.01% (wt/vol) sodium azide + 0.02% (wt/vol) heparin sodium]:
- Anti-CK19 (rabbit monoclonal, e.g., Abcam ab52625), 1:200 dilution → **Alexa Fluor 488 channel** (bile duct primary marker)
- Anti-CK7 (mouse monoclonal, e.g., Abcam ab9021), 1:200 dilution → **Alexa Fluor 568 channel** (bile duct cross-validation marker)
- Anti-CD31/PECAM-1 (goat polyclonal, e.g., R&D AF3628), 1:150 dilution → **Alexa Fluor 647 channel** (vascular reference / negative control for bile duct identity)

6.2 Incubation with primary antibody cocktail (sample fully submerged, gentle rolling agitation). (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days)

---

### 7 Post-Primary Antibody Washes

7.1 Wash with Labeling Solution [1× PBS + 0.2% (wt/vol) gelatin + 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 + 0.01% (wt/vol) sodium azide + 0.02% (wt/vol) heparin sodium]. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 8 × 1 hour, then overnight)

---

### 8 Secondary Antibody Immunolabeling

8.1 Prepare Secondary Antibody Cocktail in Labeling Solution:
- Donkey anti-rabbit IgG conjugated to **Alexa Fluor 488** (Thermo Fisher A21206), 1:400 dilution
- Donkey anti-mouse IgG conjugated to **Alexa Fluor 568** (Thermo Fisher A10037), 1:400 dilution
- Donkey anti-goat IgG conjugated to **Alexa Fluor 647** (Thermo Fisher A21447), 1:400 dilution

8.2 Incubation with secondary antibody cocktail (protected from light, gentle rolling agitation). (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 5 days)

---

### 9 Nuclear Counterstain (DAPI)

9.1 Wash secondary antibody with Labeling Solution. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 5 × 1 hour)

9.2 Incubation with DAPI (4′,6-diamidino-2-phenylindole) at 5 µg/mL in 1× PBS + 0.1% (vol/vol) Triton X-100. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours, protected from light)

9.3 Wash with 1× PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 × 30 minutes)

---

### 10 Post-labeling Dehydration (Second Methanol Series)

10.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in H₂O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

10.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in H₂O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

10.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in H₂O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

10.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in H₂O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

10.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol (anhydrous). (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

10.6 Repeat 100% methanol incubation (second change). (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

---

### 11 Delipidation with Dichloromethane (DCM)

11.1 Incubation with 66% (vol/vol) DCM (dichloromethane) / 33% (vol/vol) methanol to initiate lipid extraction from the large, lipid-rich liver parenchyma. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours, fume hood, gentle shaking)

11.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DCM (two changes) to complete delipidation. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 × 30 minutes, fume hood)

---

### 12 Refractive Index Matching with DBE

12.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DBE (dibenzyl ether, Sigma-Aldrich 108014, RI = 1.559) — first change — without shaking, protected from light. (Temperature: RT, Time: 4 hours)

12.2 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) DBE — second change — until sample is fully transparent and uniformly clear throughout the ~20 mm depth. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12–24 hours, protected from light)

---

### 13 Sample Storage and Imaging Preparation

13.1 Transfer cleared liver into a glass imaging chamber (e.g., custom 3D-printed holder or glass cuvette) filled with 100% DBE. Ensure sample is fully submerged and mechanically stabilized with low-melting agarose (1% in DBE-compatible medium) or custom spacers to prevent movement during acquisition. (Temperature: RT)

13.2 Store cleared sample in sealed glass vial filled with 100% DBE, protected from light, until imaging. (Temperature: RT, Time: up to 4 weeks)

13.3 For light-sheet fluorescence microscopy (LSFM) acquisition: mount sample in DBE-filled chamber compatible with the objective dipping medium (RI-matched objective, e.g., ×4 or ×10 LSFM objective corrected for RI ≈ 1.56). Acquire four channels sequentially:
- Channel 1: DAPI (405 nm excitation) — nuclear reference / tissue zoning
- Channel 2: Alexa Fluor 488 (488 nm excitation) — CK19 (primary bile duct marker)
- Channel 3: Alexa Fluor 568 (561 nm excitation) — CK7 (cross-validation bile duct marker)
- Channel 4: Alexa Fluor 647 (638 nm excitation) — CD31 (vascular negative reference)
(Temperature: RT, Z-step: 2–5 µm for full volumetric reconstruction)

**Chosen Method:** iDISCO+
**Chosen Labeling:** [CK19 (导管) + Alexa Fluor 647, CD31 (PECAM1) + Alexa Fluor 568, Lectin + Alexa Fluor 488, DAPI]

**Justification:** iDISCO+ is selected because: (1) it achieves excellent clearing of large, lipid-rich solid organs such as intact mouse liver (~20×15×10 mm) through organic solvent-based delipidation (methanol + DCM/DBE), yielding high transparency suitable for light-sheet microscopy; (2) its methanol-based pretreatment and detergent-based immunolabeling protocol supports deep antibody penetration into thick tissues via extended incubation at 37 °C; (3) organic solvent-compatible fluorophores (Alexa Fluor series) are well-preserved under DBE RI-matching. Labeling strategy: **CK19** (biliary epithelial marker) labels the entire intrahepatic bile duct network including main trunks, branches, and terminal ductules — directly addressing the bile duct reactive proliferation and remodeling question; **CD31 (PECAM1)** labels portal vein and hepatic artery endothelium to define portal tract spatial coordinates; **Lectin** (perfused or bath-applied) labels vascular luminal surfaces as an auxiliary portal tract channel; **DAPI** provides nuclear counterstain for tissue architecture reference. This multi-channel combination enables co-registration of bile duct topology with portal tract positions across all liver lobes.

---

**Protocol Steps:**

**1 Post-fixation Wash**
1.1 Wash fixed intact liver (4% PFA-fixed) with 1× PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour × 3 washes)

**2 Lectin Vascular Labeling (Pre-clearing Intravascular Perfusion Substitute — Bath Application)**
2.1 Incubate tissue in 1× PBS containing Lectin–Alexa Fluor 488 conjugate (50 µg/mL, e.g., Lycopersicon esculentum lectin or GSL I-IB4 conjugated to Alexa Fluor 488) with gentle rocking to label luminal vascular surfaces. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 48 hours)
2.2 Wash with 1× PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour × 3 washes)
2.3 Post-fix with 4% PFA in PBS to stabilize lectin signal. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
2.4 Wash with 1× PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes × 2 washes)

**3 Pretreatment — Methanol Dehydration Series**
3.1 Incubate with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in ddH₂O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
3.2 Incubate with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in ddH₂O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
3.3 Incubate with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in ddH₂O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
3.4 Incubate with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in ddH₂O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
3.5 Incubate with 100% methanol. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
3.6 Incubate with 100% methanol (second change). (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

**4 Bleaching**
4.1 Incubate with chilled fresh 5% H₂O₂ in methanol (1 volume 30% H₂O₂ : 5 volumes 100% MeOH) to quench autofluorescence (critical for liver due to high intrinsic autofluorescence). (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 16 hours)

**5 Rehydration**
5.1 Incubate with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in ddH₂O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
5.2 Incubate with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in ddH₂O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
5.3 Incubate with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in ddH₂O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
5.4 Incubate with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in ddH₂O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
5.5 Incubate with 1× PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

**6 Permeabilization and Blocking**
6.1 Incubate with permeabilization/blocking solution: PBS containing 0.2% Triton X-100, 10% DMSO, 0.3 M glycine, 5% normal donkey serum (PTxs-Glycine-NDS). (Temperature: 37 °C, Time: 48 hours)

**7 Primary Antibody Immunolabeling**
7.1 Prepare primary antibody cocktail in PTwH (PBS + 0.2% Tween-20 + 10 µg/mL heparin) + 5% DMSO + 3% normal donkey serum:
- Anti-CK19 (rabbit monoclonal, e.g., Abcam ab52625), 1:200 dilution — bile duct epithelial network
- Anti-CD31/PECAM1 (goat polyclonal, e.g., R&D AF3628), 1:100 dilution — portal tract vascular endothelium
7.2 Incubate tissue in primary antibody cocktail with gentle rocking. (Temperature: 37 °C, Time: 7 days)
7.3 Wash with PTwH (PBS + 0.2% Tween-20 + 10 µg/mL heparin). (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour × 5 washes over 24 hours)

**8 Secondary Antibody Immunolabeling**
8.1 Prepare secondary antibody cocktail in PTwH + 3% normal donkey serum:
- Donkey anti-rabbit Alexa Fluor 647 (1:400) — for CK19
- Donkey anti-goat Alexa Fluor 568 (1:400) — for CD31
8.2 Incubate tissue in secondary antibody cocktail with gentle rocking, protected from light. (Temperature: 37 °C, Time: 5 days)
8.3 Wash with PTwH. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour × 5 washes over 24 hours)

**9 Nuclear Counterstain**
9.1 Incubate with DAPI (5 µg/mL in PTwH) to label nuclei for tissue architecture reference. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)
9.2 Wash with PTwH. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour × 3 washes)
9.3 Wash with 1× PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour × 2 washes)

**10 Dehydration for Clearing**
10.1 Incubate with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in ddH₂O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
10.2 Incubate with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in ddH₂O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
10.3 Incubate with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in ddH₂O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
10.4 Incubate with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in ddH₂O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
10.5 Incubate with 100% methanol. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
10.6 Incubate with 100% methanol (second change). (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

**11 Delipidation**
11.1 Incubate with 33% (vol/vol) DCM (dichloromethane) in methanol (1 volume DCM : 2 volumes MeOH) to initiate lipid extraction. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours)
11.2 Incubate with 100% DCM (two changes) to complete delipidation of the lipid-rich liver tissue. (Temperature: RT, Time: 15 minutes × 2)

**12 Refractive Index Matching**
12.1 Incubate with 100% DBE (dibenzyl ether, Sigma 108014) without shaking, protected from light, until tissue becomes fully transparent (RI = 1.559, matched to light-sheet imaging). (Temperature: RT, Time: 24–48 hours, check transparency at 24 h; extend to 48 h if core opacity persists for this large liver volume)

**13 Storage Prior to Imaging**
13.1 Store cleared liver in fresh 100% DBE in a sealed glass vial, protected from light. (Temperature: RT, Time: up to 4 weeks; image as soon as possible to minimize fluorescence decay)

**14 Imaging Preparation**
14.1 Mount cleared liver in a DBE-filled imaging chamber (glass-bottom dish or custom agarose mold with DBE overlay) compatible with the light-sheet microscope objective (e.g., LSFM with 4× or 12× long-working-distance objective, RI-corrected for DBE = 1.559).
14.2 Acquire multi-channel z-stacks:
- Channel 1: 488 nm excitation → Lectin–Alexa Fluor 488 (portal/hepatic vasculature lumen)
- Channel 2: 561 nm excitation → CD31–Alexa Fluor 568 (portal tract endothelium)
- Channel 3: 647 nm excitation → CK19–Alexa Fluor 647 (bile duct epithelial network)
- Channel 4: 405 nm excitation → DAPI (nuclear architecture)
