model_response:
**Chosen Method:** iDISCO+
**Chosen Labeling:** [PGP9.5 + Alexa Fluor 647, Lectin + Alexa Fluor 555, DAPI]

**Justification:** iDISCO+ is selected because it employs organic solvent-based delipidation (methanol + DCM/DBE) that efficiently clears small, lipid-rich human skin biopsies (3–4 mm diameter, 2–3 mm thick) while preserving antigenicity for whole-mount immunolabeling. Its methanol dehydration/rehydration cycle permeabilizes the dense stratum corneum and dermis, enabling deep antibody penetration without sectioning. PGP9.5 (protein gene product 9.5, a pan-axonal marker identical to the clinical gold standard for IENF quantification) is used to label intraepidermal nerve fibers and their dermal parent fibers, directly supporting small fiber neuropathy diagnosis. Lectin (e.g., tomato lectin or IB4, both listed in the allowed Dye list) is used as a vascular counterstain to label endothelial glycocalyx of dermal papillary and superficial dermal vessels, providing the required vascular reference network. DAPI labels nuclei to delineate the dermo-epidermal junction, epidermal layers, and dermal papillae, enabling spatial relationship analysis. The final RI matching with DBE (n ≈ 1.56) is compatible with both confocal and light-sheet microscopy. The entire workflow is optimized for small human biopsy dimensions, with shortened incubation times relative to whole-organ protocols.

---

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Sample Preparation and Pre-fixation Wash
1.1 Receive fresh clinical punch biopsy (3–4 mm diameter, 2–3 mm thick) immediately post-excision; trim excess subcutaneous fat with a scalpel to retain epidermis, papillary dermis, and superficial reticular dermis only. (Temperature: RT, Time: 5 min)
1.2 Wash tissue in 1× PBS (pH 7.4) to remove blood and surface contaminants. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 × 5 min)

2 Post-fixation
2.1 Immerse tissue in 4% (wt/vol) paraformaldehyde (PFA) in 1× PBS (pH 7.4). (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 24 hours)
2.2 Wash in 1× PBS (pH 7.4). (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 × 20 min)

3 Dehydration (Methanol Series)
3.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in H₂O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
3.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in H₂O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
3.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in H₂O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
3.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in H₂O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
3.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
3.6 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol (second change). (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

4 Bleaching (Peroxide Treatment to Reduce Autofluorescence)
4.1 Incubation with chilled fresh 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in 100% methanol (1 volume 30% H₂O₂ : 5 volumes MeOH). (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)

5 Rehydration (Methanol Series, Reverse)
5.1 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in H₂O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
5.2 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in H₂O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
5.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in H₂O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
5.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in H₂O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
5.5 Incubation with 1× PBS (pH 7.4). (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

6 Permeabilization and Blocking
6.1 Incubation with permeabilization buffer: 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100, 20% (vol/vol) DMSO, 0.3 M glycine in 1× PBS (pH 7.4). (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)
6.2 Incubation with blocking buffer: 0.2% (vol/vol) Tween-20, 10% (vol/vol) DMSO, 6% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum (NDS) in 1× PBS (pH 7.4). (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)

7 Primary Antibody Labeling
7.1 Prepare primary antibody cocktail in antibody diluent buffer (0.2% Tween-20, 10% DMSO, 3% NDS in 1× PBS):
— Anti-PGP9.5 (rabbit polyclonal, e.g., Abcam ab10404) at 1:200 dilution (targets IENF and dermal nerve fibers)
— Biotinylated Lectin (e.g., Lycopersicon esculentum / tomato lectin, Vector Labs B-1175) at 5 µg/mL (targets vascular endothelial glycocalyx for blood vessel network visualization). (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 48 hours)
7.2 Wash in PTwH buffer (0.2% Tween-20, 0.1% heparin sodium salt in 1× PBS). (Temperature: RT, Time: 5 × 1 hour)

8 Secondary Antibody and Streptavidin Labeling
8.1 Prepare secondary labeling cocktail in antibody diluent buffer (0.2% Tween-20, 3% NDS in 1× PBS):
— Donkey anti-rabbit IgG conjugated to Alexa Fluor 647 at 1:400 dilution (detects PGP9.5 → IENF channel)
— Streptavidin conjugated to Alexa Fluor 555 at 1:400 dilution (detects biotinylated Lectin → vascular channel). (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)
8.2 Wash in PTwH buffer. (Temperature: RT, Time: 5 × 1 hour)

9 Nuclear Counterstain (DAPI)
9.1 Incubation with DAPI (4′,6-diamidino-2-phenylindole) at 5 µg/mL in 1× PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)
9.2 Wash in 1× PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 × 20 min)

10 Dehydration (Pre-clearing Methanol Series)
10.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in H₂O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 min)
10.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in H₂O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 min)
10.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in H₂O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 min)
10.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in H₂O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 min)
10.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 min)
10.6 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol (second change). (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 min)

11 Delipidation
11.1 Incubation with 33% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) / 67% (vol/vol) methanol (DCM:MeOH = 1:2 vol/vol). (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours)
11.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DCM (two changes) to remove residual methanol. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 × 15 min)

12 Refractive Index Matching
12.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dibenzyl ether (DBE, Sigma-Aldrich 108014; RI ≈ 1.56) without shaking, in a sealed glass vial protected from light. Replace with fresh DBE after first 2 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 4 hours total, with one change at 2 hours)
12.2 Confirm tissue is fully transparent and uniformly matched before imaging; store in fresh DBE in sealed glass vial protected from light until imaging. (Temperature: RT, Time: up to 7 days)

13 Mounting and Imaging Preparation
13.1 Mount cleared biopsy in a glass-bottom imaging chamber or between two coverslips using DBE as the immersion/mounting medium; seal edges with silicone grease to prevent evaporation. Orient tissue with the epidermal surface facing the objective. (Temperature: RT, Time: 10 min)
13.2 Image using confocal microscope (25× water-immersion or silicone-oil objective, NA ≥ 0.95) or light-sheet fluorescence microscope with DBE-compatible objective; acquire z-stacks spanning full biopsy thickness (2–3 mm) with ≤ 2 µm z-step for IENF channel (Alexa Fluor 647, Ex/Em 650/668 nm), ≤ 5 µm z-step for vascular channel (Alexa Fluor 555, Ex/Em 555/565 nm), and nuclear channel (DAPI, Ex/Em 360/460 nm). (Temperature: RT, Time: per imaging session)

**Chosen Method:** iDISCO+
**Chosen Labeling:** [PGP9.5 + Alexa Fluor 647, Collagen IV + Alexa Fluor 568, DAPI]

**Justification:**
iDISCO+ is selected because it provides excellent antibody penetration into fixed, lipid-rich skin tissue through organic solvent-based delipidation (methanol/DCM/DBE), which is critical for labeling the dense keratinocyte layers and dermal matrix of a 3–4 mm biopsy punch. The solvent-based clearing achieves high transparency and RI homogeneity suitable for confocal or light-sheet 3D imaging of thin but structurally complex skin. PGP9.5 (protein gene product 9.5, a pan-axonal marker identical to UCHL1) is the gold-standard antibody target for IENF identification and density quantification in small fiber neuropathy diagnostics, directly fulfilling the primary scientific goal. Collagen IV labels the basement membrane at the dermal-epidermal junction (DEJ), providing a continuous structural reference to delineate the DEJ boundary and dermal papillae, enabling accurate assignment of nerve fibers as intraepidermal vs. subepidermal and supporting volumetric IENF density calculations. DAPI labels keratinocyte nuclei to define epidermal thickness, stratification layers, and tissue orientation, serving as the auxiliary channel for epidermal architecture. CD31 was considered for vascular reference but Collagen IV was preferred as it simultaneously marks the DEJ and vessel basement membranes, providing both structural references in a single channel. The three-channel strategy (nerve / DEJ+vasculature / nuclei) directly addresses the stated needs: continuous nerve fiber tracing, epidermal thickness measurement, dermal papilla structure, and avoidance of orientation/sectioning bias through full 3D volumetric acquisition.

---

**Protocol Steps:**

**1 Post-fixation Wash**
1.1 Wash fixed biopsy (3–4 mm diameter, 2–3 mm thick, 4% PFA-fixed) with 1× PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 × 10 minutes)

**2 Pretreatment – Methanol Dehydration Series**
2.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in ddH₂O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
2.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in ddH₂O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
2.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in ddH₂O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
2.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in ddH₂O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
2.5 Incubation with 100% methanol. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
2.6 Incubation with 100% methanol (second change). (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

**3 Bleaching (H₂O₂ / Methanol)**
3.1 Incubation with chilled fresh 5% H₂O₂ in 100% methanol (1 volume 30% H₂O₂ : 5 volumes MeOH). (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)

**4 Rehydration Series**
4.1 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in ddH₂O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
4.2 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in ddH₂O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
4.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in ddH₂O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
4.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in ddH₂O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
4.5 Incubation with 1× PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 × 15 minutes)

**5 Permeabilization and Blocking**
5.1 Incubation with permeabilization buffer: 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100, 20% (vol/vol) DMSO, 0.3 M glycine in 1× PBS. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)
5.2 Incubation with blocking buffer: 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100, 10% (vol/vol) DMSO, 6% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum (NDS) in 1× PBS. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)

**6 Primary Antibody Incubation**
6.1 Prepare primary antibody cocktail in PTwH buffer (1× PBS, 0.2% Tween-20, 10 µg/mL heparin) supplemented with 5% (vol/vol) DMSO and 3% (vol/vol) NDS:
- Rabbit anti-PGP9.5 (UCHL1) at 1:400 dilution
- Mouse anti-Collagen IV at 1:300 dilution
6.2 Incubation with primary antibody cocktail. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 48 hours, with gentle rocking)
6.3 Wash with PTwH buffer. (Temperature: RT, Time: 5 × 1 hour, with gentle rocking)

**7 Secondary Antibody Incubation**
7.1 Prepare secondary antibody cocktail in PTwH buffer supplemented with 3% (vol/vol) NDS:
- Donkey anti-Rabbit IgG conjugated to Alexa Fluor 647 at 1:500 dilution (for PGP9.5 / IENF channel)
- Donkey anti-Mouse IgG conjugated to Alexa Fluor 568 at 1:500 dilution (for Collagen IV / DEJ channel)
7.2 Incubation with secondary antibody cocktail. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours, with gentle rocking, protected from light)
7.3 Wash with PTwH buffer. (Temperature: RT, Time: 5 × 1 hour, protected from light)

**8 Nuclear Counterstain (DAPI)**
8.1 Incubation with DAPI at 5 µg/mL in 1× PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours, protected from light)
8.2 Wash with 1× PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 × 15 minutes, protected from light)

**9 Dehydration for Clearing**
9.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in ddH₂O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
9.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in ddH₂O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
9.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in ddH₂O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
9.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in ddH₂O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
9.5 Incubation with 100% methanol. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
9.6 Incubation with 100% methanol (second change). (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

**10 Delipidation**
10.1 Incubation with 33% (vol/vol) DCM (dichloromethane) in 100% methanol (1:2 DCM:MeOH). (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours)
10.2 Incubation with 100% DCM (two changes) to wash out methanol. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 × 15 minutes)

**11 Refractive Index Matching**
11.1 Incubation with 100% DBE (dibenzyl ether, Sigma-Aldrich 108014) without shaking, in a glass vial, protected from light. Tissue should sink and become fully transparent. (Temperature: RT, Time: 4 hours)
11.2 Replace with fresh 100% DBE and confirm full optical transparency of the biopsy. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours, protected from light)

**12 Storage Prior to Imaging**
12.1 Store cleared biopsy in 100% DBE in a sealed glass vial, protected from light. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: up to 4 weeks)

**13 Mounting for Imaging**
13.1 Transfer cleared biopsy into a glass-bottom imaging chamber or custom PTFE holder filled with 100% DBE (RI ≈ 1.56). Orient the biopsy with the epidermal surface facing the objective to ensure optimal IENF signal acquisition from the DEJ upward.
13.2 Seal the chamber with a glass coverslip using silicone grease to prevent DBE evaporation. (Temperature: RT)
13.3 Acquire 3D z-stack images using a confocal or light-sheet microscope equipped with an oil-immersion or DBE-compatible objective (e.g., 25× NA 0.95 or 20× NA 0.8 long-working-distance objective). Recommended channels: DAPI (405 nm excitation), Alexa Fluor 568 (561 nm excitation), Alexa Fluor 647 (638 nm excitation). Z-step: 1–2 µm throughout the full biopsy thickness.

**Justification:**
iDISCO+ is selected over CUBIC for this revised protocol for the following reasons:
1. **Melanin bleaching compatibility:** iDISCO+ includes a methanol-based dehydration and H₂O₂ bleaching step that effectively reduces melanin pigmentation in the stratum basale, directly addressing the primary interference problem identified in the problem statement. CUBIC-L/RA does not include a dedicated bleaching step and is less effective at melanin removal in human skin.
2. **Antibody penetration in dense skin tissue:** iDISCO+ uses methanol-based permeabilization and detergent washes that enhance antibody penetration through the compact stratum corneum and dermis of human skin punch biopsies (3–4 mm diameter, 2–3 mm thick), which is superior to the aqueous CUBIC approach for dense keratinized tissue.
3. **Fluorescence preservation with Alexa Fluor dyes:** iDISCO+ is well-validated for Alexa Fluor-conjugated secondary antibodies, which are bright and photostable, compensating for the inherently weak IENF signal.
4. **Marker selection rationale:**
   - **PGP9.5 (UCHL1):** The gold-standard pan-axonal marker for IENF detection and density quantification in small fiber neuropathy diagnosis; provides reliable labeling of intraepidermal nerve fibers and their terminals.
   - **CD31 (PECAM1):** Labels dermal vascular endothelium, providing a 3D vascular reference map of the superficial dermal plexus to serve as spatial landmarks for IENF counting and tissue layer orientation.
   - **DAPI:** Labels nuclei to delineate the dermo-epidermal junction (DEJ), epidermal layers, and tissue architecture, enabling precise IENF crossing-point identification at the DEJ.
5. **Low deformation:** The iDISCO+ final RI matching medium (DBE, n ≈ 1.56) provides excellent tissue transparency with minimal swelling, preserving the thin epidermal layer geometry critical for accurate IENF density measurement.
6. **3D imaging compatibility:** DBE-cleared samples are directly compatible with light-sheet fluorescence microscopy (LSFM) and oil-immersion confocal microscopy for volumetric IENF tracing and automated counting.

**0 Pre-treatment Notes**
Tissue is a 3–4 mm diameter, 2–3 mm thick human skin punch biopsy, already PFA-fixed (4% PFA, 24 h, 4 °C) and post-fixed. 2.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in ddH₂O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

2.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in ddH₂O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

2.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in ddH₂O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

2.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in ddH₂O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

2.5 Incubation with 100% methanol (anhydrous). (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

2.6 Incubation with 100% methanol (anhydrous), second change. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

---

**3 Melanin Bleaching (H₂O₂ in Methanol)**

3.1 Prepare fresh bleaching solution: 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in 100% methanol (1 volume 30% H₂O₂ : 5 volumes 100% MeOH). Pre-chill to 4 °C before use.

3.2 Incubation with chilled fresh 5% H₂O₂ in methanol. Protect from light. This step bleaches melanin granules in the stratum basale and reduces autofluorescence. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 16 hours)

3.3 Check bleaching: tissue should appear visibly depigmented. If residual brown pigmentation remains, replace with fresh bleaching solution and continue for an additional 4–8 hours at 4 °C.

---

**4 Methanol Rehydration**

4.1 Incubation with 100% methanol (anhydrous) to remove H₂O₂. (Temperature: RT, Time: 20 minutes)

4.2 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in ddH₂O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 20 minutes)

4.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in ddH₂O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 20 minutes)

4.4 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in ddH₂O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 20 minutes)

4.5 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in ddH₂O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 20 minutes)

4.6 Incubation with 1× PBS (pH 7.4). (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 × 15 minutes)

---

**5 Enhanced Permeabilization and Blocking**

5.1 Incubation with permeabilization solution: 1× PBS containing 0.2% (wt/vol) gelatin, 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100, 0.01% (wt/vol) sodium azide (PTxwH). (Temperature: 37 °C, Time: 2 hours)

5.2 Incubation with blocking solution: 1× PBS containing 0.2% (wt/vol) gelatin, 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100, 0.01% (wt/vol) sodium azide, and 10% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum (NDS) (PTxwH + 10% NDS). (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours)

---

**6 Primary Antibody Immunolabeling**

6.1 Prepare primary antibody cocktail in PTxwH + 5% NDS:
- Anti-PGP9.5 (rabbit polyclonal, e.g., Abcam ab10404): 1:500 dilution
- Anti-CD31/PECAM1 (mouse monoclonal, e.g., Dako JC70A or equivalent): 1:200 dilution

6.2 Incubation with primary antibody cocktail. Gently rock at 37 °C for the first 24 hours, then continue at 37 °C. (Temperature: 37 °C, Time: 48 hours)

6.3 Wash with PTxwH (1× PBS + 0.2% gelatin + 0.5% Triton X-100 + 0.01% NaN₃). (Temperature: RT, Time: 5 × 1 hour)

---

**7 Secondary Antibody Immunolabeling and Nuclear Counterstain**

7.1 Prepare secondary antibody cocktail in PTxwH + 5% NDS:
- Donkey anti-rabbit Alexa Fluor 488 (for PGP9.5/IENF): 1:500 dilution
- Donkey anti-mouse Alexa Fluor 647 (for CD31/vasculature): 1:500 dilution
- DAPI: 1 µg/mL (for nuclear/DEJ reference)

7.2 Incubation with secondary antibody and DAPI cocktail. Protect from light. (Temperature: 37 °C, Time: 48 hours)

7.3 Wash with PTxwH. Protect from light. (Temperature: RT, Time: 5 × 1 hour)

7.4 Post-fixation wash: incubation with 1× PBS containing 4% (wt/vol) PFA to stabilize antibody-antigen complexes. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

7.5 Wash with 1× PBS (pH 7.4). (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 × 10 minutes)

---

**8 Methanol Dehydration (pre-clearing)**

8.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in ddH₂O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

8.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in ddH₂O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

8.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in ddH₂O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

8.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in ddH₂O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

8.5 Incubation with 100% methanol (anhydrous). (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

8.6 Incubation with 100% methanol (anhydrous), second change. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

---

**9 Delipidation with Dichloromethane (DCM)**

9.1 Incubation with 66% (vol/vol) DCM / 33% methanol (2:1 DCM:MeOH). This step removes residual lipids and further reduces light scattering in the dermis. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours)

9.2 Incubation with 100% DCM (anhydrous, Sigma 270997). Two changes to ensure complete methanol removal. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 × 15 minutes)

---

**10 Refractive Index Matching and Optical Clearing**

10.1 Transfer tissue to glass vial. Incubation with 100% dibenzyl ether (DBE, Sigma 108014; RI ≈ 1.562). Ensure tissue is fully submerged. Protect from light. Tissue should become transparent within 1–3 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3–12 hours, until fully transparent)

10.2 Replace with fresh 100% DBE. Store in sealed glass vial protected from light until imaging. (Temperature: RT or 4 °C, Time: up to 2 weeks)

---

**11 Sample Mounting and Imaging Preparation**

11.1 Mount cleared tissue in a custom imaging chamber or glass-bottom dish filled with 100% DBE. Orient the tissue with the epidermis facing the objective for IENF imaging. Use DBE-compatible silicone or PTFE spacers to prevent compression.

11.2 For light-sheet fluorescence microscopy (LSFM): use a DBE-compatible dipping objective (e.g., Zeiss Plan-Apochromat 20×/1.0 or Olympus XLPLN25XWMP2 with DBE-compatible immersion). Acquire z-stacks spanning the full 2–3 mm tissue depth at 1–2 µm z-step intervals for IENF tracing; use 5 µm z-steps for full-volume vascular reference.

11.3 For confocal microscopy: use an oil-immersion objective (63×/1.4 NA) with DBE as immersion medium. Acquire tile-scan z-stacks covering the full biopsy area.

11.4 Imaging channels:
- DAPI (405 nm excitation): nuclear/DEJ reference, epidermal layer delineation
- Alexa Fluor 488 (488 nm excitation): PGP9.5⁺ IENF fibers and terminals
- Alexa Fluor 647 (633/647 nm excitation): CD31⁺ dermal vascular network

11.5 For IENF density quantification: use 3D image analysis software (e.g., Imaris, Fiji with Simple Neurite Tracer, or NeuronJ) to trace individual nerve fibers crossing the DEJ (identified by DAPI nuclear layer boundary) and count IENF per unit epidermal surface area (fibers/mm²) in 3D volumetric reconstructions.

model_response:
**Chosen Method:** ClearSee
**Chosen Labeling:** [EGFP, mCherry]

**Justification:** ClearSee is an aqueous-based optical clearing method specifically developed and validated for *C. elegans*, making it the optimal choice for intact adult worms (~1 mm length, 50–100 μm diameter). It was designed to preserve endogenous fluorescent protein signals (including GFP/EGFP and RFP/mCherry variants) while achieving high transparency in the cuticle-enclosed worm body. Unlike solvent-based methods (iDISCO+, uDISCO, FDISCO), ClearSee does not require dehydration steps that would quench or destroy GFP and mCherry fluorescence. Compared to CUBIC or PEGASOS, ClearSee is specifically optimized for the small dimensions and cuticle barrier of *C. elegans*, providing sufficient clearing without over-processing. Since the worms already carry EGFP and mCherry/RFP endogenous reporters in neuronal populations, no additional antibody labeling or chemical dyes are required—the dual-color endogenous signals are sufficient to resolve the nerve ring, head neuron soma, neurites, and major nerve bundles in 3D. The RI matching solution used in ClearSee (88% Histodenz) is compatible with confocal and spinning-disk microscopy, which are standard for *C. elegans* neuroimaging at this scale.

---

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Sample Preparation and Pre-clearing Wash
1.1 Transfer fixed adult *C. elegans* (post-fixation in 4% PFA/PBS) into a 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tube. Wash with 1× PBS (phosphate-buffered saline, pH 7.4) by gentle inversion. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 × 5 minutes)
1.2 Remove residual fixative by washing with PBST (1× PBS + 0.1% Tween-20) to permeabilize the cuticle slightly and facilitate reagent penetration. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 × 10 minutes)

2 ClearSee Clearing
2.1 Prepare ClearSee solution: 10% (wt/vol) xylitol, 15% (wt/vol) sodium deoxycholate (SDC), 25% (wt/vol) urea in distilled water. Filter-sterilize (0.22 μm) and store at RT protected from light.
2.2 Incubate worms in ClearSee solution (approximately 200 μL per tube, ensuring worms are fully submerged) with gentle rocking. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 days)
2.3 Replace ClearSee solution with fresh ClearSee solution and continue incubation until worms appear optically transparent (typically total 3–7 days depending on batch). Check transparency under a stereomicroscope daily. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2–4 additional days, replace solution every 2 days)

3 Fluorescence Signal Verification
3.1 After clearing, briefly image a test worm on a glass slide with a coverslip in ClearSee solution using a fluorescence stereomicroscope or widefield epifluorescence microscope. Verify retention of EGFP signal (excitation ~488 nm, emission ~507 nm) and mCherry/RFP signal (excitation ~587 nm, emission ~610 nm) before proceeding to RI matching. (Temperature: RT, Time: 5–10 minutes)

4 Refractive Index (RI) Matching
4.1 Prepare RI matching solution: 88% (wt/vol) Histodenz (Sigma-Aldrich D2158) in 0.02 M phosphate buffer (pH 7.4). Dissolve by gentle warming at 37 °C and vortexing; final RI ≈ 1.458. Filter through 0.22 μm membrane. Store at 4 °C protected from light.
4.2 Transfer cleared worms from ClearSee into 88% Histodenz RI matching solution. Incubate with gentle rocking to allow equilibration. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)
4.3 Replace with fresh 88% Histodenz solution and continue equilibration. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)

5 Sample Mounting for 3D Imaging
5.1 Prepare imaging chamber: apply two layers of double-sided tape (~100 μm spacer) or use a commercially available imaging spacer (e.g., SecureSeal, 0.12 mm depth) on a #1.5 high-precision coverslip (0.17 mm thickness, refractive index matched to objective specification).
5.2 Transfer 2–5 cleared worms in a minimal volume (~5 μL) of 88% Histodenz onto the imaging coverslip within the spacer chamber. Orient worms laterally (left-right) or dorsoventrally as needed for nerve ring imaging using a fine eyelash tool or pulled glass capillary.
5.3 Carefully place a second #1.5 coverslip on top, avoiding air bubbles. Seal all edges with clear nail varnish or VALAP (1:1:1 vaseline:lanolin:paraffin wax). (Temperature: RT, Time: 10–15 minutes for sealing and curing)
5.4 Allow sealed slides to equilibrate horizontally before imaging. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)

6 3D Confocal Imaging
6.1 Image mounted samples on a laser-scanning confocal or spinning-disk confocal microscope equipped with a 40× or 63× oil-immersion objective (NA ≥ 1.3, immersion oil RI = 1.515; note: slight RI mismatch with Histodenz at 1.458 is acceptable for worm-scale imaging; alternatively use a water-dipping or glycerol objective for better RI matching). Acquire EGFP channel: 488 nm laser excitation, 500–540 nm emission bandpass filter. (Temperature: RT, Time: per acquisition)
6.2 Acquire mCherry/RFP channel: 561 nm or 594 nm laser excitation, 600–650 nm emission bandpass filter. Sequential acquisition mode to minimize spectral bleed-through between EGFP and mCherry channels. (Temperature: RT, Time: per acquisition)
6.3 Acquire Z-stack spanning the full dorsoventral depth of the worm (~50–100 μm) with Z-step size of 0.3–0.5 μm for nerve ring region and 0.5–1.0 μm for full-body neuronal surveys. (Temperature: RT, Time: 15–60 minutes per worm depending on volume)

7 Post-imaging Storage
7.1 If re-imaging is required, store sealed slides horizontally at 4 °C in the dark. Fluorescence and transparency are stable in ClearSee/Histodenz for up to 2–4 weeks. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: up to 4 weeks)

model_response:
**Chosen Method:** ClearSee
**Chosen Labeling:** [EGFP (内源), mCherry (内源), DAPI]

**Justification:** ClearSee is specifically designed and validated for optical clearing of *C. elegans* whole-mount specimens. It is an aqueous-based, mild clearing solution (containing urea, Triton X-100, and sodium deoxycholate) that effectively reduces light scattering in the nematode cuticle and body while demonstrating excellent compatibility with GFP/EGFP and RFP/mCherry fluorescent protein signals—preserving both channels simultaneously without the quenching commonly seen with organic-solvent or strong oxidative methods (e.g., iDISCO+, uDISCO). The sample (fixed adult *C. elegans*, ~1 mm × 50–100 μm) is ideally suited to ClearSee: the small size means clearing is complete within hours to a few days, and no delipidation or dehydration steps are required, minimizing fluorophore degradation. DAPI is added as an optional nuclear counterstain to assist in anatomical registration of the nerve ring and ganglia. The endogenous EGFP and mCherry signals serve as the primary dual-color reporters for the two neuronal populations; no antibody amplification is required, preserving the direct genetically encoded labeling strategy.

---

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Post-fixation Verification and Pre-wash
1.1 Transfer fixed adult *C. elegans* worms (fixed in 4% paraformaldehyde/PBS) into a 1.5 mL low-binding microcentrifuge tube. Wash with 1× PBS (phosphate-buffered saline, pH 7.4). (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 × 5 minutes each wash)
1.2 Aspirate PBS carefully, leaving ~20 µL to avoid desiccation of the pellet. Confirm worms are intact under a stereomicroscope before proceeding. (Temperature: RT, Time: 5 minutes)

2 Permeabilization (to facilitate DAPI entry and ensure ClearSee penetration)
2.1 Incubate worms in permeabilization buffer: 1× PBS containing 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 and 1% (vol/vol) DMSO. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 × 15 minutes each, with gentle rocking)
2.2 Wash with 1× PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 × 5 minutes each wash)

3 DAPI Nuclear Counterstain (optional auxiliary step)
3.1 Incubate worms in DAPI solution: 1 µg/mL DAPI in 1× PBS containing 0.1% (vol/vol) Triton X-100. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes, protected from light, gentle rocking)
3.2 Wash with 1× PBS to remove excess DAPI. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 × 10 minutes each wash, protected from light)

4 Tissue Optical Clearing with ClearSee
4.1 Prepare fresh ClearSee solution: 10% (wt/vol) xylitol, 15% (wt/vol) sodium deoxycholate, 25% (wt/vol) urea in distilled water. Adjust to pH ~7.5 and filter through a 0.22 µm membrane. (Temperature: RT, preparation step)
4.2 Replace PBS with ClearSee solution. Incubate worms fully submerged in ClearSee. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours, gentle rocking, protected from light)
4.3 Replace with fresh ClearSee solution. Continue incubation until worms appear optically transparent (typically 1–3 days total; check clarity under stereomicroscope at 24 h intervals). (Temperature: RT, Time: 24–48 additional hours, protected from light)

5 Refractive Index (RI) Matching
5.1 ClearSee solution itself serves as the RI-matching medium (RI ≈ 1.44–1.45 at working concentration), which is compatible with water-dipping objectives (NA ≥ 0.8) and standard confocal/spinning-disk setups. Confirm worms remain in ClearSee for imaging without further medium exchange. (Temperature: RT, Time: equilibrate for at least 1 hour before imaging)
5.2 If using an oil-immersion or glycerol-immersion objective, transfer worms into 80% (vol/vol) glycerol in PBS (RI ≈ 1.45) as an alternative RI-matching medium. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1–2 hours equilibration, protected from light)

6 Sample Mounting for Confocal/Light-Sheet Imaging
6.1 Transfer cleared worms onto a #1.5 glass-bottom dish or coverslip-bottom chamber. Orient worms in the desired plane (lateral or dorsal) using a fine eyelash tool or pulled glass needle. (Temperature: RT, Time: 5–10 minutes)
6.2 Add sufficient ClearSee (or 80% glycerol/PBS) to fully cover the worms. Gently place a coverslip (for confocal) or leave open (for light-sheet dipping objective). Seal edges with clear nail varnish if using a coverslip to prevent evaporation. (Temperature: RT, Time: 5 minutes)
6.3 Allow the mounting medium to equilibrate and any bubbles to dissipate before imaging. (Temperature: RT, Time: 15–30 minutes)

7 Imaging Parameters (guidance)
7.1 Acquire EGFP channel: excitation 488 nm laser, emission 505–540 nm bandpass filter. Z-step: 0.5–1.0 µm for nerve ring region; 1.0–2.0 µm for full-body survey. (Temperature: RT, Time: per acquisition)
7.2 Acquire mCherry/RFP channel: excitation 561 nm laser, emission 590–650 nm bandpass filter. Sequential acquisition recommended to minimize spectral bleed-through between EGFP and mCherry channels. (Temperature: RT, Time: per acquisition)
7.3 Acquire DAPI channel (if used): excitation 405 nm laser, emission 420–480 nm bandpass filter. Use as anatomical reference for nerve ring and ganglia identification. (Temperature: RT, Time: per acquisition)

8 Sample Storage
8.1 Store cleared, mounted samples in ClearSee solution in sealed chambers at 4 °C in the dark. Fluorescence is stable for up to 2–4 weeks under these conditions. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: up to 4 weeks)

**Chosen Method:** ClearSee

**Chosen Labeling:** [EGFP, mCherry, Hoechst]

**Justification:** ClearSee is an aqueous-based optical clearing method specifically developed and validated for *C. elegans* and other small nematodes/plant tissues. It uses a xylitol/urea/sodium deoxycholate solution that achieves excellent transparency in intact worms (~1 mm length, 50–100 μm diameter) within days without organic solvents, thereby preserving GFP-family and RFP-family endogenous fluorescence signals with minimal photobleaching or signal loss. This is critical here because EGFP and mCherry/RFP are the primary reporters for dual-color neuronal circuit mapping. ClearSee is fully compatible with post-clearing nuclear staining (Hoechst 33342 penetrates well in cleared worms) to provide a morphological reference for cell body identification and worm orientation. The method requires no specialized equipment, is gentle enough for the delicate cuticle-enclosed nematode body, and achieves refractive index (RI) matching (~1.44) suitable for confocal or spinning-disk imaging with standard glass-bottom dishes or coverslip-mounted samples. Compared to solvent-based methods (iDISCO+, uDISCO, FDISCO), ClearSee avoids fluorophore quenching of mCherry/RFP and cuticle distortion. Compared to CUBIC, ClearSee is better validated specifically for *C. elegans* and does not require high-temperature incubation steps that risk epitope/fluorophore degradation.

---

**Protocol Steps:**

**1 Sample Collection and Pre-fixation Wash**

1.1 Transfer synchronized young adult *C. elegans* (24 h post-L4) from NGM plates into a 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tube using M9 buffer. Pellet worms by brief centrifugation at 300 × g. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 min)

1.2 Wash worms 3× with M9 buffer (1 mL per wash) to remove bacteria. Pellet by centrifugation at 300 × g between washes. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 min per wash)

1.3 Wash worms 2× with PBS (pH 7.4, 1 mL per wash) to exchange buffer. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 min per wash)

---

**2 Fixation**

2.1 Remove supernatant and resuspend worm pellet in freshly prepared 4% (wt/vol) paraformaldehyde (PFA) in PBS (pH 7.4), ~500 µL. Rotate gently on a tube rotator. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

2.2 Pellet worms at 300 × g and wash 3× with PBS (1 mL per wash) to remove residual PFA. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 min per wash)

2.3 Optional freeze-crack step to improve reagent penetration: resuspend fixed worms in PBS, transfer to a glass slide, place on dry ice for 5 min until frozen, then allow to thaw at RT. Repeat freeze-thaw cycle 3×. Return worms to microcentrifuge tube in PBS. (Temperature: RT / dry ice, Time: ~15 min total)

---

**3 Permeabilization**

3.1 Remove PBS supernatant and incubate worms in PBST (PBS + 0.1% (vol/vol) Triton X-100), 500 µL, with gentle rotation. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 min)

3.2 Remove PBST and incubate worms in PBST + 1% (vol/vol) β-mercaptoethanol (BME) + 1% (wt/vol) SDS, 500 µL, with gentle rotation. This step aids cuticle permeabilization without disrupting fluorescent protein structure. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)

3.3 Wash worms 3× with PBST (1 mL per wash, 5 min each) with gentle rotation. (Temperature: RT, Time: 5 min per wash)

---

**4 Nuclear Counterstain (Hoechst 33342 — Auxiliary Channel)**

4.1 Incubate worms in Hoechst 33342 solution at 5 µg/mL in PBST (500 µL), with gentle rotation, protected from light. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)

4.2 Wash worms 3× with PBST (1 mL per wash, 10 min each) with gentle rotation, protected from light. (Temperature: RT, Time: 10 min per wash)

4.3 Wash worms 1× with PBS (1 mL) to remove detergent before ClearSee incubation. (Temperature: RT, Time: 5 min)

---

**5 Optical Clearing with ClearSee**

5.1 Prepare ClearSee solution: dissolve 10% (wt/vol) xylitol, 15% (wt/vol) sodium deoxycholate, and 25% (wt/vol) urea in distilled water. Stir at 37 °C until fully dissolved, then cool to RT. Filter through a 0.22 µm membrane. Store at RT protected from light.

5.2 Remove PBS supernatant from worm pellet. Add 500 µL ClearSee solution. Incubate with gentle rotation, protected from light. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 days)

5.3 Replace ClearSee solution with fresh ClearSee (500 µL) and continue incubation with gentle rotation, protected from light. Monitor clearing progress daily; worms should become visually transparent. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 additional days; total ClearSee incubation: ~5 days)

---

**6 Refractive Index Matching**

6.1 Remove ClearSee and incubate worms in fresh ClearSee solution supplemented with 50% (wt/vol) xylitol (high-xylitol ClearSee, RI ≈ 1.44) to achieve final RI matching for confocal imaging. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)

6.2 Verify RI of the final mounting medium using a hand-held refractometer; target RI = 1.44 ± 0.01.

---

**7 Sample Mounting for Imaging**

7.1 Transfer cleared worms onto a #1.5 glass-bottom dish (35 mm, e.g., MatTek) or a glass-bottom 8-well chamber slide using a wide-bore pipette tip to avoid shearing. (Temperature: RT, Time: 5 min)

7.2 Remove excess liquid and add a small volume (~20 µL) of high-xylitol ClearSee mounting medium over the worms to maintain RI matching and prevent dehydration. (Temperature: RT, Time: immediate)

7.3 Gently place a #1.5 coverslip over the sample. Seal edges with clear nail varnish or VALAP (1:1:1 vaseline:lanolin:paraffin) to prevent evaporation. Allow sealant to cure. (Temperature: RT, Time: 10 min)

7.4 Store mounted samples protected from light at 4 °C until imaging. Image within 2 weeks for optimal fluorescence retention. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: up to 14 days)

---

**8 Confocal / Spinning-Disk Imaging Parameters (Guidance)**

8.1 Image on an inverted confocal or spinning-disk confocal microscope using a 40× water-immersion or 25× multi-immersion objective (NA ≥ 0.8). Acquire z-stacks with 0.5–1.0 µm step size to fully resolve the nerve ring (~20 µm diameter) and ventral nerve cord along the full 1 mm body length.

8.2 Acquire three channels sequentially to minimize spectral bleed-through:
- Channel 1: 405 nm excitation / 420–480 nm emission → Hoechst 33342 (nuclear reference)
- Channel 2: 488 nm excitation / 505–545 nm emission → EGFP (neuronal population A)
- Channel 3: 561 nm excitation / 580–650 nm emission → mCherry/RFP (neuronal population B)
(Temperature: RT, Time: per acquisition session)

8.3 Export z-stack image series as 16-bit TIFF files. Perform 3D reconstruction and spatial mapping of nerve ring, head ganglia, neuronal processes, and ventral nerve cord using Fiji/ImageJ (BigStitcher, 3D Viewer) or Imaris software with dual-color channel overlay. (Temperature: RT, Time: as required)

**Chosen Method:** ClearSee
**Chosen Labeling:** [EGFP, mCherry]

**Justification:** ClearSee is specifically designed and validated for *C. elegans* whole-mount specimens. It is an aqueous-based clearing solution (sodium deoxycholate + urea + Triton X-100) that achieves excellent refractive index matching for small nematode bodies (~1 mm × 50–100 μm) without organic solvents, thereby minimizing tissue deformation and shrinkage—critical for preserving the delicate architecture of the nerve ring, head ganglia, and major nerve bundles. Most importantly, ClearSee is well-documented to preserve GFP-family (EGFP) and RFP-family (mCherry/RFP) fluorescence signals with high fidelity, enabling dual-color endogenous reporter imaging without any additional labeling steps. The protocol is rapid (total ~3–5 days), compatible with standard confocal or spinning-disk microscopy, and requires no specialized equipment. Because the sample is already fixed and post-fixed, no additional fixation steps are needed; the protocol begins directly with permeabilization and clearing.

---

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Post-fixation Wash and Permeabilization
1.1 Wash fixed worms 3× with PBS (1×, pH 7.4) to remove residual fixative. (Temperature: RT, Time: 5 min per wash)
1.2 Incubate worms in PBST (1× PBS + 0.1% (vol/vol) Tween-20) to begin permeabilization and remove surface debris. (Temperature: RT, Time: 15 min)
1.3 Incubate worms in 1× PBS + 1% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 to enhance permeabilization of the cuticle. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 min)
1.4 Wash 2× with 1× PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 5 min per wash)

2 Pre-clearing Equilibration
2.1 Incubate worms in ClearSee working solution [10% (wt/vol) sodium deoxycholate + 25% (wt/vol) urea + 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in ddH₂O, freshly prepared and filter-sterilized] at low concentration (50% diluted in 1× PBS) to gently begin RI equilibration and reduce osmotic shock. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)

3 Tissue Optical Clearing
3.1 Transfer worms to full-strength ClearSee solution [10% (wt/vol) sodium deoxycholate + 25% (wt/vol) urea + 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in ddH₂O] in a 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tube with gentle rotation. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)
3.2 Replace with fresh full-strength ClearSee solution and continue incubation with gentle rotation until worms appear optically transparent (typically 1–3 additional days; check daily under a stereomicroscope). (Temperature: RT, Time: 24–72 hours)
3.3 Verify clearing completeness: worms should appear uniformly transparent with no visible granular autofluorescence under white-light illumination. If residual opacity remains, replace ClearSee and extend incubation by 24 hours.

4 Post-clearing Wash
4.1 Wash cleared worms 2× with 1× PBS to remove excess ClearSee reagents before RI matching. (Temperature: RT, Time: 10 min per wash)

5 Refractive Index Matching
5.1 Incubate worms in 50% (vol/vol) ClearSee in 1× PBS as a graded RI step to avoid osmotic shock during transition to the final RI-matching medium. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 min)
5.2 Transfer worms to pure ClearSee solution (RI ≈ 1.44) as the final RI-matching medium for imaging. Ensure worms are fully submerged. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)

6 Sample Mounting for 3D Imaging
6.1 Prepare a #1.5 glass-bottom dish or a custom imaging chamber. Apply a thin layer of 1% (wt/vol) low-melting-point agarose (prepared in ClearSee solution, cooled to ~35 °C) to the imaging surface to immobilize worms without compression. (Temperature: 35 °C agarose application, then RT for gelation, Time: 5 min for gelation)
6.2 Place cleared worms in the liquid agarose droplet and orient them in the desired imaging plane (lateral or dorsal view for nerve ring visualization) using a fine tungsten needle before gelation. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2–3 min)

**Chosen Method:** Ce3D

**Chosen Labeling:** [Phalloidin (Alexa Fluor 488-conjugated), Myosin VIIa + Alexa Fluor, DAPI]

**Justification:** Ce3D (Clearing-Enhanced 3D) is an aqueous-based, detergent-free clearing method optimized for whole-mount immunofluorescence on small specimens. It is particularly well-suited for 5 dpf zebrafish larvae (~4 mm) because: (1) it preserves antigenicity and fluorescence signal through the entire protocol, enabling post-clearing immunolabeling; (2) it achieves excellent RI matching (~1.49) compatible with confocal and light-sheet microscopy; (3) the mild aqueous chemistry is compatible with Phalloidin (which requires intact F-actin and is incompatible with organic-solvent-based methods such as iDISCO+/uDISCO); (4) the small tissue size clears rapidly and completely. Labeling strategy: **Phalloidin–Alexa Fluor 488** directly labels F-actin/stereocilia bundles at hair cell apices (priority probe per instructions); **anti-Myosin VIIa** (secondary: Alexa Fluor 568) confirms hair cell identity (Myosin VIIa is the canonical inner/lateral-line hair cell marker expressed throughout the cell body); **DAPI** provides nuclear counterstain for neuromast cytoarchitecture and cell counting. This three-channel combination allows simultaneous visualization of hair cell position/number/arrangement (Myosin VIIa), stereocilia bundle morphology (Phalloidin), and overall cellular organization (DAPI) across the entire larval body.

---

**Protocol Steps:**

**1 Pre-clearing Permeabilization and Blocking**

1.1 Wash fixed 5 dpf zebrafish larvae (stored in 1× PBS after post-fixation) with 1× PBS containing 0.1% (vol/vol) Tween-20 (PBST). (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 × 10 min)

1.2 Permeabilize with 1× PBS containing 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 and 0.1% (wt/vol) saponin (PBTX-S). (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)

1.3 Block with Ce3D blocking buffer: 1× PBS containing 10% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum (NDS), 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100, 0.1% (wt/vol) saponin, and 0.5% (wt/vol) bovine serum albumin (BSA). (Temperature: RT, Time: 4 hours)

---

**2 Primary Antibody Labeling (Myosin VIIa)**

2.1 Incubate with rabbit anti-Myosin VIIa primary antibody (1:200 dilution in Ce3D blocking buffer). (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours)

2.2 Wash with PBST (1× PBS + 0.1% Tween-20). (Temperature: RT, Time: 5 × 30 min)

---

**3 Secondary Antibody Labeling (Alexa Fluor 568)**

3.1 Incubate with donkey anti-rabbit Alexa Fluor 568 secondary antibody (1:500 dilution in Ce3D blocking buffer). (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours, protected from light)

3.2 Wash with PBST. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 × 30 min)

---

**4 Phalloidin Labeling (F-actin / Stereocilia Bundles)**

4.1 Incubate with Phalloidin–Alexa Fluor 488 (1:40 dilution from stock, e.g., Thermo Fisher A12379, in 1× PBS + 0.1% Triton X-100). (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours, protected from light)

4.2 Wash with PBST. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 × 20 min)

---

**5 Nuclear Counterstain (DAPI)**

5.1 Incubate with DAPI (1 µg/mL in 1× PBS). (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours, protected from light)

5.2 Wash with 1× PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 × 15 min)

---

**6 Tissue Optical Clearing (Ce3D)**

6.1 Prepare Ce3D clearing solution: 40% (wt/vol) N-methylacetamide (NMA), 20% (vol/vol) Histodenz (Sigma D2158), 0.1% (vol/vol) Triton X-100, and 0.5% (vol/vol) 1-thioglycerol in 1× PBS (RI ≈ 1.49). Filter through 0.22 µm membrane before use.

6.2 Transfer labeled larvae into 500 µL Ce3D clearing solution in 1.5 mL microtubes. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours, gentle rotation, protected from light)

6.3 Replace with fresh Ce3D clearing solution and continue incubation until larvae are fully transparent (visually confirmed). (Temperature: RT, Time: 24–48 hours, gentle rotation, protected from light)

---

**7 Refractive Index Matching and Mounting**

7.1 Transfer cleared larvae into fresh Ce3D solution (same formulation as step 6.1) in a glass-bottom imaging dish or custom imaging chamber. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours equilibration, protected from light)

7.2 Orient larvae in the desired imaging plane (lateral or dorsal) using low-melting agarose (1% in Ce3D solution) or custom spacers to immobilize the specimen.

7.3 Seal the imaging chamber with a coverslip and apply a thin layer of Ce3D solution to fill any air gaps. Confirm RI of mounting medium with a refractometer (target: 1.49 ± 0.01).

---

**8 Storage Prior to Imaging**

8.1 Store mounted samples in Ce3D solution in sealed, light-protected containers at 4 ℃ until imaging. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: up to 7 days; image as soon as possible for optimal Phalloidin signal)

8.2 Allow samples to equilibrate to RT for 30 min before confocal or light-sheet imaging. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 min)

**Chosen Method:** FDISCO
**Chosen Labeling:** [Phalloidin (Alexa Fluor 546 or similar far-red conjugate), Myosin VIIa + Alexa Fluor, DAPI]

**Justification:**
FDISCO (Fast Solvent-based Clearing with fluorescence preservation) is selected because: (1) 5 dpf zebrafish larvae (~4 mm) are small, thin specimens that clear rapidly with solvent-based methods; (2) FDISCO uses a tetrahydrofuran (THF)/dibenzyl ether (DBE) pipeline at low temperature (4 °C), which dramatically reduces fluorophore quenching compared to room-temperature solvent methods such as standard iDISCO+/uDISCO, preserving both small-molecule dyes (Phalloidin) and antibody-based signals; (3) the high final RI (~1.56 with DBE) provides excellent transparency for confocal or light-sheet imaging of the entire larval body. Phalloidin is retained as the direct F-actin label for stereocilia bundles (small-molecule penetration is sufficient in 4 mm larvae after mild permeabilization). Myosin VIIa antibody is chosen as the gold-standard hair-cell identity marker (labels all lateral-line neuromast hair cells in zebrafish). DAPI provides nuclear counterstain for neuromast architecture. All three labels are applied before clearing (post-fixation immunostaining), which is compatible with FDISCO's solvent pipeline.

---

**Protocol Steps:**

**1 Post-fixation Wash**
1.1 Wash fixed larvae (4% PFA in PBS, already fixed) 3 × in 1× PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 10 min each wash)

**2 Permeabilization & Blocking**
2.1 Incubate in permeabilization buffer: 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100, 0.1% (wt/vol) saponin, 5% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum (NDS), 1% (wt/vol) BSA in 1× PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)

**3 Primary Antibody Labeling (Myosin VIIa – Hair Cell Identity)**
3.1 Incubate with anti-Myosin VIIa primary antibody (rabbit polyclonal, e.g., Proteus 25-6790, 1:200 dilution) in antibody diluent buffer (0.2% Triton X-100, 5% NDS, 1% BSA in 1× PBS). (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 48 hours)
3.2 Wash 3 × in PBS + 0.2% Triton X-100 (PTx). (Temperature: RT, Time: 20 min each wash)

**4 Secondary Antibody Labeling**
4.1 Incubate with donkey anti-rabbit Alexa Fluor 647 secondary antibody (1:500 dilution) in antibody diluent buffer (0.2% Triton X-100, 5% NDS, 1% BSA in 1× PBS). (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 24 hours)
4.2 Wash 3 × in PTx. (Temperature: RT, Time: 20 min each wash)

**5 Phalloidin Labeling (F-actin / Stereocilia Bundles)**
5.1 Incubate with Phalloidin–Alexa Fluor 546 (or Phalloidin–Alexa Fluor 488; use a spectrally distinct channel from secondary antibody; 1:40 dilution from stock, e.g., Thermo A22283) in 1× PBS + 0.1% Triton X-100. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours, protected from light)
5.2 Wash 3 × in 1× PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 10 min each wash)

**6 Nuclear Counterstain (DAPI)**
6.1 Incubate with DAPI (1 µg/mL in 1× PBS). (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour, protected from light)
6.2 Wash 3 × in 1× PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 10 min each wash)

**7 Post-labeling Fixation (Stabilization before Solvent Clearing)**
7.1 Re-fix labeled larvae in 4% PFA in 1× PBS to stabilize fluorophore–target conjugates before solvent exposure. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
7.2 Wash 3 × in 1× PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 10 min each wash)

**8 Dehydration (FDISCO – THF Series, chilled)**
8.1 Incubate in 50% (vol/vol) tetrahydrofuran (THF, anhydrous, stabilizer-free, Sigma 401757) in ddH₂O. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 1 hour, on gentle shaker, protected from light)
8.2 Incubate in 70% (vol/vol) THF in ddH₂O. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 1 hour)
8.3 Incubate in 80% (vol/vol) THF in ddH₂O. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 1 hour)
8.4 Incubate in 100% THF (anhydrous). (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 1 hour)
8.5 Incubate in fresh 100% THF (anhydrous), second change. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 1 hour)

**9 Delipidation & Clearing (Dichloromethane)**
9.1 Incubate in 100% dichloromethane (DCM, Sigma 270997) to remove residual lipids and complete dehydration. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 30 min, in fume hood)
9.2 Replace with fresh 100% DCM. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 30 min)

**10 Refractive Index Matching (Dibenzyl Ether)**
10.1 Transfer larvae into 100% dibenzyl ether (DBE, Sigma 108014, RI ≈ 1.562) in a glass vial. Ensure complete submersion. Samples will become fully transparent within minutes. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 2–4 hours, protected from light)
10.2 Replace with fresh 100% DBE and confirm full transparency of the 4 mm larval body. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 1 hour)

**11 Sample Mounting & Imaging Preparation**
11.1 Mount cleared larvae in fresh DBE in a glass-bottom imaging dish or between two coverslips sealed with silicone grease; use DBE as immersion/mounting medium (RI ≈ 1.56). Ensure larvae are oriented laterally (for head and trunk neuromast access) or dorsally as needed. (Temperature: 4 °C or RT, Time: immediate use preferred)
11.2 Image on confocal (oil-immersion objective, RI 1.515–1.56 compatible) or light-sheet microscope equipped with a DBE-compatible chamber. Acquire z-stacks spanning the full dorsoventral extent of each neuromast (~20–40 µm per neuromast) for stereocilia bundle orientation analysis. (Temperature: RT, Time: as required per imaging session)

**12 Storage (if imaging is delayed)**
12.1 Store cleared larvae in sealed glass vials in 100% DBE, wrapped in aluminum foil to protect from light. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: up to 2 weeks; note that Phalloidin signal may gradually diminish beyond 1 week)

**Chosen Method:** iDISCO+
**Chosen Labeling:** [Phalloidin (Alexa Fluor 647-conjugated), β-III Tubulin (TUJ1) + Alexa Fluor, DAPI]

**Justification:** iDISCO+ is selected because: (1) it achieves excellent whole-mount clearing of small aqueous samples (4 mm zebrafish larvae) with high optical transparency via organic solvent-based delipidation and RI matching with DBE; (2) its methanol dehydration/delipidation series is well-tolerated by 5 dpf zebrafish and preserves antigenicity for immunolabeling; (3) the protocol supports deep antibody penetration into intact small specimens via organic solvent pretreatment; (4) Phalloidin-Alexa Fluor 647 directly labels F-actin in hair cell stereociliary bundles (apical cuticular plate) as a structural probe without requiring transgenic lines; (5) anti-β-III Tubulin (TUJ1) antibody labels lateral line afferent nerve fibers and neuromasts innervation, enabling 3D spatial analysis of nerve-hair cell relationships; (6) DAPI provides nuclear counterstain for neuromast cytoarchitecture reference. This combination covers all three scientific objectives: hair cell position, apical F-actin/stereocilia structure, and lateral line nerve fiber innervation topology.

**1 Pre-clearing Wash**
1.1 Wash fixed 5 dpf zebrafish larvae (whole body, ~4 mm) in 1× PBS with 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (PTx0.2). (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 × 10 min)

2.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

**3 Bleaching (Pigment Removal)**

**4 Methanol Rehydration**
4.1 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in H₂O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
4.2 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in H₂O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
4.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in H₂O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
4.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in H₂O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
4.5 Incubation with 1× PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

**5 Permeabilization and Blocking**
5.1 Wash with PTx0.2 (1× PBS + 0.2% Triton X-100). (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 × 30 min)
5.2 Incubation with Permeabilization Solution: 1× PBS + 0.2% Triton X-100 + 20% DMSO + 0.3 M glycine. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)
5.3 Incubation with Blocking Solution: 1× PBS + 0.2% Tween-20 + 10% DMSO + 6% normal donkey serum (NDS) + 0.1% heparin (PTwH/DMSO/NDS). (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)

**6 Primary Antibody Labeling (TUJ1 for Lateral Line Nerve Fibers)**
6.1 Incubation with anti-β-III Tubulin (TUJ1) primary antibody (1:500 dilution in PTwH + 5% DMSO + 3% NDS; PTwH: 1× PBS + 0.2% Tween-20 + 0.1% heparin). (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 48 hours, with gentle shaking)
6.2 Wash with PTwH. (Temperature: RT, Time: 5 × 1 hour)

**7 Secondary Antibody Labeling**
7.1 Incubation with Alexa Fluor 555-conjugated donkey anti-mouse IgG secondary antibody (1:500 dilution in PTwH + 3% NDS), targeting TUJ1 primary antibody. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours, in dark, with gentle shaking)
7.2 Wash with PTwH. (Temperature: RT, Time: 5 × 1 hour)

**8 Phalloidin Labeling (Hair Cell F-actin / Stereocilia)**
8.1 Incubation with Alexa Fluor 647-conjugated Phalloidin (1:50 dilution from stock in PTwH + 1% BSA; final concentration ~165 nM). (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours, in dark, with gentle shaking)
8.2 Wash with PTwH. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 × 30 min)

**9 Nuclear Counterstain (DAPI)**
9.1 Incubation with DAPI (1 µg/mL in 1× PBS). (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours, in dark)
9.2 Wash with 1× PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 × 15 min)

**10 Methanol Dehydration (Pre-clearing)**
10.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in H₂O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
10.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in H₂O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
10.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in H₂O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
10.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in H₂O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
10.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
10.6 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol (second change). (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

**11 Delipidation with DCM**
11.1 Incubation with 33% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) in methanol. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours)
11.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DCM. (Temperature: RT, Time: 15 min)
11.3 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DCM (second change). (Temperature: RT, Time: 15 min)

**12 Refractive Index Matching with DBE**
12.1 Remove DCM completely and immediately transfer sample to 100% (vol/vol) dibenzyl ether (DBE, Sigma 108014) without shaking. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours, in dark)
12.2 Replace with fresh 100% (vol/vol) DBE and incubate until sample is fully transparent (typically overnight). (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours, in dark)

**13 Storage and Imaging Preparation**
13.1 Store cleared samples in 100% DBE in sealed glass vials wrapped in aluminum foil until imaging. (Temperature: RT, Time: up to 4 weeks, in dark)
13.2 Mount sample in a glass-bottom imaging chamber or custom agarose mold filled with 100% DBE for light-sheet or confocal imaging. Use DBE-compatible immersion objective (RI = 1.56). (Temperature: RT)
13.3 Acquire 3D z-stack images using: Channel 1 – DAPI (405 nm excitation) for nuclear reference; Channel 2 – Alexa Fluor 555 / TUJ1 (555 nm excitation) for lateral line nerve fibers; Channel 3 – Alexa Fluor 647 / Phalloidin (647 nm excitation) for hair cell F-actin and stereocilia bundles. Step size: 1–2 µm for full-body lateral line survey; 0.3–0.5 µm for high-resolution neuromast z-stacks. (Temperature: RT)

**Chosen Method:** ScaleS (修正版梯度方案，替换原有的 ScaleS0→ScaleS4 两步跳跃方案)

**Chosen Labeling:** [GFP (内源性转基因，用于毛细胞身份标记), Phalloidin (Alexa Fluor 标记，用于 F-actin/静纤毛束结构), DAPI (细胞核复染)]

**Justification:**
ScaleS 是一种基于山梨醇/尿素的水性透明化方法，专为保留荧光蛋白信号和维持组织形态而设计，膨胀系数极低（线性膨胀 <5%），非常适合 4 mm 量级的完整斑马鱼幼鱼。原方案直接从 ScaleS0 跳至 ScaleS4 导致渗透压骤变（山梨醇浓度从 0% 跳至 40%），引发组织膨胀和荧光淬灭。修正方案引入 ScaleS1→ScaleS2→ScaleS3 梯度过渡步骤，使渗透压和折射率逐步升高，从而抑制形变并保护荧光。标记策略：① 利用 Tg(myo6b:GFP) 或 Tg(atoh1a:GFP) 等内源性 GFP 转基因系标记毛细胞身份，无需额外抗体孵育，避免透明化前抗体渗透不均问题；② 透明化前在渗透化步骤后进行 Phalloidin-Alexa Fluor 488/568 染色，直接标记 F-actin/静纤毛束；③ DAPI 用于神经丘细胞核计数和空间定位。三者组合可同时满足毛细胞数量、排列、感觉束完整性和发育状态的三维分析需求，适合共聚焦或光片显微镜成像。

---

**Protocol Steps:**

**1 样本预处理与渗透化（透明化前标记准备）**

1.1 将已完成 4% PFA 固定及后固定的完整 5 dpf 斑马鱼幼鱼用 1× PBS 洗涤。(Temperature: RT, Time: 3 × 10 min)

1.2 用 0.5% Triton X-100 in 1× PBS（PBST）对样本进行渗透化处理，轻摇。(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)

1.3 用 1× PBS 洗涤样本。(Temperature: RT, Time: 3 × 10 min)

**2 Phalloidin F-actin 染色**

2.1 配制 Phalloidin-Alexa Fluor 568（或 Alexa Fluor 488，根据 GFP 通道选择非重叠波长；推荐 568 nm）工作液：1:40 稀释于 0.1% PBST（含 1% BSA）中（终浓度约 5 U/mL）。(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 16–18 hours)

2.2 用 0.1% PBST 洗涤样本，轻摇。(Temperature: RT, Time: 3 × 20 min)

**3 DAPI 核染色**

3.1 用 DAPI 工作液（1 μg/mL in 1× PBS）孵育样本，轻摇。(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

3.2 用 1× PBS 洗涤样本。(Temperature: RT, Time: 3 × 10 min)

**4 ScaleS 梯度透明化——第一步：ScaleS0 平衡**

4.1 将样本转入 ScaleS0 溶液（0% 山梨醇、0.2% Triton X-100、10% 甘油、4 M 尿素 in ddH₂O，RI ≈ 1.38），轻摇。(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)

**5 ScaleS 梯度透明化——第二步：ScaleS1 过渡**

5.1 将样本转入 ScaleS1 溶液（10% 山梨醇、0.2% Triton X-100、10% 甘油、4 M 尿素 in ddH₂O，RI ≈ 1.40），轻摇。(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)

**6 ScaleS 梯度透明化——第三步：ScaleS2 过渡**

6.1 将样本转入 ScaleS2 溶液（20% 山梨醇、0.2% Triton X-100、10% 甘油、4 M 尿素 in ddH₂O，RI ≈ 1.42），轻摇。(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)

**7 ScaleS 梯度透明化——第四步：ScaleS3 过渡**

7.1 将样本转入 ScaleS3 溶液（30% 山梨醇、0.2% Triton X-100、10% 甘油、4 M 尿素 in ddH₂O，RI ≈ 1.44），轻摇。(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)

**8 ScaleS 梯度透明化——第五步：ScaleS4 终透明化**

8.1 将样本转入 ScaleS4 溶液（40% 山梨醇、0.2% Triton X-100、10% 甘油、4 M 尿素 in ddH₂O，RI ≈ 1.46），轻摇。(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 24 hours)

8.2 更换新鲜 ScaleS4 溶液，继续孵育至样本充分透明（幼鱼体壁呈半透明至透明状）。(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 24 hours)

**9 折射率匹配（RI Matching）**

9.1 将透明后样本转入 ScaleS4 溶液（同上，RI ≈ 1.46）作为短期 RI 匹配介质，确认透明度。(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

9.2 若使用光片显微镜（LSFM）成像，将样本转入 ScaleCUBIC-R（或等效 RI = 1.46–1.48 的水性 RI 匹配液，如 80% 2,2'-硫代二乙醇 TDE in PBS，RI ≈ 1.46）进行最终 RI 匹配，轻摇。(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)

9.3 若使用共聚焦显微镜成像，可直接在 ScaleS4 溶液中成像，使用水浸或甘油浸物镜（NA ≥ 0.8，工作距离 ≥ 2 mm）。(Temperature: RT, Time: —)

**10 样本封片与保存**

10.1 将样本置于玻底培养皿或定制成像腔室中，加入足量 ScaleS4 或 TDE RI 匹配液，用低熔点琼脂糖（1% in ScaleS4，45 ℃ 灌注后冷却固定）包埋固定样本方向，避免样本漂移。(Temperature: RT, Time: 凝固约 10 min)

model_response:
**Chosen Method:** ClearSee
**Chosen Labeling:** [GFP, YFP, SCRI Renaissance 2200]

**Justification:** ClearSee is specifically developed for plant tissue optical clearing and is the gold-standard aqueous-based method for intact Arabidopsis seedlings. It uses a xylitol/urea/sodium deoxycholate solution that effectively removes chlorophyll autofluorescence (a major obstacle in plant imaging) and reduces refractive index heterogeneity across cell walls, vascular tissue, and aerial organs—without requiring organic solvents or harsh delipidation steps that would destroy GFP/YFP fluorescence. Critically, ClearSee is fully compatible with endogenous GFP and YFP signals, preserving them for direct observation across the entire seedling (primary root, lateral roots, root tips, vasculature, hypocotyl, and shoot). SCRI Renaissance 2200 (SR2200) is a cell wall–binding fluorescent brightener that labels callose and cellulose in plant cell walls with bright blue fluorescence (excitation ~360 nm, emission ~440 nm), spectrally well-separated from GFP (em ~510 nm) and YFP (em ~527 nm), enabling simultaneous three-channel imaging to co-register fluorescent reporter expression with cell-layer and tissue-boundary information. No antibodies are needed. The combination of ClearSee + SR2200 + endogenous GFP/YFP is the most validated, minimally invasive strategy for whole Arabidopsis seedling 3D imaging.

---

**Protocol Steps:**

**1 Pre-clearing Wash**
1.1 Remove fixative by washing fixed seedlings (15–20 mm intact seedlings, post-fixed in 4% PFA/PBS) with 1× PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 × 10 minutes)

**2 Chlorophyll Removal Pre-treatment (Ethanol Series)**
2.1 Incubation with 30% (vol/vol) ethanol in distilled water to begin chlorophyll extraction. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
2.2 Incubation with 50% (vol/vol) ethanol in distilled water. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
2.3 Incubation with 70% (vol/vol) ethanol in distilled water. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
2.4 Incubation with 100% ethanol to complete chlorophyll removal. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 × 1 hour)
2.5 Rehydration: incubation with 70% (vol/vol) ethanol in distilled water. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)
2.6 Rehydration: incubation with 50% (vol/vol) ethanol in distilled water. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)
2.7 Rehydration: incubation with 30% (vol/vol) ethanol in distilled water. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)
2.8 Rehydration: incubation with distilled water. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 × 15 minutes)

**3 SCRI Renaissance 2200 (SR2200) Cell Wall Staining**
3.1 Prepare SR2200 working solution: dilute SR2200 stock to 0.1% (vol/vol) in 1× PBS. Protect from light throughout all staining steps.
3.2 Incubation of rehydrated seedlings in 0.1% (vol/vol) SR2200 / 1× PBS solution with gentle agitation. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)
3.3 Wash excess SR2200 with 1× PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 × 10 minutes)

**4 ClearSee Clearing**
4.1 Prepare ClearSee solution: dissolve xylitol 10% (wt/vol), urea 15% (wt/vol), and sodium deoxycholate 25% (wt/vol) in distilled water; stir until fully dissolved; filter through 0.22 µm membrane; store at RT protected from light.
4.2 Transfer SR2200-stained seedlings into ClearSee solution in 1.5 mL microtubes (ensure seedlings are fully submerged). (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours, gentle agitation on orbital shaker, protected from light)
4.3 Replace ClearSee solution with fresh ClearSee. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours, gentle agitation, protected from light)
4.4 Assess clearing: tissue should appear translucent/transparent with no visible green chlorophyll coloration. If residual pigmentation remains, continue incubation in fresh ClearSee. (Temperature: RT, Time: up to additional 24 hours)

**5 Post-clearing Wash and RI Equilibration**
5.1 Wash cleared seedlings briefly with 1× PBS to remove residual detergent before RI matching. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 × 5 minutes)

**6 Refractive Index Matching**
6.1 Prepare ClearSee RI-matching medium: use the same ClearSee solution (RI ≈ 1.44) as the imaging medium, or alternatively prepare 50% (vol/vol) glycerol in PBS (RI ≈ 1.41) for confocal imaging with water/glycerol objectives.
6.2 Transfer cleared seedlings into ClearSee imaging medium in a glass-bottom dish or imaging chamber. Allow equilibration. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)
6.3 For light-sheet microscopy: embed seedlings in 1% (wt/vol) low-melting-point agarose prepared in ClearSee solution; mount in imaging capillary or chamber filled with ClearSee as immersion medium. (Temperature: RT, Time: allow agarose to solidify ~5 minutes at RT after brief cooling)

**7 Sample Storage Prior to Imaging**
7.1 If imaging is not immediate, store cleared seedlings in ClearSee solution in sealed microtubes protected from light. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: up to 2 weeks; note: prolonged storage may cause gradual GFP/YFP signal reduction—image within 3–5 days for optimal signal)

**8 Imaging Parameters (Reference)**
8.1 Channel 1 – SR2200 cell wall: excitation 405 nm (UV/violet laser), emission 420–480 nm (blue channel); use 20× or 40× water/glycerol immersion objective.
8.2 Channel 2 – GFP endogenous fluorescence: excitation 488 nm, emission 500–540 nm (green channel); acquire z-stack spanning full root depth (primary root, lateral roots, root tips, vasculature) and aerial organs.
8.3 Channel 3 – YFP endogenous fluorescence (if spectrally distinct from GFP in the experimental line): excitation 514 nm, emission 520–560 nm (yellow-green channel); apply linear unmixing if GFP and YFP are co-expressed.
8.4 Acquire full-seedling tile-scan z-stacks at 1–2 µm z-step intervals for 3D reconstruction of expression domains across all organs.

**Chosen Method:** ClearSee
**Chosen Labeling:** [GFP, YFP, SCRI Renaissance 2200]

**Justification:** ClearSee is specifically designed for plant tissue optical clearing and is the gold-standard aqueous-based method for *Arabidopsis* and other plant specimens. It uses a xylitol/urea/sodium deoxycholate solution that effectively clears plant cell walls and chlorophyll autofluorescence while preserving GFP/YFP fluorescent protein signals—a critical requirement here. Unlike solvent-based methods (iDISCO+, uDISCO, FDISCO), ClearSee does not quench or denature GFP/YFP. SCRI Renaissance 2200 (SR2200) is a cell wall–binding fluorescent brightener (excitation ~360 nm, emission ~460 nm) that labels callose and cellulose in plant cell walls with high specificity, providing clear delineation of cell outlines, tissue layers, root tip zones, lateral root primordia, and vascular boundaries—exactly the structural context required. SR2200 is fully compatible with ClearSee and GFP/YFP in multi-channel confocal imaging. No antibodies are needed because the endogenous GFP/YFP reporter signal and the chemical cell wall dye together fully satisfy the scientific objectives.

---

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Post-fixation Verification and Pre-clearing Wash
1.1 Rinse fixed whole seedlings (15–20 mm) 3× with 1× PBS (pH 7.4). (Temperature: RT, Time: 5 min each wash)
1.2 Transfer seedlings to 1.5 mL microtubes. Ensure samples are fully submerged in all subsequent solutions. (Temperature: RT, Time: N/A)

2 Cell Wall Staining with SCRI Renaissance 2200 (SR2200)
2.1 Prepare SR2200 working solution: 0.1% (wt/vol) SR2200 dissolved in 1× PBS (pH 7.4). Protect from light.
2.2 Incubate seedlings in SR2200 working solution with gentle agitation on a rotary shaker. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)
2.3 Wash seedlings 3× with 1× PBS (pH 7.4) to remove excess SR2200. (Temperature: RT, Time: 10 min each wash)

3 ClearSee Optical Clearing
3.1 Prepare ClearSee solution: 10% (wt/vol) xylitol, 15% (wt/vol) sodium deoxycholate, 25% (wt/vol) urea in distilled water. Dissolve completely at 37 °C with stirring, then cool to RT before use.
3.2 Transfer stained seedlings into ClearSee solution (sufficient volume to fully submerge, ~500 µL per tube). Protect from light with aluminum foil. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)
3.3 Replace ClearSee solution with fresh ClearSee solution. Continue incubation with gentle agitation. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)
3.4 Inspect clearing progress: roots and shoot tissue should appear translucent/transparent with loss of green chlorophyll color. If residual opacity remains, replace with fresh ClearSee and continue. (Temperature: RT, Time: up to 24 additional hours)

4 Post-clearing Wash and RI Equilibration
4.1 Wash cleared seedlings 2× with fresh ClearSee solution to remove any precipitates. (Temperature: RT, Time: 10 min each wash)
4.2 Transfer seedlings into ClearSee solution for final RI equilibration (RI ≈ 1.44, matching ClearSee). Protect from light. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)

5 Sample Mounting for Confocal Imaging
5.1 Place a small volume (~100–150 µL) of ClearSee solution onto a #1.5 glass-bottom dish or coverslip-bottomed chamber.
5.2 Orient cleared seedlings in ClearSee solution using fine forceps. For root imaging, orient roots parallel to the coverslip surface. For shoot imaging, adjust orientation accordingly.
5.3 Carefully place a #1.5 coverslip over the sample, avoiding air bubbles. Seal edges with clear nail varnish or silicone grease to prevent evaporation and maintain RI matching. (Temperature: RT, Time: allow sealant to set ~5 min before imaging)
5.4 Store mounted samples protected from light at 4 °C if imaging is not performed immediately. Samples are stable for up to 1 week under these conditions. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: up to 7 days)

6 Confocal Imaging Parameters (Reference)
6.1 Image SR2200 cell wall signal using 405 nm laser excitation, emission collected at 425–475 nm (blue channel). (Temperature: RT, Time: per imaging session)
6.2 Image GFP/YFP reporter signal using 488 nm laser excitation, emission collected at 505–540 nm (green channel). (Temperature: RT, Time: per imaging session)
6.3 Acquire z-stacks with 1–2 µm step size for root tip zone analysis and lateral root primordia; use 3–5 µm steps for full seedling overview scans. Adjust laser power and gain to avoid photobleaching during long acquisitions. (Temperature: RT, Time: per imaging session)

**Chosen Method:** ClearSee
**Chosen Labeling:** [GFP (内源), YFP (内源), SCRI Renaissance 2200]

**Justification:** ClearSee is specifically designed for plant tissue optical clearing and is the gold-standard aqueous clearing method for whole Arabidopsis seedlings. It preserves GFP/YFP endogenous fluorescence exceptionally well (unlike solvent-based methods such as iDISCO+ or uDISCO which quench GFP), achieves high transparency in complete seedlings (15–20 mm) within days, and is fully compatible with SCRI Renaissance 2200 (SR2200), a cell wall–binding fluorescent brightener that labels callose and cellulose in all plant cell wall types. SR2200 can be applied directly during or after ClearSee treatment without additional antibody steps, providing a bright, spectrally distinct cell wall channel (excitation ~355 nm, emission ~400 nm) that is orthogonal to GFP/YFP channels. This combination allows simultaneous 3D mapping of transgene expression (GFP/YFP) and cell wall architecture (SR2200) throughout deep root tissues, hypocotyl, and shoot in a single imaging session on a confocal or light-sheet microscope.

---

**Protocol Steps:**

**1 Post-fixation Wash**
1.1 Remove fixative (1× PBS wash): Incubate fixed whole seedlings in 1× PBS (phosphate-buffered saline, pH 7.4). (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 × 10 minutes)

**2 Cell Wall Staining with SCRI Renaissance 2200 (SR2200)**
2.1 Prepare SR2200 working solution: Dilute SR2200 stock (1 mg/mL in DMSO) to 0.1% (vol/vol) in 1× PBS containing 0.1% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (PBST).
2.2 Incubate whole seedlings in SR2200 working solution (0.1% SR2200 in PBST) with gentle agitation on a rotary shaker. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)
2.3 Wash seedlings in 1× PBST (0.1% Triton X-100 in PBS) to remove excess SR2200. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 × 15 minutes)

**3 ClearSee Clearing Solution Preparation**
3.1 Prepare ClearSee solution: Dissolve xylitol (10% wt/vol), sodium deoxycholate (15% wt/vol), and urea (25% wt/vol) in ultrapure water. Stir at 37 °C until fully dissolved. Store at RT protected from light.

**4 Tissue Clearing with ClearSee**
4.1 Transfer SR2200-stained, washed seedlings directly into ClearSee solution in 1.5 mL microtubes or glass vials. Ensure seedlings are fully submerged. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours, gentle agitation)
4.2 Replace ClearSee solution with fresh ClearSee solution. Continue incubation with gentle agitation until seedlings become fully transparent (typically 3–7 days total; 15–20 mm seedlings typically require 5–7 days). (Temperature: RT, Time: 4–6 days, change solution every 2 days)
4.3 Monitor clearing progress visually. Seedlings are ready when roots and hypocotyl appear optically transparent under white light.

**5 Refractive Index (RI) Matching**
5.1 ClearSee solution itself serves as the RI-matching medium (RI ≈ 1.44). Confirm seedlings remain submerged in fresh ClearSee solution for final RI equilibration. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)

**6 Sample Mounting for Imaging**
6.1 Transfer cleared seedlings into a glass-bottom imaging dish (e.g., 35 mm glass-bottom dish, #1.5 coverslip, 0.17 mm thickness) or a custom imaging chamber suitable for light-sheet or confocal microscopy.
6.2 Orient seedlings in ClearSee mounting medium: pipette sufficient ClearSee solution to fully cover the sample and prevent drying. For confocal imaging, place a coverslip gently on top and seal edges with clear nail varnish to prevent evaporation. (Temperature: RT, Time: 15 minutes equilibration before imaging)
