model_response:
**Chosen Method:** ClearSee (optimized extended protocol)
**Chosen Labeling:** [GFP, YFP, SCRI Renaissance 2200]

**Justification:** ClearSee is the only method in the provided list specifically developed and validated for plant tissues. It is an aqueous-based clearing solution (xylitol + sodium deoxycholate + urea) that effectively removes chlorophyll autofluorescence from Arabidopsis seedlings while preserving endogenous GFP/YFP fluorescence — a critical requirement here. Solvent-based methods (iDISCO+, uDISCO, FDISCO, etc.) would quench GFP/YFP and are incompatible with plant cell wall integrity at this scale. CUBIC and ScaleS are animal-tissue-optimized and lack validated chlorophyll removal for intact seedlings. The original protocol failure (2 days RT, insufficient chlorophyll removal and RI mismatch) is corrected by: (1) adding an ethanol-based chlorophyll pre-extraction step before ClearSee immersion, (2) extending ClearSee incubation to 5–7 days at 4 °C with gentle agitation, and (3) using the ClearSee solution itself (RI ≈ 1.44) as the final RI-matching medium. SCRI Renaissance 2200 (SR2200) is a cell-wall-binding fluorescent brightener compatible with ClearSee and excitable at 405 nm (emission ~450 nm), spectrally well-separated from GFP (488/507 nm) and YFP (514/527 nm), enabling simultaneous three-channel imaging of cell wall architecture, GFP signal, and YFP signal without cross-talk.

---

**Protocol Steps:**

**1 Post-fixation Verification and Pre-wash**
1.1 Rinse fixed whole Arabidopsis seedlings (15–20 mm) 3× with 1× PBS (pH 7.4) to remove residual fixative. (Temperature: RT, Time: 5 min per wash)
1.2 Incubation with 1× PBS containing 0.1% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (PBST) to permeabilize cell membranes and facilitate subsequent reagent penetration. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 min)

**2 Chlorophyll Pre-extraction**
2.1 Incubation with 10% (vol/vol) ethanol in distilled water to begin gradual chlorophyll solubilization while minimizing tissue distortion. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 min, gentle agitation on orbital shaker at 30 rpm)
2.2 Incubation with 30% (vol/vol) ethanol in distilled water. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 min, gentle agitation at 30 rpm)
2.3 Incubation with 50% (vol/vol) ethanol in distilled water. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour, gentle agitation at 30 rpm)
2.4 Incubation with 70% (vol/vol) ethanol in distilled water. Monitor solution color; repeat this step once if solution turns strongly green. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours, gentle agitation at 30 rpm)
2.5 Rehydration: incubation with 50% (vol/vol) ethanol in distilled water. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 min, gentle agitation at 30 rpm)
2.6 Rehydration: incubation with 30% (vol/vol) ethanol in distilled water. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 min, gentle agitation at 30 rpm)
2.7 Rehydration: incubation with 10% (vol/vol) ethanol in distilled water. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 min, gentle agitation at 30 rpm)
2.8 Wash 2× with 1× PBS to fully remove ethanol before staining. (Temperature: RT, Time: 10 min per wash)

**3 SCRI Renaissance 2200 (SR2200) Cell Wall Staining**
3.1 Prepare SR2200 working solution: dilute SR2200 stock to 0.1% (vol/vol) in 1× PBS. Protect from light throughout all staining steps.
3.2 Incubation with SR2200 working solution (0.1% vol/vol in 1× PBS) to label cell walls of root, hypocotyl, shoot, and vascular tissues. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours, gentle agitation at 30 rpm, protected from light)
3.3 Wash 3× with 1× PBS to remove unbound SR2200. (Temperature: RT, Time: 10 min per wash, protected from light)

**4 ClearSee Tissue Clearing**
4.1 Prepare fresh ClearSee solution: dissolve xylitol 10% (wt/vol), sodium deoxycholate 15% (wt/vol), and urea 25% (wt/vol) in distilled water. Stir at 37 °C until fully dissolved, then cool to RT. Final RI ≈ 1.44. Store at 4 °C protected from light.
4.2 Initial ClearSee immersion: transfer stained seedlings into ClearSee solution in 1.5 mL amber microtubes or glass vials. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 24 hours, gentle agitation at 20 rpm on orbital shaker, protected from light)
4.3 Replace ClearSee with fresh ClearSee solution. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 48 hours, gentle agitation at 20 rpm, protected from light)
4.4 Replace ClearSee with fresh ClearSee solution for final clearing. Continue until tissue appears optically transparent and solution shows minimal green coloration (typically 2–4 additional days; total clearing time 5–7 days). (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 48–96 hours, gentle agitation at 20 rpm, protected from light)
4.5 Visual quality check: inspect seedlings under white light transillumination. Root and hypocotyl should appear translucent. If residual green pigmentation persists in shoot/cotyledons, replace with fresh ClearSee and extend incubation by 24 hours at 4 °C.

**5 Refractive Index Matching and Equilibration**
5.1 Transfer cleared seedlings into fresh ClearSee solution in imaging chambers (e.g., #1.5 glass-bottom dishes or custom imaging chambers). ClearSee (RI ≈ 1.44) serves directly as the RI-matching medium, compatible with water-dipping objectives (RI 1.33) and glycerol objectives (RI 1.45). (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 12 hours, static, protected from light)
5.2 For confocal or light-sheet imaging with glycerol-immersion objectives (RI 1.45): supplement ClearSee with 5% (wt/vol) additional xylitol to fine-tune RI to ≈1.45 if needed. Equilibrate samples in adjusted solution. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours, static, protected from light)

**6 Sample Mounting and Imaging Preparation**
6.1 Mount seedlings in ClearSee solution on #1.5 borosilicate glass-bottom dishes. Orient roots vertically or horizontally as required for deep root imaging. Seal edges with silicone grease to prevent evaporation and maintain RI stability.
6.2 Imaging channel configuration: Channel 1 — SR2200 cell wall signal: excitation 405 nm laser, emission 425–475 nm (BP 450/50). Channel 2 — GFP signal: excitation 488 nm laser, emission 500–540 nm (BP 515/30). Channel 3 — YFP signal: excitation 514 nm laser (or 488 nm with spectral unmixing), emission 520–560 nm (BP 535/30). Acquire Z-stacks with step size 1–2 µm for root tip regions and 3–5 µm for hypocotyl/shoot regions.
6.3 For long-term storage prior to imaging: keep mounted samples in ClearSee at 4 °C in the dark. GFP/YFP fluorescence is stable for up to 2 weeks under these conditions. Do not freeze.

model_response:
**Chosen Method:** Ce3D

**Chosen Labeling:** [alpha-bungarotoxin (Alexa Fluor conjugate, for AChR/postsynaptic membrane), Tuj1 (β-III Tubulin, for motor nerve terminals/axons + Alexa Fluor secondary), DAPI (nuclear counterstain)]

**Justification:**
Ce3D (Clearing-Enhanced 3D) is an aqueous-based, detergent-free clearing method using N-methylacetamide and Histodenz that achieves excellent RI matching (~1.52) with minimal tissue distortion and outstanding fluorescence preservation. For dense skeletal muscle (~8 mm × 5 mm × 3 mm), Ce3D is particularly advantageous because: (1) it avoids organic solvents and harsh delipidation that cause muscle fiber shrinkage and synaptic signal loss; (2) it is fully compatible with small-molecule fluorescent conjugates such as fluorophore-conjugated alpha-bungarotoxin (α-BTX), which directly and specifically labels nicotinic AChRs at the postsynaptic membrane without requiring antibody amplification; (3) it preserves immunofluorescence signal from antibody staining (Tuj1/β-III Tubulin for nerve terminals) through the entire tissue depth; (4) the protocol is completed within ~3–4 days, suitable for intact muscle samples of this size. Alpha-bungarotoxin conjugated to Alexa Fluor 555 or 647 is the gold-standard label for NMJ postsynaptic morphology (AChR clustering, fragmentation, area) and is used directly without substitution by an antibody surrogate. Tuj1 is selected from the Marker list to visualize motor axons and nerve terminals for co-localization with AChR plaques.

---

**Protocol Steps:**

**1 Post-fixation Verification and Pre-clearing Wash**

1.1 Confirm sample has been post-fixed in 4% (wt/vol) PFA in PBS. Rinse intact gastrocnemius muscle (≈8 mm × 5 mm × 3 mm) 3× with 1× PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 10 min per wash)

1.2 Incubation in 1× PBS containing 0.1% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (PBST) to permeabilize surface membranes gently. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours, gentle rocking)

**2 Blocking**

2.1 Incubation in blocking buffer: 5% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum (NDS) + 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 + 0.1% (wt/vol) saponin in 1× PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 4 hours, gentle rocking)

**3 Primary Labeling — Alpha-Bungarotoxin (AChR / Postsynaptic Membrane)**

3.1 Incubation with fluorophore-conjugated alpha-bungarotoxin (α-BTX–Alexa Fluor 555, 5 µg/mL) in blocking buffer (5% NDS, 0.5% Triton X-100, 0.1% saponin in PBS). (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours, gentle rocking, protected from light)

3.2 Wash 3× with PBST (0.5% Triton X-100 in PBS). (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 min per wash, gentle rocking)

**4 Primary Antibody Incubation — Tuj1 (β-III Tubulin, Motor Nerve Terminals / Axons)**

4.1 Incubation with anti-β-III Tubulin (Tuj1) primary antibody (rabbit anti-mouse, 1:500 dilution) in antibody diluent buffer (3% NDS + 0.5% Triton X-100 + 0.1% saponin in PBS). (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours, gentle rocking)

4.2 Wash 3× with PBST (0.5% Triton X-100 in PBS). (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 min per wash, gentle rocking)

**5 Secondary Antibody Incubation — Tuj1 Detection**

5.1 Incubation with donkey anti-rabbit Alexa Fluor 647 secondary antibody (1:500 dilution) in antibody diluent buffer (3% NDS + 0.5% Triton X-100 + 0.1% saponin in PBS). (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 24 hours, gentle rocking, protected from light)

5.2 Wash 3× with PBST (0.5% Triton X-100 in PBS). (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 min per wash, gentle rocking)

**6 Nuclear Counterstain — DAPI**

6.1 Incubation with DAPI (1 µg/mL) in 1× PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours, gentle rocking, protected from light)

6.2 Wash 2× with 1× PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 15 min per wash)

**7 Ce3D Clearing Solution Preparation**

7.1 Prepare Ce3D clearing solution: dissolve Histodenz (Sigma D2158) to 86% (wt/vol) in 1× PBS containing 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 and 0.1% (wt/vol) saponin; add N-methylacetamide (NMA) to 40% (vol/vol) final concentration; adjust to pH 7.4. Prepare fresh and filter through 0.22 µm membrane. (Temperature: 37 ℃ water bath to dissolve Histodenz, then cool to RT before use)

**8 Tissue Optical Clearing — Ce3D**

8.1 Incubation in Ce3D clearing solution (50% vol/vol diluted in 1× PBS, i.e., half-strength Ce3D) as a gradual equilibration step. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours, gentle rocking, protected from light)

8.2 Incubation in full-strength Ce3D clearing solution (86% Histodenz, 40% NMA, 0.5% Triton X-100, 0.1% saponin in PBS, RI ≈ 1.49–1.52). (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours, gentle rocking, protected from light)

8.3 Replace with fresh full-strength Ce3D clearing solution and continue incubation until tissue is visually transparent (typically an additional 12–24 hours for this tissue size). (Temperature: RT, Time: 12–24 hours, gentle rocking, protected from light)

**9 Refractive Index Matching and Mounting**

9.1 Transfer cleared muscle to a glass-bottom imaging dish or custom imaging chamber. Remove excess Ce3D solution gently with a pipette without allowing the tissue to dry.

9.2 Immerse sample in fresh full-strength Ce3D solution (RI ≈ 1.52) as the final RI-matching medium for imaging. Ensure tissue is fully submerged and free of air bubbles. (Temperature: RT, Time: equilibrate for 2 hours before imaging)

9.3 Seal the imaging chamber with a coverslip using silicone grease to prevent evaporation and maintain RI stability. (Temperature: RT)

**10 Storage Prior to Imaging**

10.1 If imaging is not performed immediately, store the cleared and mounted sample in full-strength Ce3D solution in a sealed container protected from light. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: up to 7 days; bring to RT for 1 hour before imaging)

**11 Imaging Parameters (Guidance)**

11.1 Image using a light-sheet fluorescence microscope (LSFM) or confocal microscope equipped with an objective compatible with RI ≈ 1.52 immersion medium (e.g., 10× or 25× long-working-distance objective). Acquire z-stacks spanning the full muscle depth. Recommended channels: DAPI (405 nm excitation), α-BTX–Alexa Fluor 555 (561 nm excitation, postsynaptic AChR), Alexa Fluor 647–Tuj1 (638 nm excitation, motor nerve terminals). Step size: 2–5 µm for full-volume survey; 0.5–1 µm for high-resolution NMJ morphology analysis. (Temperature: RT, Time: per experimental requirement)

**Chosen Labeling:** [alpha-bungarotoxin (Alexa Fluor 647-conjugated), β-III Tubulin (TUJ1) + Alexa Fluor, DAPI]

**Justification:**
iDISCO+ is selected for this application because: (1) it achieves excellent clearing of dense skeletal muscle tissue (~8×5×3 mm) through organic solvent-based delipidation, providing high transparency suitable for light-sheet or confocal 3D imaging; (2) it is fully compatible with whole-mount immunolabeling protocols, enabling deep antibody penetration into intact muscle; (3) the methanol-based dehydration and dibenzyl ether (DBE) RI-matching step yield a final RI of ~1.56, well-suited for long-working-distance objectives. For labeling strategy: **alpha-bungarotoxin (α-BTX) conjugated to Alexa Fluor 647** is the gold-standard direct probe for nicotinic AChR clusters at the postsynaptic membrane of NMJs — it binds with extremely high affinity and specificity, making it the primary signal for AChR aggregation, endplate area, fragmentation, and denervation analysis. **Anti-β-III Tubulin (TUJ1)** antibody (secondary: Alexa Fluor 555) labels motor axons and nerve terminals to assess presynaptic coverage and reinnervation. **DAPI** provides nuclear counterstaining for tissue orientation and regional mapping. This dual-channel NMJ labeling strategy directly addresses the co-registration of postsynaptic AChR clusters with presynaptic motor nerve terminals in 3D.

---

**Protocol Steps:**

**1 Pre-treatment and Permeabilization**
1.1 Wash fixed gastrocnemius muscle (post-fixed in 4% PFA/PBS) with 1× PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 × 10 minutes)
1.2 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in distilled water with gentle shaking. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
1.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in distilled water with gentle shaking. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
1.4 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in distilled water with gentle shaking. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
1.5 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in distilled water with gentle shaking. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
1.6 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol with gentle shaking. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
1.7 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol (second change) with gentle shaking. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

**2 Bleaching**
2.1 Incubation with chilled fresh 5% H₂O₂ in 100% methanol (1 volume 30% H₂O₂ : 5 volumes MeOH) to quench autofluorescence. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 16 hours)

**3 Rehydration**
3.1 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in distilled water with gentle shaking. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
3.2 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in distilled water with gentle shaking. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
3.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in distilled water with gentle shaking. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
3.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in distilled water with gentle shaking. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
3.5 Incubation with 1× PBS with gentle shaking. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 × 30 minutes)

**4 Pre-incubation / Blocking**
4.1 Incubation with PTwH buffer (1× PBS + 0.2% Tween-20 + 10 µg/mL heparin) to wash and equilibrate tissue. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 × 30 minutes)
4.2 Incubation with blocking/permeabilization solution: PTwH + 5% (vol/vol) DMSO + 3% (wt/vol) donkey serum + 0.3% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 to block non-specific binding and enhance antibody penetration. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)

**5 Primary Labeling — alpha-Bungarotoxin (AChR postsynaptic marker)**
5.1 Incubation with Alexa Fluor 647-conjugated alpha-bungarotoxin (α-BTX-AF647, 5 µg/mL) diluted in PTwH + 5% DMSO + 3% donkey serum. This directly labels nicotinic AChR clusters at NMJ postsynaptic membranes. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 48 hours)
5.2 Wash with PTwH buffer with gentle shaking. (Temperature: RT, Time: 5 × 1 hour)

**6 Primary Antibody Incubation — Motor Nerve Terminals (TUJ1)**
6.1 Incubation with anti-β-III Tubulin (TUJ1) primary antibody (rabbit monoclonal, 1:500 dilution) in PTwH + 5% DMSO + 3% donkey serum to label motor axons and nerve terminals. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 48 hours)
6.2 Wash with PTwH buffer with gentle shaking. (Temperature: RT, Time: 5 × 1 hour)

**7 Secondary Antibody Incubation**
7.1 Incubation with donkey anti-rabbit Alexa Fluor 555 secondary antibody (1:500 dilution) in PTwH + 3% donkey serum to visualize TUJ1 signal. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)
7.2 Wash with PTwH buffer with gentle shaking. (Temperature: RT, Time: 5 × 1 hour)

**8 Nuclear Counterstaining**
8.1 Incubation with DAPI (1 µg/mL) in 1× PBS for nuclear labeling and tissue orientation. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)
8.2 Wash with 1× PBS with gentle shaking. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 × 30 minutes)

**9 Dehydration (iDISCO+ Clearing — Step 1)**
9.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in distilled water with gentle shaking. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
9.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in distilled water with gentle shaking. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
9.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in distilled water with gentle shaking. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
9.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in distilled water with gentle shaking. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
9.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol with gentle shaking. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
9.6 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol (second change) with gentle shaking. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

**10 Delipidation**
10.1 Incubation with 33% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) in methanol (1 volume DCM : 2 volumes MeOH) with gentle shaking to begin lipid extraction. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours)
10.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DCM (two changes) with gentle shaking for complete delipidation of skeletal muscle. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 × 30 minutes)

**11 Refractive Index Matching**
11.1 Transfer tissue to glass vial. Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dibenzyl ether (DBE, Sigma 108014-1KG) without shaking, until tissue is fully transparent (RI ≈ 1.56). (Temperature: RT, Time: 4–6 hours, or until transparent)
11.2 Replace with fresh 100% DBE and store until imaging. (Temperature: RT, Time: minimum 2 hours before imaging)

**12 Sample Mounting and Imaging Preparation**
12.1 Mount cleared gastrocnemius muscle in a glass-bottom imaging chamber or custom holder filled with 100% DBE. Ensure tissue is fully submerged and oriented with the superficial muscle surface facing the objective for systematic NMJ mapping across muscle regions. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes equilibration)
12.2 Image using light-sheet fluorescence microscopy (LSFM) or confocal microscopy with appropriate objectives (e.g., 10× or 25× long-working-distance, DBE-compatible objective). Acquire three channels: DAPI (405 nm excitation), Alexa Fluor 555/TUJ1 (561 nm excitation), Alexa Fluor 647/α-BTX (638 nm excitation). Tile acquisition recommended to cover full muscle volume for spatial NMJ distribution analysis. (Temperature: RT, Time: per imaging session)

**Chosen Method:** iDISCO+
**Chosen Labeling:** [alpha-bungarotoxin (Alexa Fluor 647-conjugated), β-III Tubulin (TUJ1) + Alexa Fluor, Phalloidin (Alexa Fluor 488-conjugated)]

**Justification:** iDISCO+ is selected because it provides excellent whole-mount immunolabeling penetration through organic solvent-based delipidation, which is critical for a dense, lipid-rich skeletal muscle (~8×5×3 mm). The methanol/DCM/DBE pipeline achieves high transparency and RI matching (n≈1.56) compatible with light-sheet microscopy. Alpha-bungarotoxin (BTX, Alexa Fluor 647) directly and specifically labels nicotinic AChR clusters at the NMJ postsynaptic membrane without requiring antibody penetration into the synapse cleft, making it the primary NMJ marker. Anti-β-III Tubulin (TUJ1) antibody labels motor axons and nerve terminals to visualize presynaptic innervation. Phalloidin-Alexa Fluor 488 labels F-actin in myofibers, providing the structural reference for fiber orientation, terminal band distribution, and local fiber architecture. The three spectrally separated channels (488/secondary mid-range/647) allow simultaneous 3D mapping of postsynaptic AChR, motor axons, and myofiber structure. iDISCO+ is well-validated for skeletal muscle NMJ imaging and preserves both small-molecule (BTX, Phalloidin) and antibody-based signals when the labeling is performed prior to dehydration.

---

**Protocol Steps:**

**0 Pre-clearing Tissue Preparation**

0.1 Confirm tissue is fixed in 4% PFA/PBS. If freshly dissected, immerse intact gastrocnemius muscle in 4% (wt/vol) paraformaldehyde in 0.1 M PBS. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 24 hours)

0.2 Wash fixed tissue with 1× PBS three times to remove residual PFA. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 × 30 minutes)

**1 Pre-labeling Permeabilization and Blocking**

1.1 Incubation with PBS/0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (PTx0.2) to permeabilize tissue. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 × 1 hour)

1.2 Incubation with blocking/permeabilization buffer: PBS containing 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100, 10% (vol/vol) DMSO, 6% (wt/vol) normal donkey serum (NDS), and 0.3 M glycine. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)

**2 Primary Labeling — Alpha-Bungarotoxin (AChR / NMJ Postsynaptic Membrane)**

2.1 Prepare alpha-bungarotoxin conjugated to Alexa Fluor 647 (BTX-AF647, e.g., Thermo Fisher B35450) at 5 µg/mL in PTx0.2 + 5% NDS. Incubate tissue fully submerged with gentle rocking. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours)

2.2 Wash with PTx0.2 to remove unbound BTX-AF647. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 × 1 hour)

**3 Primary Antibody Labeling — β-III Tubulin / TUJ1 (Motor Axons and Nerve Terminals)**

3.1 Incubate tissue with anti-β-III Tubulin (TUJ1) primary antibody (e.g., rabbit anti-TUJ1, Abcam ab18207) at 1:200 dilution in PTwH buffer (PBS + 0.2% Tween-20 + 10 µg/mL heparin) supplemented with 5% NDS and 5% DMSO. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 72 hours)

3.2 Wash with PTwH buffer to remove unbound primary antibody. (Temperature: RT, Time: 5 × 1 hour, then overnight)

**4 Secondary Antibody Labeling — Anti-Rabbit Alexa Fluor 555**

4.1 Incubate tissue with donkey anti-rabbit IgG conjugated to Alexa Fluor 555 (e.g., Thermo Fisher A31572) at 1:500 dilution in PTwH + 5% NDS + 5% DMSO. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 48 hours)

4.2 Wash with PTwH buffer to remove unbound secondary antibody. (Temperature: RT, Time: 5 × 1 hour, then overnight)

**5 Phalloidin Labeling — F-Actin / Myofiber Structure**

5.2 Wash with PTx0.2 to remove unbound Phalloidin. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 × 1 hour)

# Analysis and Protocol Design

## Chosen Method: CUBIC

## Chosen Labeling: [alpha-bungarotoxin (Alexa Fluor conjugated), β-III Tubulin (TUJ1) + Alexa Fluor, DAPI]

## Justification:

**Why CUBIC:**
The core problems identified are (1) severe tissue shrinkage and (2) weak alpha-bungarotoxin (α-BTX) signal. The previous protocol used THF/DBE (a solvent-based/uDISCO-type approach), which is known to cause significant tissue shrinkage (15–30%) in skeletal muscle and can quench or denature fluorescent conjugates on α-BTX. CUBIC (Clear, Unobstructed Brain/Body Imaging Cocktails and Computational analysis) is an **aqueous-based** clearing method that:

- **Minimizes shrinkage/distortion**: Aqueous reagents preserve tissue morphology far better than organic solvents for soft tissues like skeletal muscle (~5–8 mm × 3 mm block), making it ideal for quantitative NMJ morphometry (endplate fragmentation, innervation ratio).
- **Preserves fluorescence**: CUBIC's alkaline/detergent chemistry (CUBIC-1 for delipidation, CUBIC-2 for RI matching) is compatible with Alexa Fluor dyes conjugated to α-BTX and secondary antibodies, unlike THF/DBE which bleaches these fluorophores.
- **Compatible with whole-mount immunolabeling**: The aqueous environment allows post-clearing or pre-clearing antibody labeling with full penetration into an 8 × 5 × 3 mm muscle block using optimized incubation times.
- **Sufficient RI matching**: CUBIC-2 (RI ≈ 1.49–1.52) provides excellent optical clearing for skeletal muscle, compatible with light-sheet and confocal microscopy.

**Why this labeling strategy:**
- **α-Bungarotoxin–Alexa Fluor** (e.g., Alexa Fluor 555 or 647 conjugate): Direct, high-affinity ligand for nicotinic AChRs at the postsynaptic membrane. Applied **before** clearing (post-fixation, pre-delipidation) to maximize signal intensity and receptor occupancy. The previous protocol's failure was likely due to insufficient incubation time (1 day may be inadequate for whole intact muscle) and fluorophore destruction by THF/DBE.
- **β-III Tubulin (TUJ1) + Alexa Fluor**: Labels axonal/nerve terminal cytoskeleton (β-III tubulin is expressed in motor axons and terminals), enabling co-visualization of motor nerve endings for NMJ pairing, nerve coverage, and denervation assessment. Detected via whole-mount immunofluorescence with a secondary Alexa Fluor antibody in a spectrally distinct channel from α-BTX.
- **DAPI**: Nuclear counterstain for tissue orientation and morphological reference; compatible with CUBIC aqueous environment.

---

## Protocol Steps:

### 1 Sample Preparation and Pre-treatment

1.1 Retrieve fixed gastrocnemius muscle (previously fixed in 4% PFA/PBS and post-fixed; ~8 mm × 5 mm × 3 mm). Wash in 1× PBS to remove residual fixative. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 × 10 minutes)

1.2 Trim any excess connective tissue or fat from the muscle surface using fine scissors under a dissection microscope to improve reagent penetration. (Temperature: RT, Time: as needed)

1.3 Transfer muscle to a 2 mL microcentrifuge tube or glass vial. Incubate in 1× PBS containing 0.1% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (PBS-T) with gentle rocking to permeabilize surface membranes and facilitate subsequent reagent penetration. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 × 1 hour)

---

### 2 Alpha-Bungarotoxin Labeling (AChR Postsynaptic Membrane)

2.1 Prepare α-bungarotoxin–Alexa Fluor 555 (or Alexa Fluor 647) working solution at 5 µg/mL in PBS containing 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100, 5% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum (NDS), and 0.02% (wt/vol) sodium azide. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: preparation on ice)

2.2 Incubate muscle in α-bungarotoxin–Alexa Fluor working solution with gentle rocking. **Note: Extended incubation (3–4 days) is critical for full penetration of intact gastrocnemius muscle and is the primary correction over the previous 1-day protocol.** (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 72–96 hours)

2.3 Wash in PBS-T (0.5% Triton X-100 in 1× PBS) with gentle rocking to remove unbound α-BTX. (Temperature: RT, Time: 4 × 30 minutes)

---

### 3 Whole-Mount Immunolabeling for β-III Tubulin (TUJ1) — Motor Nerve Terminals and Axons

3.1 Incubate muscle in blocking/permeabilization solution: PBS containing 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100, 10% (vol/vol) NDS, 0.02% (wt/vol) sodium azide, with gentle rocking. (Temperature: RT, Time: 4 hours)

3.2 Prepare primary antibody solution: anti-β-III Tubulin (TUJ1) rabbit monoclonal antibody at 1:200 dilution in PBS containing 0.5% Triton X-100, 5% NDS, 0.02% sodium azide. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: preparation on ice)

3.3 Incubate muscle in primary antibody (anti-TUJ1) solution with gentle rocking. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 5–7 days)

3.4 Wash in PBS-T (0.5% Triton X-100 in 1× PBS) with gentle rocking. (Temperature: RT, Time: 4 × 1 hour, then overnight wash)

3.5 Prepare secondary antibody solution: donkey anti-rabbit IgG conjugated to Alexa Fluor 488 at 1:400 dilution in PBS containing 0.5% Triton X-100, 5% NDS, 0.02% sodium azide. Ensure spectral separation from α-BTX–Alexa Fluor 555/647 channel. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: preparation on ice)

3.6 Incubate muscle in secondary antibody solution with gentle rocking, protected from light. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 3–4 days)

3.7 Wash in PBS-T (0.5% Triton X-100 in 1× PBS) with gentle rocking, protected from light. (Temperature: RT, Time: 4 × 1 hour, then overnight wash)

---

### 4 DAPI Nuclear Counterstaining

4.1 Incubate muscle in DAPI solution at 1 µg/mL in 1× PBS with gentle rocking, protected from light. (Temperature: RT, Time: 4 hours)

4.2 Wash in 1× PBS with gentle rocking to remove excess DAPI. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 × 30 minutes)

---

### 5 CUBIC Delipidation — CUBIC-1 Treatment

5.1 Prepare CUBIC-1 solution: 25% (wt/vol) urea, 25% (wt/vol) N,N,N′,N′-tetrakis(2-hydroxypropyl)ethylenediamine (Quadrol), 15% (wt/vol) Triton X-100 in distilled water. Adjust to pH ~9.0–9.5. (Temperature: RT, Time: preparation)

5.2 Incubate muscle in 50% (vol/vol) CUBIC-1 diluted in distilled water (1:1 with dH₂O) with gentle shaking, protected from light. This gradual introduction reduces osmotic shock and tissue distortion. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)

5.3 Replace with full-strength CUBIC-1 solution and incubate with gentle shaking, protected from light. Change CUBIC-1 solution every 24 hours. Monitor clearing progress visually. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 3–5 days, until tissue becomes visibly translucent)

5.4 Wash in 1× PBS with gentle rocking to remove CUBIC-1 residues. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 × 1 hour)

---

### 6 CUBIC Refractive Index Matching — CUBIC-2 Treatment

6.1 Prepare CUBIC-2 solution: 50% (wt/vol) sucrose, 25% (wt/vol) urea, 10% (wt/vol) 2,2′-thiodiethanol (TDE), 1% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in distilled water. Adjust RI to ~1.49–1.52 using a refractometer. (Temperature: RT, Time: preparation)

6.2 Incubate muscle in 50% (vol/vol) CUBIC-2 diluted in 1× PBS (1:1 with PBS) with gentle rocking, protected from light. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)

6.3 Replace with full-strength CUBIC-2 solution and incubate with gentle rocking, protected from light. (Temperature: RT, Time: 48–72 hours, until tissue is fully transparent and RI-matched)

6.4 Verify tissue transparency visually and confirm RI of CUBIC-2 solution matches tissue RI (~1.49–1.52) using a hand-held refractometer before imaging. (Temperature: RT, Time: 10 minutes)

---

### 7 Mounting for 3D Imaging

7.1 Transfer cleared muscle to a custom imaging chamber (e.g., 35 mm glass-bottom dish or custom 3D-printed holder) filled with fresh CUBIC-2 solution. Orient the muscle with the superficial surface facing the objective for optimal NMJ imaging. (Temperature: RT, Time: as needed)

7.2 Seal the chamber with a coverslip using silicone grease or vacuum grease to prevent evaporation and maintain RI matching. Ensure no air bubbles are trapped. (Temperature: RT, Time: as needed)

7.3 Allow the mounted sample to equilibrate in CUBIC-2 for at least 1 hour before imaging to ensure complete RI homogeneity throughout the tissue. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1–2 hours)

---

### 8 3D Imaging Parameters (Recommended)

8.1 Image using a light-sheet fluorescence microscope (LSFM) or confocal microscope equipped with a long-working-distance, water/glycerol-immersion objective (e.g., 10× or 25× objective, NA ≥ 0.8) compatible with CUBIC-2 RI (~1.49). Acquire z-stacks spanning the full muscle depth with ≤2 µm z-step for NMJ morphometry. (Temperature: RT, Time: per imaging session)

8.2 Acquire multi-channel images sequentially: Channel 1 — DAPI (405 nm excitation); Channel 2 — Alexa Fluor 488/TUJ1-nerve terminals (488 nm excitation); Channel 3 — α-BTX–Alexa Fluor 555 (561 nm excitation) or α-BTX–Alexa Fluor 647 (638 nm excitation). Adjust laser power and exposure to minimize photobleaching. (Temperature: RT, Time: per imaging session)

8.3 For post-imaging analysis of NMJ pairing, endplate fragmentation, nerve coverage, and denervation: use 3D reconstruction software (e.g., Imaris, Fiji/ImageJ with 3D plugins) to co-register α-BTX (postsynaptic AChR) and TUJ1 (presynaptic nerve terminal) channels for quantitative NMJ assessment. (Temperature: RT, Time: post-acquisition)

model_response:
**Chosen Method:** iDISCO+
**Chosen Labeling:** [PGP9.5 (pan-neuronal marker, primary antibody + Alexa Fluor 647 secondary), TH (tyrosine hydroxylase, sympathetic fibers, primary antibody + Alexa Fluor 568 secondary), Alexa Fluor 488 (anti-VIP antibody, parasympathetic/vagal fibers)]

**Justification:** iDISCO+ is selected because: (1) it achieves excellent whole-organ clearing of soft tissues (~20×15×8 mm mouse stomach) via organic solvent-based delipidation, enabling deep antibody penetration throughout all gastric wall layers (mucosa, submucosa, muscularis, serosa); (2) its methanol-based dehydration and dibenzyl ether (DBE) RI-matching are well-suited for preserving antigenicity when combined with optimized immunolabeling; (3) the protocol supports multiplexed immunofluorescence with Alexa Fluor dyes that are stable in organic solvents; (4) the cleared tissue achieves RI ~1.56 (DBE), compatible with light-sheet fluorescence microscopy (LSFM) for full 3D reconstruction of the intact stomach. For labeling strategy: **PGP9.5** (protein gene product 9.5, encoded by UCHL1) serves as the primary pan-neuronal marker to visualize all nerve fibers, branches, and terminals throughout the gastric wall; **TH** labels sympathetic adrenergic fibers to distinguish sympathetic innervation; **VIP** (vasoactive intestinal peptide) labels parasympathetic/vagal peptidergic terminals, directly addressing the vagal innervation mapping goal. This three-channel strategy enables comprehensive mapping of fiber trunk morphology, branching complexity, regional density differences (fundus, corpus, antrum, pylorus), and laminar spatial localization. DiI/DiO are excluded as primary markers because anterograde/retrograde lipophilic tracers require in vivo injection and only label specific projection pathways, failing to provide the pan-neuronal whole-wall network view required by the scientific objective.

---

**Protocol Steps:**

**1 Pre-clearing Tissue Preparation**
1.1 Retrieve fixed whole mouse stomach (post-fixed in 4% PFA/PBS); wash with 1× PBS to remove residual fixative. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 × 10 min)
1.2 Open stomach along greater curvature with micro-scissors, gently flush luminal contents with 1× PBS; re-close or pin flat on silicone pad if needed for uniform clearing. (Temperature: RT, Time: 15 min)
1.3 Post-fix in freshly prepared 4% (wt/vol) paraformaldehyde in 1× PBS to ensure complete fixation of all wall layers. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: overnight, ~16 hours)
1.4 Wash with 1× PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 × 20 min)

**2 Dehydration (Methanol Series)**
2.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in ddH₂O with gentle shaking. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
2.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in ddH₂O with gentle shaking. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
2.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in ddH₂O with gentle shaking. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
2.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in ddH₂O with gentle shaking. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
2.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol with gentle shaking. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
2.6 Repeat incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

**3 Bleaching (Peroxide Treatment)**
3.1 Prepare chilled bleaching solution: 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in 100% methanol (1 volume 30% H₂O₂ : 5 volumes 100% MeOH); incubate sample fully submerged. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 16 hours)

**4 Rehydration**
4.1 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in ddH₂O with gentle shaking. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
4.2 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in ddH₂O with gentle shaking. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
4.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in ddH₂O with gentle shaking. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
4.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in ddH₂O with gentle shaking. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
4.5 Incubation with 1× PBS with gentle shaking. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
4.6 Repeat wash with fresh 1× PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

**5 Permeabilization and Blocking**
5.1 Incubation with permeabilization solution: 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100, 20% (vol/vol) DMSO, 0.3 M glycine in 1× PBS, with gentle shaking. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)
5.2 Incubation with blocking solution: 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100, 10% (vol/vol) DMSO, 6% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum (NDS) in 1× PBS, with gentle shaking. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 48 hours)

**6 Primary Antibody Immunolabeling**
6.1 Prepare primary antibody cocktail in PTwH buffer (1× PBS, 0.2% Tween-20, 10 µg/mL heparin) supplemented with 5% (vol/vol) DMSO and 3% (vol/vol) NDS:
- Anti-PGP9.5 (rabbit polyclonal, e.g., Abcam ab108986), dilution 1:500
- Anti-TH (sheep polyclonal, e.g., Millipore AB1542), dilution 1:400
- Anti-VIP (guinea pig polyclonal, e.g., Immunostar 20077), dilution 1:300
Incubate with gentle rocking. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days)
6.2 Wash with PTwH buffer (1× PBS + 0.2% Tween-20 + 10 µg/mL heparin) with gentle shaking. (Temperature: RT, Time: 5 × 1 hour, then overnight)

**7 Secondary Antibody Immunolabeling**
7.1 Prepare secondary antibody cocktail in PTwH buffer supplemented with 3% (vol/vol) NDS:
- Donkey anti-rabbit Alexa Fluor 647 (e.g., Thermo A31573), dilution 1:500 → labels PGP9.5 (pan-neuronal)
- Donkey anti-sheep Alexa Fluor 568 (e.g., Thermo A21099), dilution 1:500 → labels TH (sympathetic)
- Donkey anti-guinea pig Alexa Fluor 488 (e.g., Jackson 706-545-148), dilution 1:500 → labels VIP (parasympathetic/vagal)
Incubate with gentle rocking, protected from light. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 5 days)
7.2 Wash with PTwH buffer with gentle shaking, protected from light. (Temperature: RT, Time: 5 × 1 hour, then overnight)

**8 Post-immunolabeling Fixation**
8.1 Post-fix in 4% (wt/vol) paraformaldehyde in 1× PBS to stabilize antibody-antigen complexes before organic solvent clearing. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: overnight, ~16 hours)
8.2 Wash with 1× PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 × 20 min)

**9 Second Dehydration (Methanol Series)**
9.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in ddH₂O with gentle shaking. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
9.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in ddH₂O with gentle shaking. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
9.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in ddH₂O with gentle shaking. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
9.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in ddH₂O with gentle shaking. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
9.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol with gentle shaking. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
9.6 Repeat incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

**10 Delipidation**
10.1 Incubation with 33% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) in 100% methanol (1 volume DCM : 2 volumes MeOH) with gentle shaking in a fume hood. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours)
10.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DCM (Sigma 270997) with gentle shaking in a fume hood; tissue should sink to bottom of vial when fully delipidated. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 × 15 min)

**11 Refractive Index Matching**
11.1 Transfer tissue immediately from DCM into 100% (vol/vol) dibenzyl ether (DBE, Sigma 108014-1KG) without shaking; ensure complete submersion. RI of DBE ≈ 1.559, matching cleared gastric tissue. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours)
11.2 Replace with fresh 100% (vol/vol) DBE and incubate without shaking until tissue is fully transparent (appears glass-like). (Temperature: RT, Time: overnight, ~16 hours)

**12 Storage and Pre-imaging Preparation**
12.1 Store cleared stomach in 100% DBE in a sealed glass vial, protected from light, until imaging. (Temperature: RT, Time: up to 4 weeks)
12.2 For light-sheet fluorescence microscopy (LSFM): mount cleared stomach in a custom glass chamber or FEP tube filled with 100% DBE; orient sample to allow sequential imaging of fundus, corpus, antrum, and pylorus regions. Objective: use DBE-compatible long-working-distance objectives (e.g., ZEISS Lightsheet Z.1 with 5× or 12× clearing objectives, or LaVision Ultramicroscope with 2×/4× objectives). Laser lines: 488 nm (VIP/Alexa Fluor 488), 561 nm (TH/Alexa Fluor 568), 647 nm (PGP9.5/Alexa Fluor 647). (Temperature: RT, Time: as required for imaging session)

**Chosen Method:** iDISCO+
**Chosen Labeling:** [PGP9.5 + Alexa Fluor 647, TH + Alexa Fluor 568, DAPI]

**Justification:**
iDISCO+ is selected because: (1) it achieves deep, uniform clearing of thick, lipid-rich visceral organs (20×15×8 mm intact stomach) via organic-solvent delipidation (methanol/DCM/DBE), enabling whole-organ light-sheet imaging; (2) it is fully compatible with immunolabeling of intramural neural networks using whole-mount antibody staining with optimized permeabilization and blocking; (3) the solvent-based RI matching (DBE, n≈1.56) provides excellent transparency for deep-tissue confocal or light-sheet microscopy. For labeling strategy: **PGP9.5 (protein gene product 9.5 / UCHL1)** is a pan-neuronal/pan-axonal marker that labels all nerve fibers (both sympathetic and parasympathetic/vagal) comprehensively, serving as the primary channel for mapping the full enteric and extrinsic neural network. **TH (tyrosine hydroxylase)** labels sympathetic adrenergic fibers specifically, allowing discrimination of sympathetic vs. non-sympathetic (including vagal parasympathetic) innervation by subtraction/comparison with the PGP9.5 channel. **DAPI** provides nuclear counterstain for tissue layer orientation (mucosa/submucosa/muscularis/serosa) and serves as a structural reference. This two-marker neuronal strategy directly addresses the goal of comprehensively mapping vagal terminal distribution and comparing fiber density across gastric regions and wall layers.

---

## Protocol Steps

### 1 Post-fixation Wash
1.1 Wash fixed intact stomach (4% PFA in PBS, already fixed) with 1× PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour × 3 washes)

### 2 Pretreatment – Gastric Lumen Flushing
2.1 Inject 1× PBS into the gastric lumen via syringe through the pylorus to flush residual contents; repeat 3×. (Temperature: RT, Time: 10 minutes total)
2.2 Ligate pylorus and cardia with surgical suture to maintain organ integrity during clearing. (Temperature: RT, Time: 5 minutes)

### 3 Dehydration (Methanol Series)
3.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in H₂O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
3.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in H₂O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
3.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in H₂O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
3.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in H₂O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
3.5 Incubation with 100% methanol. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
3.6 Incubation with 100% methanol (second change). (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

### 4 Bleaching
4.1 Incubation with chilled fresh 5% H₂O₂ in 100% methanol (1 volume 30% H₂O₂ : 5 volumes MeOH). (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 16 hours)

### 5 Rehydration (Methanol Series, Reverse)
5.1 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in H₂O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
5.2 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in H₂O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
5.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in H₂O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
5.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in H₂O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
5.5 Incubation with 1× PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour × 2 washes)

### 6 Permeabilization and Blocking
6.1 Incubation with permeabilization solution [0.2% (wt/vol) gelatin, 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100, 0.01% (wt/vol) sodium azide in 1× PBS (PTxwH)]. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours, with gentle shaking)
6.2 Incubation with blocking solution [0.2% (wt/vol) gelatin, 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100, 10% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum, 0.01% (wt/vol) sodium azide in 1× PBS]. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours, with gentle shaking)

### 7 Primary Antibody Incubation
7.1 Incubation with primary antibody cocktail in PTxwH + 10% normal donkey serum:
- Anti-PGP9.5 (rabbit polyclonal, e.g., Abcam ab108986), 1:500 dilution
- Anti-TH (chicken polyclonal, e.g., Abcam ab76442), 1:400 dilution
(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 5 days, with gentle shaking on orbital shaker)

### 8 Post-primary Antibody Wash
8.1 Wash with PTxwH solution [0.2% gelatin, 0.5% Triton X-100, 0.01% sodium azide in 1× PBS]. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 1 hour × 5 washes)
8.2 Extended overnight wash with PTxwH. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 12 hours)

### 9 Secondary Antibody and Nuclear Stain Incubation
9.1 Incubation with secondary antibody cocktail + nuclear stain in PTxwH + 10% normal donkey serum:
- Donkey anti-rabbit Alexa Fluor 647 (e.g., Thermo Fisher A31573), 1:500 dilution → labels PGP9.5 (pan-neuronal, primary channel)
- Donkey anti-chicken Alexa Fluor 568 (e.g., Thermo Fisher A78952), 1:500 dilution → labels TH (sympathetic fibers, secondary channel)
- DAPI, 1 µg/mL → nuclear counterstain for tissue layer reference
(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 3 days, with gentle shaking, protected from light)

### 10 Post-secondary Antibody Wash
10.1 Wash with PTxwH solution. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 1 hour × 5 washes, protected from light)
10.2 Extended overnight wash with PTxwH. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 12 hours, protected from light)
10.3 Final wash with 1× PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes × 2 washes)

### 11 Dehydration (Pre-clearing, Methanol Series)
11.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in H₂O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
11.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in H₂O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
11.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in H₂O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
11.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in H₂O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
11.5 Incubation with 100% methanol. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
11.6 Incubation with 100% methanol (second change). (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

### 12 Delipidation with DCM
12.1 Incubation with 33% (vol/vol) DCM (dichloromethane) in methanol. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours, with gentle shaking in fume hood)
12.2 Incubation with 100% DCM. (Temperature: RT, Time: 20 minutes × 2 washes, fume hood)
12.3 Check tissue: stomach should appear white/opaque and sink to bottom of vial.

### 13 Refractive Index Matching with DBE
13.1 Incubation with 100% DBE (dibenzyl ether, Sigma-Aldrich 108014) without shaking, protected from light. (Temperature: RT, Time: 4 hours)
13.2 Replace with fresh 100% DBE; incubate until tissue is fully transparent (visually clear). (Temperature: RT, Time: 12–24 hours, protected from light)

### 14 Storage Prior to Imaging
14.1 Store cleared stomach in 100% DBE in a sealed glass vial, protected from light. (Temperature: RT, Time: up to 4 weeks; for longer storage use 4 ℃)

### 15 Imaging Preparation (Light-Sheet or Confocal)
15.1 Mount cleared stomach in a custom agarose-free glass chamber filled with 100% DBE; orient with anterior gastric wall facing objective for systematic z-stack acquisition. (Temperature: RT)
15.2 Imaging channels:
- DAPI: 405 nm excitation → tissue layer structural reference (mucosa/submucosa/muscularis/serosa)
- Alexa Fluor 568 (TH): 561 nm excitation → sympathetic adrenergic fiber network
- Alexa Fluor 647 (PGP9.5): 638 nm excitation → pan-neuronal/all nerve fiber network (primary vagal mapping channel)
15.3 Acquire whole-organ tile z-stacks at 4–10 µm z-step (overview) and 1–2 µm z-step (high-resolution sub-regions: cardia, fundus, corpus, antrum, pylorus) using 4× (overview) and 25× water/silicone-immersion objectives compatible with RI ≈ 1.56 (DBE). (Temperature: RT)
15.4 Post-acquisition: register multi-tile stacks using BigStitcher (Fiji); perform 3D reconstruction and fiber density/connectivity analysis using Imaris or NeuTube to generate the 3D reference atlas of gastric vagal terminal distribution. (Temperature: RT)

**Chosen Method:** iDISCO+
**Chosen Labeling:** [PGP9.5 + Alexa Fluor 647, Phalloidin + Alexa Fluor 568]

**Justification:** iDISCO+ is selected because: (1) it achieves excellent whole-organ delipidation of a ~20 mm × 15 mm × 8 mm intact mouse stomach via organic solvent-based clearing, enabling full-thickness imaging through mucosa, submucosa, muscularis propria, and serosa; (2) its methanol-based dehydration and dibenzyl ether (DBE) RI-matching step (RI ≈ 1.56) are well-matched to light-sheet microscopy; (3) the immunolabeling-first workflow (antibody staining performed after permeabilization but before clearing) is compatible with large-volume antibody penetration when combined with extended incubation at 37 °C. PGP9.5 (protein gene product 9.5, a pan-neuronal ubiquitin hydrolase) is chosen as the primary neuronal marker because it labels all autonomic and sensory nerve fibers and terminals throughout the gastric wall—including vagal afferent/efferent endings in the submucosal and myenteric plexuses and serosal nerve bundles—providing the pan-neuronal identity required by the scientific goal. Phalloidin conjugated to Alexa Fluor 568 is chosen as the structural reference because it binds F-actin with high specificity and stoichiometry, directly delineating the circular and longitudinal smooth muscle layers of the muscularis propria as well as the muscularis mucosae, fulfilling the restriction's preference for Phalloidin as the muscle/F-actin reference probe. Alexa Fluor 647 on the secondary antibody for PGP9.5 provides spectral separation from Phalloidin-568, enabling simultaneous two-channel acquisition. Both fluorophores survive the iDISCO+ DBE clearing step when fixation is adequate.

---

**Protocol Steps:**

**1 Pre-clearing Wash**
1.1 Wash intact fixed stomach (post-fixed in 4% PFA/PBS) with 1× PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour × 3 washes)

**2 Permeabilization and Blocking**
2.1 Incubation with permeabilization/blocking solution: PBS containing 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100, 20% (vol/vol) DMSO, 0.3 M glycine, and 5% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum (NDS). (Temperature: 37 °C, Time: 48 hours, with gentle shaking)

**3 Primary Antibody Labeling (PGP9.5)**
3.1 Incubation with primary antibody solution: rabbit anti-PGP9.5 (1:500 dilution) in PTwH buffer [PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Tween-20 + 10 µg/mL heparin] supplemented with 5% (vol/vol) NDS and 5% (vol/vol) DMSO. (Temperature: 37 °C, Time: 7 days, with gentle shaking)
3.2 Wash with PTwH buffer. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour × 5 washes over 24 hours total)

**4 Secondary Antibody Labeling (anti-rabbit Alexa Fluor 647)**
4.1 Incubation with secondary antibody solution: donkey anti-rabbit IgG conjugated to Alexa Fluor 647 (1:500 dilution) in PTwH buffer supplemented with 5% (vol/vol) NDS and 5% (vol/vol) DMSO. (Temperature: 37 °C, Time: 5 days, with gentle shaking)
4.2 Wash with PTwH buffer. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour × 5 washes over 24 hours total)

**5 Phalloidin Labeling (F-actin / Muscularis Reference)**
5.1 Incubation with Phalloidin–Alexa Fluor 568 (5 U/mL, i.e., ~200 nM) in PTwH buffer supplemented with 5% (vol/vol) NDS. (Temperature: 37 °C, Time: 4 days, with gentle shaking)
5.2 Wash with PTwH buffer. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour × 5 washes over 24 hours total)
5.3 Final wash with 1× PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes × 2 washes)

**6 Dehydration (Methanol Gradient)**
6.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in ddH₂O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
6.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in ddH₂O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
6.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in ddH₂O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
6.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in ddH₂O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
6.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol (anhydrous). (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
6.6 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol (anhydrous), second change. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

**7 Bleaching (Endogenous Pigment Removal)**
7.1 Incubation with chilled fresh 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in 100% methanol (1 volume 30% H₂O₂ : 5 volumes MeOH). (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 12 hours, protected from light)
7.2 Wash with 100% (vol/vol) methanol (anhydrous). (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes × 3 washes)

**8 Delipidation with Dichloromethane (DCM)**
8.1 Incubation with 66% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) / 33% (vol/vol) methanol mixture. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours, with gentle shaking)
8.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DCM. (Temperature: RT, Time: 15 minutes)
8.3 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DCM, second change. (Temperature: RT, Time: 15 minutes)

**9 Refractive Index Matching with Dibenzyl Ether (DBE)**
9.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DBE (Sigma-Aldrich, 108014; RI ≈ 1.562) without shaking, in a glass vial protected from light. (Temperature: RT, Time: 4 hours)
9.2 Replace with fresh 100% (vol/vol) DBE; incubate until tissue is fully transparent and optically homogeneous (typically overnight). (Temperature: RT, Time: 12–16 hours, protected from light)

**10 Storage Prior to Imaging**
10.1 Transfer cleared stomach to a clean glass vial filled with fresh 100% (vol/vol) DBE, sealed with Parafilm to prevent evaporation. Store protected from light. (Temperature: RT or 4 °C, Time: up to 4 weeks)

**11 Imaging Preparation (Light-Sheet Microscopy)**
11.1 Mount cleared stomach in a custom glass-bottom imaging chamber filled with 100% (vol/vol) DBE. Orient the stomach with the greater curvature facing the objective to allow sequential z-stack acquisition from serosa through muscularis propria to mucosa. Use an objective compatible with DBE immersion (RI ≈ 1.56; e.g., LSFM 4×/0.35 or 12×/0.53 long-working-distance objective with DBE-compatible housing). (Temperature: RT, Time: as required for acquisition)
11.2 Acquire dual-channel z-stacks: Channel 1 — 638 nm excitation / 680 nm emission (PGP9.5–Alexa Fluor 647, pan-neuronal fibers and terminals); Channel 2 — 561 nm excitation / 600 nm emission (Phalloidin–Alexa Fluor 568, circular muscle, longitudinal muscle, muscularis mucosae F-actin reference). Step size: 2–5 µm for full-thickness survey; 1 µm for high-resolution myenteric plexus regions. (Temperature: RT, Time: as required for acquisition)

**Chosen Method:** iDISCO+
**Chosen Labeling:** [Alexa Fluor (anti-HuC/D + Alexa Fluor secondary), Alexa Fluor (anti-TH + Alexa Fluor secondary), DAPI]

**Justification:**
iDISCO+ is selected because: (1) it employs methanol-based dehydration and dichloromethane (DCM) delipidation, which effectively removes lipids and myelin from thick, lipid-rich gastric wall tissue (~8 mm), enabling deep antibody penetration; (2) the methanol/H₂O₂ bleaching step eliminates autofluorescence from gastric mucosa and muscle layers, directly addressing the high-background problem; (3) the organic solvent-based RI matching reagent DBE (n=1.56) provides excellent transparency for light-sheet imaging of the full stomach volume; (4) iDISCO+ has been extensively validated for whole-organ immunolabeling of enteric and vagal nerve networks in gastrointestinal tissues. For markers: **HuC/D** (pan-neuronal RNA-binding protein) labels all enteric neuron cell bodies and vagal terminal ganglia comprehensively across all gastric regions and wall layers; **TH** (tyrosine hydroxylase) labels sympathetic/adrenergic fibers and allows discrimination of adrenergic vs. non-adrenergic innervation, together providing dual-channel full coverage of the gastric neural network including fiber trunks, branches, terminal arborizations, and regional/layer-specific distribution differences. **DAPI** is excluded from the final iDISCO+ protocol as it is incompatible with organic solvents; nuclear counterstaining is omitted per iDISCO+ standard practice. Two spectrally separated Alexa Fluor secondaries (e.g., Alexa Fluor 488 and Alexa Fluor 647) are used for dual-channel detection.

---

**Protocol Steps:**

**1 Sample Preparation and Pre-treatment**

1.1 Retrieve fixed whole mouse stomach (post-fixed in 4% PFA/PBS). Rinse with 1× PBS to remove residual fixative. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 × 10 min)

1.2 Trim excess connective tissue and fat from the serosal surface with fine scissors. Open the stomach along the greater curvature, gently flush luminal contents with PBS, then re-close or keep intact depending on imaging orientation. (Temperature: RT, Time: ~15 min)

1.3 Incubation in 1× PBS with gentle rocking to ensure complete rehydration and removal of fixative. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 × 30 min)

---

**2 Dehydration (Methanol Series)**

2.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in ddH₂O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

2.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in ddH₂O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

2.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in ddH₂O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

2.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in ddH₂O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

2.5 Incubation with 100% methanol (anhydrous). (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

2.6 Incubation with 100% methanol (anhydrous), second change. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

---

**3 Bleaching (Autofluorescence Quenching)**

3.1 Prepare fresh bleaching solution: 5% H₂O₂ (vol/vol) in 100% methanol (1 volume 30% H₂O₂ : 5 volumes 100% MeOH). Incubate sample fully submerged. This step is critical to eliminate gastric mucosal autofluorescence and hemoglobin-derived background. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 16 hours, overnight)

---

**4 Rehydration**

4.1 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in ddH₂O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

4.2 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in ddH₂O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

4.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in ddH₂O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

4.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in ddH₂O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

4.5 Incubation with 1× PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

4.6 Incubation with 1× PBS, second change. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

---

**5 Permeabilization and Blocking**

5.1 Incubation with Permeabilization/Blocking Solution: PBS containing 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100, 20% (vol/vol) DMSO, 0.3 M glycine, 5% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum (NDS). This step simultaneously permeabilizes membranes, blocks non-specific binding sites, and reduces background in thick gastric wall tissue. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 48 hours, with gentle shaking)

---

**6 Primary Antibody Immunolabeling**

6.1 Prepare primary antibody solution in PTwH buffer [PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Tween-20 + 10 µg/mL heparin] supplemented with 5% (vol/vol) DMSO and 3% (vol/vol) NDS:
- Anti-HuC/D (pan-neuronal marker; e.g., mouse monoclonal, Invitrogen A21271 or equivalent): 1:200 dilution
- Anti-TH (tyrosine hydroxylase; e.g., rabbit polyclonal, Millipore AB152 or equivalent): 1:500 dilution
Ensure the two primary antibodies are raised in different host species to allow dual secondary labeling. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days, with gentle rocking; for complete penetration of 8 mm gastric wall)

6.2 Wash with PTwH buffer [PBS + 0.2% Tween-20 + 10 µg/mL heparin]. Perform 5 washes with buffer changes every 2–3 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours total, 5 × ~4–5 hour washes with rocking)

---

**7 Secondary Antibody Immunolabeling**

7.1 Prepare secondary antibody solution in PTwH buffer supplemented with 3% (vol/vol) NDS:
- Donkey anti-mouse Alexa Fluor 488 (targeting HuC/D): 1:500 dilution
- Donkey anti-rabbit Alexa Fluor 647 (targeting TH): 1:500 dilution
Protect from light throughout all subsequent steps. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 5 days, with gentle rocking in the dark)

7.2 Wash with PTwH buffer to remove unbound secondary antibody. Perform 5 washes. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours total, 5 × ~4–5 hour washes with rocking, protected from light)

---

**8 Dehydration Prior to Clearing (Methanol Series)**

8.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in ddH₂O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

8.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in ddH₂O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

8.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in ddH₂O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

8.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in ddH₂O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

8.5 Incubation with 100% methanol (anhydrous). (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

8.6 Incubation with 100% methanol (anhydrous), second change. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

---

**9 Delipidation**

9.1 Incubation with 100% dichloromethane (DCM; Sigma 270997). DCM removes residual lipids and myelin sheaths, critical for transparency of the thick muscular gastric wall. Perform in a fume hood. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours, with gentle agitation, 2 × 1.5 hours with DCM change)

---

**10 Refractive Index Matching**

10.1 Incubation with 100% dibenzyl ether (DBE; Sigma 108014, n = 1.56) without shaking. Replace DCM completely; the sample will turn transparent within minutes. Ensure full submersion. (Temperature: RT, Time: 4 hours minimum, or until fully transparent, protected from light)

10.2 Transfer to fresh 100% DBE for storage and imaging. Confirm optical transparency visually before proceeding to imaging. (Temperature: RT, Time: until imaging, protected from light; stable for weeks to months)

---

**11 Sample Mounting and Imaging Preparation**

11.1 Mount the cleared stomach in a glass-bottom imaging chamber or custom holder filled with 100% DBE. Orient the sample to allow imaging from serosal surface through to mucosal layer for full-thickness z-stack acquisition. Seal with DBE-compatible adhesive or silicone grease to prevent evaporation. (Temperature: RT, Time: ~30 min)

11.2 Image using a light-sheet fluorescence microscope (LSFM) with objectives compatible with DBE immersion (n = 1.56; e.g., CLARITY/organic solvent-compatible objectives), or alternatively a confocal microscope with a long-working-distance objective and DBE-filled imaging chamber. Acquire dual-channel z-stacks:
- Channel 1: 488 nm excitation / 510–550 nm emission → HuC/D–Alexa Fluor 488 (pan-neuronal)
- Channel 2: 633/647 nm excitation / 660–720 nm emission → TH–Alexa Fluor 647 (adrenergic fibers)
Step size: 2–5 µm for full-volume mapping; 0.5–1 µm for high-resolution regional analysis. (Temperature: RT, Time: per imaging session)

**Chosen Method:** FDISCO
**Chosen Labeling:** [EGFP, tdTomato]
**Justification:** FDISCO（改良溶剂型透明化方法）基于四氢呋喃（THF）脱水和二苄基醚（DBE）折射率匹配，在低温（4 ℃）条件下操作，可显著减少有机溶剂对荧光蛋白的氧化损伤，相比经典 uDISCO/iDISCO+ 方案更好地保留 EGFP 和 tdTomato 内源荧光信号（文献报道 EGFP 保留率 >80%，tdTomato 保留率 >70%）。完整小鼠大脑（~10×8×6 mm）在 FDISCO 流程中可在约 3–4 天内实现高度透明，透明后 RI≈1.56（DBE），与光片显微镜（LSFM）成像窗口匹配良好，适合全脑尺度长程轴突追踪。由于目标投射神经元和轴突已携带 EGFP 与 tdTomato 双色内源荧光，无需额外抗体标记，直接利用内源信号即可同时区分两组示踪通路，避免抗体渗透不均匀问题，简化流程并保护荧光完整性。

---

**Protocol Steps:**

1 样品预处理与漂洗（Post-fixation wash）
1.1 将已完成 4% PFA 固定及后固定的完整小鼠大脑置于 1× PBS 中充分漂洗，去除残余固定液。（Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 3 × 1 hour，每次更换新鲜 PBS）
1.2 将样品转移至 1.5 mL 或 5 mL 遮光离心管中，后续所有步骤均在遮光（铝箔包裹）条件下进行，以保护 EGFP 和 tdTomato 荧光。（Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 操作步骤，无额外孵育）

2 脱水（Dehydration with THF）
2.1 在新鲜配制的 50%（vol/vol）四氢呋喃（THF，含 0.01% BHT 抗氧化剂，溶于超纯水）中孵育，轻柔旋转摇动。（Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 1 hour）
2.2 在 70%（vol/vol）THF（含 0.01% BHT）中孵育，轻柔旋转摇动。（Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 1 hour）
2.3 在 80%（vol/vol）THF（含 0.01% BHT）中孵育，轻柔旋转摇动。（Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 1 hour）
2.4 在 100%（vol/vol）THF（含 0.01% BHT）中孵育，轻柔旋转摇动，第一次。（Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 1 hour）
2.5 在 100%（vol/vol）THF（含 0.01% BHT）中孵育，轻柔旋转摇动，第二次（更换新鲜 THF）。（Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 1 hour）
2.6 在 100%（vol/vol）THF（含 0.01% BHT）中孵育，轻柔旋转摇动，第三次（更换新鲜 THF），确保完全脱水。（Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours，过夜）

3 脱脂与透明化（Delipidation and Clearing with DBE）
3.1 将样品从 THF 中取出，直接转入 100%（vol/vol）二苄基醚（DBE，Sigma-Aldrich 108014）中孵育，轻柔旋转摇动，第一次。（Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 4 hours）
3.2 更换新鲜 100%（vol/vol）DBE，继续孵育，第二次，直至样品完全透明（肉眼观察脑组织呈透明玻璃状）。（Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours，过夜）
3.3 若透明度不足，可再次更换新鲜 100% DBE 孵育至完全透明。（Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 4–12 hours，视透明程度而定）

4 折射率匹配（Refractive Index Matching）
4.1 将透明后的样品保存于 100%（vol/vol）DBE（RI ≈ 1.562）中，DBE 本身即作为最终折射率匹配介质，与光片显微镜（LSFM）使用的长工作距离物镜（RI 匹配范围 1.45–1.56）兼容。（Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 至少 2 hours，稳定 RI 后即可成像）
4.2 成像前将样品转移至适配光片显微镜样品池（如石英比色皿或定制样品槽），用 DBE 充满样品池，确保样品完全浸没，避免气泡。（Temperature: RT, Time: 30 min，平衡温度）

5 样品保存与成像前处理（Storage and Pre-imaging Preparation）
5.1 若不立即成像，将透明样品密封保存于 100% DBE 中，置于遮光容器中。（Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 可保存 1–4 周，长期保存荧光有所衰减，建议尽快成像）
5.2 成像前检查 EGFP（激发 488 nm，发射 507 nm）和 tdTomato（激发 554 nm，发射 581 nm）双通道荧光信号强度，确认信号保留良好，必要时调整激光功率和曝光参数。（Temperature: RT, Time: 成像前检查，约 15–30 min）

**Chosen Method:** iDISCO+
**Chosen Labeling:** [EGFP (内源), tdTomato (内源), MAP2 + Alexa Fluor (secondary, e.g., Alexa Fluor 647), DAPI]

**Justification:**
iDISCO+ is selected as the optimal clearing method for this problem for the following reasons:
1. **Whole-brain compatibility:** iDISCO+ is specifically validated for intact mouse whole-brain samples (~10×8×6 mm), achieving high transparency through organic solvent-based delipidation (DCM/DBE) that efficiently removes lipids from large volumes.
2. **Endogenous fluorophore preservation:** The methanol dehydration + H₂O₂ bleaching steps in iDISCO+ are compatible with robust fluorescent proteins. EGFP and tdTomato are both sufficiently photostable and structurally stable to survive the iDISCO+ protocol when fixation is adequate, allowing them to serve as primary projection tracing channels without additional immunostaining.
3. **Immunolabeling integration:** iDISCO+ includes a well-established whole-mount immunostaining pipeline with methanol-based permeabilization, enabling deep antibody penetration into the intact brain — critical for labeling MAP2 (a dendritic marker) throughout deep structures including amygdala, PFC, thalamus, and NAc.
4. **RI matching with DBE:** Dibenzyl ether (RI ≈ 1.56) provides excellent RI matching for light-sheet fluorescence microscopy (LSFM), which is the ideal imaging modality for whole-brain projection tracing at single-axon resolution.
5. **Multi-channel compatibility:** The combination of EGFP (Ch1, ~488 nm), tdTomato (Ch2, ~561 nm), Alexa Fluor 647-conjugated anti-MAP2 (Ch3, ~647 nm), and DAPI (Ch4, ~405 nm) provides four spectrally separated channels covering projection tracing, dendritic architecture, and cytoarchitectural boundaries — fully addressing the scientific goals.

**Labeling rationale:**
- **EGFP / tdTomato (endogenous):** Retained as primary projection tracing channels for axonal/dendritic projections from labeled neurons. No additional immunoamplification required if signal is strong; optional anti-GFP/anti-RFP amplification can be added if needed.
- **MAP2 + Alexa Fluor 647:** MAP2 is a somatodendritic marker (microtubule-associated protein 2) that specifically labels dendrites and soma, providing the dendritic skeleton structure in target regions. Alexa Fluor 647 is chosen for its far-red emission, minimal spectral overlap with EGFP and tdTomato, and excellent photostability in DBE.
- **DAPI:** Labels nuclei to define cytoarchitectural boundaries of amygdala, PFC, thalamus, and NAc for spatial registration and region-of-interest delineation.

---

**Protocol Steps:**

**1 Pre-clearing Wash**
1.1 Wash fixed whole brain in 1× PBS (phosphate-buffered saline, pH 7.4) with gentle rocking to remove residual fixative. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 × 1 hour)

**2 Dehydration**
2.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in distilled H₂O with gentle rocking. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
2.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in distilled H₂O with gentle rocking. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
2.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in distilled H₂O with gentle rocking. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
2.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in distilled H₂O with gentle rocking. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
2.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol with gentle rocking. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
2.6 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol (second change) with gentle rocking. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

**3 Bleaching (Endogenous Peroxidase Quenching & Tissue Brightening)**
3.1 Incubation with chilled fresh 5% H₂O₂ in 100% methanol (1 volume 30% H₂O₂ : 5 volumes MeOH, vol/vol) to reduce autofluorescence and improve transparency. Keep sample protected from light. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12–16 hours)

**4 Rehydration**
4.1 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in distilled H₂O with gentle rocking. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
4.2 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in distilled H₂O with gentle rocking. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
4.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in distilled H₂O with gentle rocking. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
4.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in distilled H₂O with gentle rocking. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
4.5 Incubation with 1× PBS with gentle rocking. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
4.6 Incubation with 1× PBS (second change) with gentle rocking. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

**5 Permeabilization**
5.1 Incubation with Permeabilization Solution [0.2% (wt/vol) gelatin, 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100, 0.01% (wt/vol) sodium azide in 1× PBS] with gentle rocking. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)
5.2 Incubation with fresh Permeabilization Solution (second change, same composition as 5.1) with gentle rocking. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)

**6 Pre-blocking**
6.1 Incubation with Blocking Solution [0.2% (wt/vol) gelatin, 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100, 0.01% (wt/vol) sodium azide, 10% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum in 1× PBS] with gentle rocking. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)

**7 Primary Antibody Immunolabeling**
7.1 Incubation with primary antibody cocktail in Antibody Diluent [0.2% (wt/vol) gelatin, 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100, 0.01% (wt/vol) sodium azide, 5% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum in 1× PBS]:
- Anti-MAP2 (rabbit polyclonal or chicken, 1:500 dilution) — for dendritic skeleton labeling
- Anti-GFP (chicken or rabbit, 1:500 dilution, optional amplification of EGFP signal) — include only if endogenous EGFP signal requires amplification after bleaching step
- Anti-RFP / anti-dsRed (rabbit, 1:500 dilution, optional amplification of tdTomato signal) — include only if endogenous tdTomato signal requires amplification
Gently rock or use rotating wheel. Protect from light. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 5–7 days)

**8 Post-primary Antibody Wash**
8.1 Wash with Wash Buffer [0.2% (wt/vol) gelatin, 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100, 0.01% (wt/vol) sodium azide in 1× PBS] with gentle rocking. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 1 hour)
8.2 Wash with fresh Wash Buffer (second change). (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 1 hour)
8.3 Wash with fresh Wash Buffer (third change). (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 1 hour)
8.4 Wash with fresh Wash Buffer (fourth change). (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 1 hour)
8.5 Wash with fresh Wash Buffer (fifth change). (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 1 hour)
8.6 Wash with fresh Wash Buffer (overnight wash). (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 12 hours)

**9 Secondary Antibody Immunolabeling & Nuclear Counterstain**
9.1 Incubation with secondary antibody cocktail in Antibody Diluent (same composition as Step 7):
- Donkey anti-rabbit Alexa Fluor 647 (1:500 dilution) — for MAP2 detection (and anti-GFP/anti-RFP amplification if used)
- DAPI (4′,6-diamidino-2-phenylindole, 1 µg/mL final concentration) — for nuclear/cytoarchitectural boundary labeling
Note: If anti-GFP (chicken) was used in Step 7, add donkey anti-chicken Alexa Fluor 488 (1:500) to amplify EGFP channel; if anti-RFP (rabbit) was used, ensure secondary is spectrally distinct (e.g., Alexa Fluor 555, 1:500) and adjust channel assignments accordingly. Protect from light. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 3–5 days)

**10 Post-secondary Antibody Wash**
10.1 Wash with Wash Buffer [0.2% (wt/vol) gelatin, 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100, 0.01% (wt/vol) sodium azide in 1× PBS] with gentle rocking. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 1 hour)
10.2 Wash with fresh Wash Buffer (second change). (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 1 hour)
10.3 Wash with fresh Wash Buffer (third change). (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 1 hour)
10.4 Wash with fresh Wash Buffer (fourth change). (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 1 hour)
10.5 Wash with fresh Wash Buffer (fifth change). (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 1 hour)
10.6 Wash with fresh Wash Buffer (overnight wash). Protect from light. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 12 hours)

**11 Dehydration (Pre-clearing)**
11.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in distilled H₂O with gentle rocking. Protect from light. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
11.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in distilled H₂O with gentle rocking. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
11.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in distilled H₂O with gentle rocking. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
11.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in distilled H₂O with gentle rocking. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
11.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol with gentle rocking. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
11.6 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol (second change) with gentle rocking. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

**12 Delipidation**
12.1 Incubation with 66% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) / 33% (vol/vol) methanol (DCM:MeOH = 2:1, vol/vol) with gentle rocking in a chemical fume hood. Ensure container is sealed to prevent evaporation. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours)
12.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DCM (two changes, 15 min each) to wash out residual methanol. (Temperature: RT, Time: 15 minutes × 2)

**13 Refractive Index Matching**
13.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dibenzyl ether (DBE, Sigma-Aldrich 108014, RI ≈ 1.5580) without shaking. Replace DBE once after first 3 hours. Protect from light. Sample should become fully transparent. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours + overnight [total ≥ 12 hours])
13.2 Replace with fresh 100% (vol/vol) DBE and confirm full optical transparency of the whole brain before imaging. Store in DBE in a sealed glass vial protected from light until imaging. (Temperature: RT, Time: until imaging, up to 1–2 weeks)

**14 Sample Mounting for Light-Sheet Fluorescence Microscopy (LSFM)**
14.1 Transfer brain from DBE storage vial into imaging chamber (e.g., custom 3D-printed cuvette or commercial LSFM sample holder) filled with 100% DBE as immersion/clearing medium. Ensure no air bubbles are introduced. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes equilibration)
14.2 Orient brain in the desired imaging axis (e.g., coronal or sagittal) using low-melting agarose (1% in DBE-compatible medium) or custom mounting putty compatible with organic solvents. Confirm orientation under low-magnification preview. (Temperature: RT, Time: as needed)
14.3 Acquire whole-brain light-sheet images using the following channel assignments:
- Ch1 (405 nm excitation / 450 nm emission): DAPI — cytoarchitectural boundaries
- Ch2 (488 nm excitation / 525 nm emission): EGFP (endogenous ± anti-GFP amplification) — projection tracing channel 1
- Ch3 (561 nm excitation / 600 nm emission): tdTomato (endogenous ± anti-RFP amplification) — projection tracing channel 2
- Ch4 (647 nm excitation / 680 nm emission): Alexa Fluor 647 (anti-MAP2) — dendritic skeleton
Use a 4× or 6.3× objective (NA 0.1–0.3) for whole-brain overview and 12× or 25× objective (NA 0.8–1.0, DBE-immersion compatible) for high-resolution regional imaging of amygdala, PFC, thalamus, and NAc. (Temperature: RT, Time: per imaging session)
