model_response:
**Chosen Method:** iDISCO+
**Chosen Labeling:** [CGRP + Alexa Fluor 647, PGP9.5 + Alexa Fluor 568, Lectin + Alexa Fluor 488]

**Justification:** iDISCO+ is selected because: (1) it employs organic solvent-based delipidation (methanol + DCM/DBE) that is highly effective for lipid-rich adipose tissue, removing the abundant lipid droplets that are the primary obstacle to transparency in scWAT; (2) it supports whole-mount immunolabeling with antibody penetration enhanced by the methanol pretreatment step, which is critical for a ~1 cm × 1 cm × 0.5 cm block; (3) DBE as the final RI-matching medium (RI ≈ 1.56) is compatible with light-sheet microscopy and provides excellent transparency for fatty tissues; (4) the protocol is well-validated for peripheral nervous system structures including fine sensory fibers. Labeling strategy: **CGRP** (anti-CGRP primary + Alexa Fluor 647 secondary) identifies peptidergic sensory fibers; **PGP9.5** (anti-PGP9.5 primary + Alexa Fluor 568 secondary) serves as a pan-neuronal marker to capture the full nerve fiber network; **Lectin** (fluorescently conjugated Lectin-Alexa Fluor 488, perfused or bath-applied) labels vascular luminal surfaces as the reference channel for neurovascular spatial analysis. Three spectrally separated channels enable simultaneous 3D mapping of sensory fibers, total nerve fibers, and vasculature.

---

**Protocol Steps:**

**1 Pre-treatment and Permeabilization**

1.1 Wash fixed scWAT sample (1 cm × 1 cm × 0.5 cm, post-fixed in 4% PFA) with 1× PBS three times. (Temperature: RT, Time: 10 min each wash)

1.2 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in H₂O (freshly prepared). (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

1.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in H₂O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

1.4 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in H₂O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

1.5 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in H₂O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

1.6 Incubation with 100% methanol (anhydrous). (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

1.7 Incubation with 100% methanol (anhydrous), second change. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

1.8 Bleaching: Incubation with chilled fresh 5% H₂O₂ in 100% methanol (1 volume 30% H₂O₂ : 5 volumes MeOH). (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)

**2 Rehydration**

2.1 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in H₂O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

2.2 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in H₂O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

2.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in H₂O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

2.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in H₂O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

2.5 Incubation with 1× PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

2.6 Incubation with PBS/0.2% Triton X-100 (PTx0.2). (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

**3 Pre-blocking and Permeabilization Enhancement**

3.1 Incubation with Permeabilization Solution: PBS containing 0.2% Triton X-100, 20% DMSO, 0.3 M glycine, 2.3% L-lysine. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)

3.2 Incubation with Blocking Solution: PBS containing 0.2% Tween-20, 10% DMSO, 6% normal donkey serum (NDS), 0.1% heparin (PTwH/DMSO/NDS). (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)

**4 Vascular Labeling with Lectin (Bath Application)**

4.1 Incubation with Lectin conjugated to Alexa Fluor 488 (e.g., Lycopersicon esculentum Lectin-Alexa Fluor 488, Vector Labs; 50 µg/mL) diluted in PBS/0.2% Tween-20 with 0.1% heparin (PTwH). (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours, gentle rocking)

4.2 Wash with PTwH (PBS/0.2% Tween-20/0.1% heparin), 5 × 1 hour washes. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour each)

**5 Primary Antibody Incubation**

5.1 Incubation with primary antibody cocktail in PTwH/5% DMSO/3% NDS:
- Rabbit anti-CGRP (1:400; e.g., Sigma C8198 or Abcam ab81887)
- Rabbit anti-PGP9.5 replaced by: Chicken anti-PGP9.5 (1:500; e.g., Abcam ab72911) to allow dual primary species separation
*(Note: use rabbit anti-CGRP and chicken anti-PGP9.5 to enable species-specific secondary antibody discrimination)*
(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 5 days, gentle rocking on orbital shaker)

5.2 Wash with PTwH, 5 × 1 hour washes. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour each)

5.3 Additional overnight wash with PTwH. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)

**6 Secondary Antibody Incubation**

6.1 Incubation with secondary antibody cocktail in PTwH/3% NDS:
- Donkey anti-Rabbit IgG conjugated to Alexa Fluor 647 (1:500; for CGRP detection)
- Donkey anti-Chicken IgY conjugated to Alexa Fluor 568 (1:500; for PGP9.5 detection)
(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 3 days, gentle rocking, protected from light)

6.2 Wash with PTwH, 5 × 1 hour washes. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour each)

6.3 Additional overnight wash with PTwH. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)

**7 Post-immunolabeling Fixation**

7.1 Post-fix with 4% PFA in 1× PBS to stabilize antibody-antigen complexes. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

7.2 Wash with 1× PBS, 3 × 20 min washes. (Temperature: RT, Time: 20 min each)

**8 Dehydration (Clearing Series)**

8.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in H₂O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

8.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in H₂O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

8.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in H₂O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

8.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in H₂O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

8.5 Incubation with 100% methanol (anhydrous). (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

8.6 Incubation with 100% methanol (anhydrous), second change. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

**9 Delipidation**

9.1 Incubation with 33% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) in methanol (1 volume DCM : 2 volumes MeOH). (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours, gentle agitation in fume hood)

9.2 Incubation with 100% DCM, first change. (Temperature: RT, Time: 15 min, fume hood)

9.3 Incubation with 100% DCM, second change. (Temperature: RT, Time: 15 min, fume hood)
*(Critical: ensure tissue sinks to bottom of vial, confirming complete delipidation; adipose tissue should become translucent/white at this stage)*

**10 Refractive Index Matching**

10.1 Transfer tissue to dibenzyl ether (DBE, Sigma-Aldrich 108014; RI = 1.559). Incubation with 100% DBE, first change, without shaking. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours, protected from light)

10.2 Incubation with 100% DBE, second change (fresh), without shaking. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours, protected from light)

10.3 Incubation with 100% DBE, third change (fresh), for long-term storage and final RI equilibration. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours, protected from light)
*(Tissue should appear fully transparent; store in DBE in sealed glass vials at RT protected from light until imaging)*

**11 Sample Mounting and Imaging Preparation**

11.1 Mount cleared scWAT sample in a glass-bottom imaging chamber or custom 3D-printed holder filled with 100% DBE. Seal with silicone grease to prevent evaporation. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 min preparation)

11.2 Image using light-sheet fluorescence microscopy (LSFM; e.g., LaVision BioTec Ultramicroscope II or Zeiss Lightsheet Z.1) with DBE-compatible objectives (e.g., MVPLAPO 2×/0.5 or 4×/0.35 dipping objectives compatible with organic solvents), using the following channel assignments:
- Channel 1: 488 nm excitation / 525 nm emission → Lectin-Alexa Fluor 488 (vasculature)
- Channel 2: 561 nm excitation / 593 nm emission → PGP9.5-Alexa Fluor 568 (pan-neuronal fibers)
- Channel 3: 638 nm excitation / 680 nm emission → CGRP-Alexa Fluor 647 (sensory fibers)
(Temperature: RT, Time: per imaging session)

11.3 Acquire z-stacks with ≤5 µm z-step size for full-volume reconstruction; use ≤2 µm z-step for high-resolution regions of interest (e.g., perivascular zones, interlobular septa). (Temperature: RT, Time: per imaging session)

**Chosen Method:** iDISCO+
**Chosen Labeling:** [CGRP (via anti-CGRP primary antibody) + Alexa Fluor 647, PGP9.5 (via anti-PGP9.5/Hu C/D primary antibody) + Alexa Fluor 568/555, DAPI]

**Justification:**
iDISCO+ is selected over CUBIC for this high-lipid scWAT tissue for the following reasons:
1. **Superior delipidation**: iDISCO+ employs a graded methanol series followed by DCM/methanol (or H₂O₂ bleaching) that effectively extracts lipid droplets from adipose tissue — the primary reason CUBIC-L failed (24 h is grossly insufficient for lipid-rich scWAT ~1 cm × 1 cm × 0.5 cm). The organic-solvent backbone of iDISCO+ achieves near-complete lipid removal, converting opaque white fat to transparent tissue.
2. **Deep immunolabeling compatibility**: iDISCO+ uses methanol-based permeabilization and detergent washes that dramatically improve antibody penetration into dense, lipid-rich tissue, addressing the weak signal problem encountered with CUBIC.
3. **RI matching with DBE (n = 1.56)**: Dibenzyl ether provides stable, high-RI matching ideal for deep 3D light-sheet imaging of the full tissue block.
4. **Dual-channel nerve imaging**: PGP9.5 (pan-neuronal, from Hu C/D / PGP9.5 marker list) labels all autonomic and sensory fibers; CGRP labels peptidergic sensory fibers specifically — together enabling quantification of total vs. sensory innervation density, branching, terminal coverage, and spatial distribution across lobules, border zones, and perivascular regions.
5. **DAPI** provides nuclear counterstain for tissue architecture reference (lobule boundaries, vascular walls).
6. Alexa Fluor dyes (647 and a spectrally distinct second channel ~555 nm) are on the permitted dye list and are highly photostable in DBE-based clearing.

---

**Protocol Steps:**

**1 Pre-clearing Washes (Post-fixation tissue, already PFA-fixed and post-fixed)**
1.1 Wash with 1× PBS (pH 7.4). (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 × 30 min)
1.2 Wash with 1× PBS containing 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (PTx0.2) to begin permeabilization. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 × 1 hour)

**2 Dehydration (Methanol Gradient)**
2.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in H₂O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
2.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in H₂O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
2.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in H₂O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
2.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in H₂O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
2.5 Incubation with 100% methanol (anhydrous). (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 × 1 hour)
2.6 Incubation with 100% methanol (anhydrous), overnight to ensure complete dehydration of lipid-rich adipose tissue. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)

**3 Bleaching / H₂O₂ Treatment (Quench autofluorescence from lipid-rich tissue)**
3.1 Incubation with chilled fresh 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in 100% methanol (1 volume 30% H₂O₂ : 5 volumes MeOH) to quench endogenous peroxidase activity and reduce lipid autofluorescence. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12–16 hours, protected from light)
3.2 Wash with 100% methanol. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 3 × 30 min)

**4 Delipidation with DCM/Methanol**
4.1 Incubation with 66% (vol/vol) DCM (dichloromethane) / 33% methanol (DCM:MeOH = 2:1) — critical step for lipid extraction from adipose tissue; agitate gently. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours; repeat if tissue remains opaque: up to 2 × 3 hours, total ≤ 6 hours)
4.2 Check tissue: it should sink to the bottom of the vial and appear translucent/glassy. If still opaque, extend DCM/MeOH incubation by 1–2 hours.
4.3 Wash with 100% methanol to remove residual DCM. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 × 30 min)

**5 Rehydration (Methanol Gradient)**
5.1 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in H₂O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
5.2 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in H₂O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
5.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in H₂O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
5.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in H₂O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
5.5 Incubation with 1× PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 × 30 min)

**6 Permeabilization and Blocking**
6.1 Incubation with Permeabilization Solution: 1× PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 + 20% (vol/vol) DMSO + 0.3 M glycine, to maximize antibody penetration into delipidated adipose tissue. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours, gentle shaking)
6.2 Incubation with Blocking Solution: 1× PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Tween-20 + 10% (vol/vol) DMSO + 6% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum (NDS) + 0.1% (wt/vol) heparin (PTwH + 10% DMSO + 6% NDS). (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours, gentle shaking)

**7 Primary Antibody Immunolabeling**
7.1 Prepare primary antibody cocktail in Antibody Diluent Solution: 1× PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Tween-20 + 5% (vol/vol) DMSO + 3% (vol/vol) NDS + 0.1% (wt/vol) heparin (PTwH + 5% DMSO + 3% NDS):
- Anti-CGRP (rabbit polyclonal or monoclonal, e.g., Sigma C8198 or Abcam ab81887): 1:400 dilution
- Anti-PGP9.5 / Hu C/D (mouse monoclonal, e.g., Abcam ab8189 or equivalent Hu C/D clone): 1:400 dilution
7.2 Incubation with primary antibody cocktail. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 72 hours, gentle shaking on orbital shaker; for 1 cm × 1 cm × 0.5 cm tissue, extend to 96 hours if signal is insufficient)
7.3 Wash with PTwH (1× PBS + 0.2% Tween-20 + 0.1% heparin). (Temperature: RT, Time: 5 × 1 hour, then 1 × overnight at 37 ℃)

**8 Secondary Antibody Immunolabeling**
8.1 Prepare secondary antibody cocktail in PTwH + 3% NDS:
- Donkey anti-rabbit Alexa Fluor 647 (targeting CGRP): 1:500 dilution
- Donkey anti-mouse Alexa Fluor 555 (targeting PGP9.5/Hu C/D): 1:500 dilution
8.2 Incubation with secondary antibody cocktail, protected from light. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 48 hours, gentle shaking)
8.3 Wash with PTwH. (Temperature: RT, Time: 5 × 1 hour, then 1 × overnight at 37 ℃, protected from light)

**9 Nuclear Counterstain with DAPI**
9.1 Incubation with DAPI (1 µg/mL in 1× PBS + 0.2% Tween-20) for tissue architecture reference (lobule boundaries, vascular walls). (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours, protected from light)
9.2 Wash with 1× PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 × 30 min)

**10 Second Dehydration (Pre-clearing, Methanol Gradient)**
10.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in H₂O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
10.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in H₂O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
10.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in H₂O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
10.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in H₂O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
10.5 Incubation with 100% methanol (anhydrous). (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 × 1 hour)

**11 Clearing with DCM**
11.1 Incubation with 100% DCM (dichloromethane, anhydrous) to complete delipidation and initiate RI shift; tissue should become fully transparent. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 × 15 min, gentle agitation)

**12 Refractive Index Matching with DBE**
12.1 Transfer tissue to glass vial. Incubation with 100% DBE (dibenzyl ether, Sigma-Aldrich 108014, n = 1.559) without shaking to avoid mechanical damage to cleared tissue. (Temperature: RT, Time: 4 hours, protected from light)
12.2 Replace with fresh 100% DBE. Incubation until tissue is fully transparent and RI-equilibrated (tissue should appear completely clear and glass-like). (Temperature: RT, Time: overnight ≥ 12 hours, protected from light)

**13 Storage and Pre-imaging Preparation**
13.1 Store cleared tissue in 100% DBE in sealed glass vials, protected from light. (Temperature: RT or 4 ℃, Time: stable for weeks to months)
13.2 For light-sheet fluorescence microscopy (LSFM): mount tissue in a custom glass cuvette or FEP tube filled with 100% DBE (RI = 1.559); use an objective compatible with DBE immersion (e.g., CLARITY/DBE-compatible long-working-distance objective, or use a silicone-oil objective with RI adapter).
13.3 For confocal imaging of sub-regions: place tissue on a glass-bottom dish, immerse in DBE, and seal with a coverslip using silicone grease. Use a 10× or 25× objective with appropriate RI correction collar set to ~1.56.
13.4 Imaging channels: DAPI (405 nm excitation / 420–480 nm emission), Alexa Fluor 555/PGP9.5-pan-neuronal (555 nm excitation / 570–620 nm emission), Alexa Fluor 647/CGRP-sensory (647 nm excitation / 660–720 nm emission). Acquire z-stacks with ≤ 5 µm step size for full 3D reconstruction and nerve fiber density/branching quantification.

**Chosen Method:** BoneClear
**Chosen Labeling:** [TH (酪氨酸羟化酶) + Alexa Fluor 647, β-III Tubulin (TUJ1) + Alexa Fluor 568, PGP9.5 + Alexa Fluor 488, MBP + Alexa Fluor 405, DAPI]

**Justification:** BoneClear is specifically designed for hard mineralized tissues (skull, long bones, bone marrow) and integrates decalcification, delipidation, and optical clearing into a single optimized pipeline compatible with immunolabeling. Unlike generic aqueous or solvent-based methods, BoneClear preserves antigenicity through a mild EDTA-based decalcification step followed by a detergent-based delipidation, enabling deep antibody penetration into dense cortical bone and bone marrow cavities. The method achieves high transparency in calcified tissues without the harsh organic solvents (e.g., DCM/DBE in uDISCO) that would destroy lipid-rich myelin sheaths and quench fluorescence critical for nerve fiber identification. The labeling panel is designed to comprehensively map the CNS–PNS neural architecture through bone: **β-III Tubulin (TUJ1)** serves as the primary pan-neuronal/axonal structural marker labeling all nerve fibers (sensory, autonomic, and motor axons) in bone canals, sutures, foramina, and meningeal surfaces; **TH** identifies sympathetic adrenergic fibers specifically (critical for bone innervation and marrow regulation); **PGP9.5** (protein gene product 9.5, a pan-neuronal ubiquitin hydrolase) provides orthogonal pan-axonal coverage to confirm fiber identity; **MBP** marks myelinated fiber segments to distinguish myelinated vs. unmyelinated nerve populations; and **DAPI** provides nuclear counterstaining for anatomical context (bone cells, marrow cells, meningeal cells). This multi-channel strategy allows unambiguous identification, tracing, and classification of nerve fibers across skull sutures, Haversian canals, nutrient foramina, bone marrow cavities, meningeal layers, and femoral cortex in 3D light-sheet imaging.

---

**Protocol Steps:**

**1 Sample Preparation and Pre-fixation Wash**
1.1 Retrieve PFA-fixed and post-fixed mouse skull (≈1.5 cm × 1 cm × 0.5 mm) and femur (≈1.5 cm) from storage. Rinse samples 3× with 1× PBS to remove residual fixative. (Temperature: RT, Time: 10 min per wash)
1.2 Transfer samples to 1× PBS containing 0.1% (wt/vol) sodium azide as antimicrobial agent for short-term holding if immunolabeling is not initiated immediately. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: up to 24 hours)

**2 Decalcification**
2.1 Incubate samples in 0.5 M EDTA (pH 7.4 adjusted with NaOH) in 1× PBS with gentle rocking. Replace EDTA solution every 48 hours. Continue until bone is fully decalcified (verified by needle-poke flexibility test and/or radiography). (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 7–14 days for skull; 14–21 days for femur)
2.2 Wash samples 3× with 1× PBS to remove residual EDTA. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 min per wash)

**3 Delipidation and Permeabilization**
3.1 Incubate samples in BoneClear delipidation solution I: 25% (vol/vol) N,N,N′,N′-tetrakis(2-hydroxypropyl)ethylenediamine (Quadrol) + 25% (wt/vol) urea + 15% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in ddH₂O, with gentle shaking. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 2 days)
3.2 Replace with fresh BoneClear delipidation solution I and continue incubation with gentle shaking. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 2 days)
3.3 Incubate samples in BoneClear delipidation solution II: 25% (vol/vol) Quadrol + 25% (wt/vol) urea + 15% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 + 10% (vol/vol) tert-butanol in ddH₂O, with gentle shaking. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 2 days)
3.4 Wash samples 3× with 1× PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (PBST). (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour per wash)

**4 Bleaching (Decolorization)**
4.1 Incubate samples in bleaching solution: 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ + 20% (wt/vol) urea + 25% (vol/vol) Quadrol in ddH₂O, with gentle shaking, to remove heme and endogenous pigments from bone marrow. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 2 days)
4.2 Wash samples 3× with PBST (1× PBS + 0.2% Triton X-100). (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour per wash)

**5 Blocking and Permeabilization for Immunolabeling**
5.1 Incubate samples in blocking/permeabilization buffer: 1× PBS + 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 + 10% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum (NDS) + 0.1% (wt/vol) heparin sodium + 0.02% (wt/vol) sodium azide, with gentle rocking. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 2 days)

**6 Primary Antibody Immunolabeling**
6.1 Prepare primary antibody cocktail in antibody incubation buffer (1× PBS + 0.5% Triton X-100 + 5% NDS + 0.1% heparin + 0.02% sodium azide):
- Rabbit anti-β-III Tubulin (TUJ1): 1:200 dilution
- Chicken anti-TH (tyrosine hydroxylase): 1:300 dilution
- Guinea pig anti-PGP9.5: 1:300 dilution
- Rat anti-MBP: 1:200 dilution
6.2 Incubate samples in primary antibody cocktail with gentle rocking. Replace antibody solution every 3 days with freshly prepared cocktail. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7–10 days for skull; 10–14 days for femur)
6.3 Wash samples 5× with PBST (1× PBS + 0.2% Triton X-100 + 0.1% heparin). (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours per wash)
6.4 Perform additional overnight wash in PBST with gentle rocking to ensure complete removal of unbound primary antibody. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)

**7 Secondary Antibody Immunolabeling**
7.1 Prepare secondary antibody cocktail in antibody incubation buffer (1× PBS + 0.5% Triton X-100 + 5% NDS + 0.1% heparin + 0.02% sodium azide):
- Donkey anti-rabbit IgG conjugated Alexa Fluor 568 (for TUJ1): 1:400 dilution
- Donkey anti-chicken IgY conjugated Alexa Fluor 647 (for TH): 1:400 dilution
- Donkey anti-guinea pig IgG conjugated Alexa Fluor 488 (for PGP9.5): 1:400 dilution
- Donkey anti-rat IgG conjugated Alexa Fluor 405 (for MBP): 1:400 dilution
7.2 Incubate samples in secondary antibody cocktail with gentle rocking, protected from light. Replace solution every 3 days. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 5–7 days)
7.3 Wash samples 5× with PBST (1× PBS + 0.2% Triton X-100 + 0.1% heparin), protected from light. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours per wash)
7.4 Perform additional overnight wash in PBST with gentle rocking, protected from light. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)

**8 Nuclear Counterstaining**
8.1 Incubate samples in DAPI solution (2 µg/mL DAPI in 1× PBS + 0.2% Triton X-100), protected from light. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)
8.2 Wash samples 3× with 1× PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 min per wash)

**9 Optical Clearing — Gradient Dehydration**
9.1 Incubate samples in BoneClear clearing solution A1: 25% (vol/vol) Quadrol + 25% (wt/vol) urea in ddH₂O (RI ≈ 1.44), with gentle shaking, protected from light. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 1 day)
9.2 Incubate samples in BoneClear clearing solution A2: 40% (vol/vol) Quadrol + 40% (wt/vol) urea in ddH₂O (RI ≈ 1.46), with gentle shaking, protected from light. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 1 day)
9.3 Incubate samples in BoneClear clearing solution A3: 55% (vol/vol) Quadrol + 55% (wt/vol) urea in ddH₂O (RI ≈ 1.48), with gentle shaking, protected from light. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 1 day)

**10 Refractive Index Matching**
10.1 Incubate samples in BoneClear RI matching solution (RIMS): 75% (vol/vol) Quadrol + 25% (wt/vol) urea in ddH₂O, adjusted to RI = 1.520 ± 0.002 (verified by refractometer), with gentle shaking, protected from light. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 2 days)
10.2 Replace RIMS with fresh solution and continue incubation until samples are fully transparent (visually confirmed). (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 1–2 additional days)
10.3 Verify final RI of RIMS with a calibrated Abbe refractometer before imaging. Target RI = 1.520 to match objective immersion medium. (Temperature: RT, Time: 5 min)

**11 Sample Mounting and Imaging Preparation**
11.1 Transfer cleared samples into custom 3D-printed or FEP-tube imaging chambers filled with BoneClear RIMS (RI = 1.520). Orient skull flat (meningeal surface up) and femur longitudinally for axial light-sheet illumination. Seal chambers to prevent evaporation. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 min)
11.2 Allow samples to equilibrate in imaging chamber to eliminate any residual RI gradients or air bubbles. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)
11.3 Image using a light-sheet fluorescence microscope (LSFM) equipped with a RI = 1.52-compatible long-working-distance objective (e.g., 4×/0.35 NA or 10×/0.6 NA CLARITY/RIMS-compatible objective) using the following channel assignments:
- 405 nm laser → Alexa Fluor 405 (MBP, myelinated fibers)
- 488 nm laser → Alexa Fluor 488 (PGP9.5, pan-axonal)
- 561 nm laser → Alexa Fluor 568 (TUJ1, pan-neuronal/axonal)
- 638 nm laser → Alexa Fluor 647 (TH, sympathetic fibers)
- 405 nm laser (low power) → DAPI (nuclei)
(Temperature: RT, Time: per imaging session)

**12 Post-imaging Storage**
12.1 Store cleared and imaged samples in BoneClear RIMS in sealed containers, protected from light. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: up to 6 months)

**Chosen Method:** BoneClear
**Chosen Labeling:** [CGRP (Marker: mapped to anti-CGRP antibody) + Alexa Fluor 647, PGP9.5 + Alexa Fluor 568, CD31 + Alexa Fluor 488, DAPI]

**Justification:** BoneClear is specifically designed for decalcification-free optical clearing of intact mineralized bone tissues (calvaria, femur, bone marrow cavity), making it the only method in the list purpose-built for this exact tissue type. It combines EDTA-free chemical clearing with RI matching optimized for dense, calcified matrices, preserving antigenicity for immunolabeling. For the scientific goals: (1) Anti-CGRP antibody (secondary: Alexa Fluor 647) serves as the primary marker for CGRP-positive sensory nerve fibers — this cannot be replaced by a generic neural tracer because CGRP identity must be confirmed immunochemically. (2) PGP9.5 (protein gene product 9.5, a pan-neuronal marker equivalent to Hu C/D / PGP9.5 in the marker list; secondary: Alexa Fluor 568) labels the entire pan-neuronal network to reveal total innervation density, branching patterns, terminal coverage, and regional enrichment across sutures, foramina, marrow cavities, meningeal junctions, and long bone interiors. (3) CD31 (Alexa Fluor 488) as an auxiliary vascular channel to delineate vascular-neural spatial relationships in bone marrow and meningeal compartments. (4) DAPI as nuclear counterstain to define tissue architecture and regional boundaries. BoneClear's aqueous-based, mild delipidation protocol preserves both the calcified bone matrix and fluorescent epitopes, enabling light-sheet microscopy of samples up to 1.5 cm in length.

---

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Post-fixation Verification and Pre-treatment
1.1 Confirm samples (calvaria ~1.5 cm × 1 cm × 0.5 mm; femur ~1.5 cm; meninges) are fully post-fixed in 4% (wt/vol) PFA in 0.01 M PBS. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)
1.2 Wash samples 3× with 0.01 M PBS to remove residual PFA. (Temperature: RT, Time: 10 minutes per wash)
1.3 Transfer samples to 1× PBS containing 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 for initial permeabilization. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)

2 Decalcification (BoneClear-compatible mild EDTA step for femur and calvaria)
2.1 Incubate femur and calvaria in 10% (wt/vol) EDTA (pH 7.4 in 0.01 M PBS) with gentle rocking. Meninges and isolated bone marrow tissue skip to Step 3. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 5 days)
2.2 Replace EDTA solution daily. Check decalcification progress by needle-probe flexibility test each day. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours per replacement)
2.3 Wash decalcified samples 3× with 0.01 M PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 15 minutes per wash)

3 Delipidation (BoneClear Step 1 — Quadrol-based clearing solution)
3.1 Incubate all samples in BoneClear Clearing Solution A: 25% (wt/vol) N,N,N′,N′-tetrakis(2-hydroxypropyl)ethylenediamine (Quadrol) in distilled water, pH adjusted to 9.0–9.5 with HCl, with gentle shaking. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 2 days)
3.2 Replace Clearing Solution A with fresh solution and continue incubation. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 2 days)
3.3 Wash samples 3× with 0.01 M PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 20 minutes per wash)

4 Bleaching (for autofluorescence reduction in mineralized bone)
4.1 Incubate samples in freshly prepared bleaching solution: 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in 0.01 M PBS. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)
4.2 Wash samples 3× with 0.01 M PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 15 minutes per wash)

5 Enhanced Permeabilization for Immunolabeling
5.1 Incubate samples in permeabilization/blocking buffer: 0.01 M PBS containing 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100, 0.1% (wt/vol) Tween-20, 0.1% (wt/vol) heparin sodium, 5% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum (NDS), and 0.02% (wt/vol) sodium azide. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 48 hours)

6 Primary Antibody Incubation
6.1 Incubate samples in primary antibody cocktail diluted in antibody incubation buffer (0.01 M PBS, 0.2% Triton X-100, 0.1% Tween-20, 0.1% heparin, 3% NDS, 0.02% sodium azide):
— Rabbit anti-CGRP antibody at 1:200 dilution
— Rabbit anti-PGP9.5 antibody at 1:300 dilution (use host-species-compatible pair; if both rabbit, use sequential labeling — see Note below)
— Rat anti-CD31 (PECAM1) antibody at 1:200 dilution. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days)

*Note: If anti-CGRP and anti-PGP9.5 are both raised in rabbit, perform sequential primary/secondary labeling: complete CGRP labeling (Steps 6–7 first round) then strip/block and repeat for PGP9.5, or use antibodies from different host species (e.g., rabbit anti-CGRP + guinea pig anti-PGP9.5 + rat anti-CD31).*

6.2 Wash samples 5× with washing buffer (0.01 M PBS, 0.2% Triton X-100, 0.1% Tween-20, 0.1% heparin). (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour per wash)

7 Secondary Antibody and Nuclear Stain Incubation
7.1 Incubate samples in secondary antibody cocktail diluted in antibody incubation buffer:
— Donkey anti-rabbit Alexa Fluor 647 at 1:400 dilution (for CGRP)
— Donkey anti-guinea pig Alexa Fluor 568 at 1:400 dilution (for PGP9.5)
— Donkey anti-rat Alexa Fluor 488 at 1:400 dilution (for CD31)

— 488 nm excitation / 525 nm emission: Alexa Fluor 488 / CD31 (vasculature)

model_response:
**Chosen Method:** BoneClear
**Chosen Labeling:** [CGRP (via anti-CGRP antibody) + Alexa Fluor 647, PGP9.5 (pan-neuronal) + Alexa Fluor 568, Lectin + Alexa Fluor 488 (vascular lumen), DAPI (nuclear counterstain)]

**Justification:** BoneClear was specifically developed for optical clearing of intact bone tissues (calvaria, long bones) and is compatible with decalcified and non-decalcified bone, bone marrow, and associated soft tissues. It employs a mild alkaline/detergent-based delipidation pipeline that preserves antigenicity for immunolabeling, making it ideal for multi-target IHC in dense mineralized tissue. Compared to iDISCO+ or uDISCO (which use harsh organic solvents damaging bone marrow architecture and meningeal integrity), BoneClear maintains structural integrity of the bone marrow cavity, vascular channels (Haversian/Volkmann canals), and meningeal layers. CGRP antibody labels peptidergic sensory fibers (CGRP+ nociceptors innervating bone and meninges); PGP9.5 provides pan-neuronal coverage to capture all nerve fibers regardless of subtype; Lectin (e.g., tomato lectin, Lycopersicon esculentum) perfused or applied post-fixation labels vascular endothelial lumens to delineate vascular channels as anatomical reference; DAPI provides nuclear/structural context for bone marrow cellularity and meningeal cell layers. This four-channel strategy enables simultaneous 3D mapping of sensory nerve trajectories relative to vascular conduits, bone canals, marrow cavities, and meningeal interfaces.

---

**Protocol Steps:**

**1 Sample Preparation and Pre-fixation Vascular Labeling**

1.1 Transcardial perfusion with ice-cold PBS (0.01 M, pH 7.4) until effluent runs clear, followed by perfusion with 4% (wt/vol) paraformaldehyde (PFA) in PBS. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: perfusion ~10 min total)

1.2 Immediately after PFA perfusion, perfuse with Lectin–Alexa Fluor 488 conjugate (100 µg in 1 mL PBS, Lycopersicon esculentum lectin, Vector Labs) to label vascular lumens in situ before tissue extraction. (Temperature: RT, Time: 5 min perfusion, allow 10 min circulation)

1.3 Dissect calvaria (with attached meninges), femur, and tibia. For calvaria, carefully retain the dura mater on the inner surface. For long bones, keep periosteum intact. Post-fix all samples in 4% PFA/PBS. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 24 hours)

1.4 Wash samples 3× in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 min each wash)

---

**2 Mild Decalcification**

2.1 Incubate samples in 0.5 M EDTA (pH 7.4 in PBS, sterile-filtered) with gentle rocking. Replace EDTA solution every 2 days. Monitor decalcification by radiography or needle-test flexibility. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 7–14 days for calvaria; 14–21 days for femur/tibia)

2.2 Wash samples 3× in PBS to remove residual EDTA. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour each wash)

---

**3 Permeabilization and Blocking (BoneClear Pre-treatment)**

3.1 Incubate samples in BoneClear Permeabilization Buffer [PBS containing 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100, 0.1% (wt/vol) sodium deoxycholate, 0.05% (wt/vol) sodium azide] with gentle rocking. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 48 hours)

3.2 Wash samples 3× in PBS-T [PBS + 0.1% (vol/vol) Tween-20]. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour each wash)

3.3 Incubate samples in Blocking Buffer [PBS containing 5% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum, 0.3% (vol/vol) Triton X-100, 0.05% (wt/vol) sodium azide] with gentle rocking. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)

---

**4 Primary Antibody Immunolabeling**

4.1 Incubate samples in primary antibody cocktail diluted in Antibody Diluent Buffer [PBS + 5% normal donkey serum + 0.3% Triton X-100 + 0.05% sodium azide]:
- Rabbit anti-CGRP (1:500; e.g., Sigma C8198 or Abcam ab81887)
- Rabbit anti-PGP9.5 / UCHL1 (1:400; e.g., Abcam ab8189) — use species-matched secondaries from different host species; alternatively use Guinea pig anti-PGP9.5 to allow dual labeling
with gentle rocking. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 5–7 days)

4.2 Wash samples 5× in PBS-T [PBS + 0.1% Tween-20] with gentle rocking. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours each wash)

---

**5 Secondary Antibody Labeling**

5.1 Incubate samples in secondary antibody cocktail diluted in Antibody Diluent Buffer:
- Donkey anti-Rabbit IgG–Alexa Fluor 647 (1:400; for CGRP detection)
- Donkey anti-Guinea pig IgG–Alexa Fluor 568 (1:400; for PGP9.5 detection)
with gentle rocking, protected from light. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 3–5 days)

5.2 Wash samples 5× in PBS-T with gentle rocking, protected from light. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours each wash)

---

**6 Nuclear Counterstain**

6.1 Incubate samples in DAPI solution (5 µg/mL in PBS) with gentle rocking, protected from light. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)

6.2 Wash samples 3× in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour each wash)

---

**7 Delipidation (BoneClear Clearing Step 1)**

7.1 Incubate samples in BoneClear Delipidation Solution A [25% (vol/vol) N,N,N′,N′-tetrakis(2-hydroxypropyl)ethylenediamine (Quadrol) in ddH₂O, pH adjusted to 9.0 with HCl] with gentle shaking. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)

7.2 Incubate samples in BoneClear Delipidation Solution B [10% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 + 25% (vol/vol) Quadrol in ddH₂O, pH 9.0] with gentle shaking. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 48 hours)

7.3 Wash samples 3× in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour each wash)

---

**8 Dehydration (BoneClear Clearing Step 2)**

8.1 Incubate samples in 30% (vol/vol) tert-butanol (TBA) in ddH₂O. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 4 hours)

8.2 Incubate samples in 50% (vol/vol) TBA in ddH₂O. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 4 hours)

8.3 Incubate samples in 70% (vol/vol) TBA in ddH₂O. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 4 hours)

8.4 Incubate samples in 80% (vol/vol) TBA in ddH₂O. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 4 hours)

8.5 Incubate samples in 90% (vol/vol) TBA in ddH₂O. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 4 hours)

8.6 Incubate samples in 96% (vol/vol) TBA in ddH₂O. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 4 hours)

8.7 Incubate samples in 100% TBA (anhydrous). (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 4 hours)

8.8 Repeat 100% TBA incubation (second change, anhydrous). (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 4 hours)

---

**9 Refractive Index Matching and Final Clearing**

9.1 Incubate samples in BoneClear RI Matching Solution [BABB-D: benzyl alcohol : benzyl benzoate : diphenyl ether = 3:1:1 (vol/vol/vol), RI ≈ 1.559] in glass vials, protected from light, without shaking. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)

9.2 Replace with fresh BoneClear RI Matching Solution (BABB-D, RI ≈ 1.559) and continue incubation until samples are fully transparent (visually clear). (Temperature: RT, Time: 24–48 hours)

---

**10 Sample Mounting and Storage Prior to Imaging**

10.1 Transfer cleared samples into glass-bottom imaging chambers or custom 3D-printed holders filled with BABB-D RI matching solution (RI ≈ 1.559). Seal chambers with optical adhesive to prevent evaporation. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1–2 hours equilibration)

10.2 Store mounted samples in sealed glass vials containing BABB-D, wrapped in aluminum foil, until imaging. (Temperature: RT, protected from light, Time: up to 2 weeks)

---

**11 Light-Sheet Fluorescence Microscopy Imaging**

11.1 Image samples using a light-sheet fluorescence microscope (e.g., LaVision BioTec Ultramicroscope II or Miltenyi LSFM) equipped with an RI-corrected dipping objective (e.g., 4×/0.35 NA or 12×/0.53 NA, corrected for RI 1.52–1.56). Use immersion medium BABB-D (RI ≈ 1.559) in the sample chamber. Acquire four channels sequentially:
- Channel 1: 488 nm excitation / 525 nm emission (Lectin–AF488, vascular lumen)
- Channel 2: 561 nm excitation / 593 nm emission (PGP9.5–AF568, pan-neuronal)
- Channel 3: 638 nm excitation / 680 nm emission (CGRP–AF647, sensory fibers)
- Channel 4: 405 nm excitation / 450 nm emission (DAPI, nuclei/structure)
(Temperature: RT, Time: per sample acquisition ~2–6 hours depending on resolution and volume)

11.2 Perform 3D image reconstruction and co-registration of all four channels using Imaris, Arivis, or Fiji/BigStitcher to generate volumetric maps of nerve fiber trajectories relative to vascular channels, bone canals, marrow cavities, and meningeal interfaces. (Temperature: RT, Time: post-acquisition analysis)

我在进行小鼠颅骨透明化实验时遇到问题：按照标准 BoneClear protocol 操作，固定后进行甲醇梯度脱水和 bleaching，然后进行远红荧光二抗孵育和 RI matching。结果骨组织仍然不透明，无法观察骨内结构，且远红信号很弱。该流程可能缺少充分脱钙、骨基质软化、深层透化和长时间抗体渗透，也可能因 bleaching 或脱水步骤过强导致抗原和荧光信号受损。请根据上述科学目标，在不引入给定标记物列表之外靶点或表外荧光团的前提下，重新选择或调整荧光/标记策略与组织透明方法。修正版应适合矿化骨组织脱钙、骨髓和脑膜结构保留、神经纤维双信号检测、低背景、深层抗体渗透和三维成像。

model_response:
**Chosen Method:** PEGASOS

**Chosen Labeling:** [Alexa Fluor (anti-CGRP primary + Alexa Fluor secondary), Alexa Fluor (anti-PGP9.5/Tuj1 primary + Alexa Fluor secondary), DAPI]

> Specifically: **PGP9.5** (pan-neuronal marker for all nerve fibers) + **β-III Tubulin (TUJ1)** (pan-axonal, labels coarser axon structures) as dual neural markers, conjugated to two spectrally distinct **Alexa Fluor** secondaries (e.g., Alexa Fluor 555 and Alexa Fluor 647); **DAPI** for nuclear/structural counterstain. CGRP is not in the provided Marker list, so the closest permitted pan-neuronal surrogates are **PGP9.5** and **β-III Tubulin (TUJ1)**, which together cover fine sensory fibers and larger axon trunks as required by the scientific goal.

---

**Justification:**
PEGASOS (PolyEthylene Glycol-associated solvent system) is specifically optimized for **mineralized/hard tissues** including bone, teeth, and skull. It incorporates a **decalcification-compatible workflow** using EDTA within the clearing pipeline, preserves both lipid-soluble and aqueous fluorescence signals, achieves high RI matching (RI ≈ 1.52) suitable for light-sheet microscopy, and maintains structural integrity of bone marrow, meninges, and periosteal/endosteal nerve networks. Unlike BoneClear (which relies on harsh methanol bleaching that damages far-red fluorophores and antigen epitopes) or iDISCO+ (which is not optimized for mineralized tissue), PEGASOS uses a PEG-based organic solvent system that is gentler on antigens and fluorophores. The protocol integrates EDTA-based decalcification before delipidation, enabling deep antibody penetration into cortical bone canals, bone marrow cavities, and meningeal interfaces. PGP9.5 labels the entire peripheral and central nerve fiber network (including fine unmyelinated fibers analogous to CGRP+ sensory fibers), while TUJ1/β-III Tubulin labels larger axon structures, fulfilling the dual-channel neural mapping requirement. Alexa Fluor dyes (e.g., AF555 and AF647) are robust under PEGASOS organic solvents when properly cross-linked. DAPI provides nuclear counterstain for anatomical reference of bone sutures, foramina, marrow cavities, and meningeal layers.

---

## Protocol Steps

### 0 Pre-clearing Verification
0.1 Confirm samples (mouse calvaria ~1.5 cm × 1 cm × 0.5 mm; femur ~1.5 cm; associated bone marrow and meninges) have been post-fixed in 4% PFA/PBS. Rinse 3× in 1× PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 10 min per wash)

---

### 1 Decalcification (EDTA-based, integrated pre-clearing step)
1.1 Immerse samples in 0.5 M EDTA (pH 7.4 in PBS, sterile-filtered), with gentle rocking. Change EDTA solution every 2 days. Monitor calvaria flexibility by gentle bending; femur requires longer treatment. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 5–7 days for calvaria; 10–14 days for femur)
1.2 Verify decalcification completion by X-ray or by confirming tissue pliability. Rinse samples 3× in 1× PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 15 min per wash)

---

### 2 Permeabilization and Blocking (Pre-immunolabeling)
2.1 Incubation in permeabilization/blocking buffer: PBS containing 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100, 0.1% (wt/vol) saponin, 0.2% (wt/vol) gelatin, 5% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum (NDS), and 0.02% (wt/vol) sodium azide. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 48 hours, with gentle rocking)

---

### 3 Primary Antibody Incubation
3.1 Incubation with primary antibody cocktail in antibody dilution buffer (PBS + 0.2% Triton X-100 + 0.1% saponin + 2% NDS + 0.02% sodium azide):
- Rabbit anti-PGP9.5 (1:500; e.g., Abcam ab108986)
- Mouse anti-β-III Tubulin/TUJ1 (1:500; e.g., BioLegend 801201)
Ensure sufficient volume to fully submerge samples. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 5–7 days, with gentle rocking on orbital shaker)
3.2 Wash samples in PTwH buffer (PBS + 0.2% Tween-20 + 10 µg/mL heparin), 5 × 1 hour washes with rocking. (Temperature: RT, Time: 5 hours total)

---

### 4 Secondary Antibody Incubation
4.1 Incubation with secondary antibody cocktail in antibody dilution buffer (same as 3.1):
- Donkey anti-Rabbit Alexa Fluor 647 (1:500; labels PGP9.5 channel)
- Donkey anti-Mouse Alexa Fluor 555 (1:500; labels TUJ1 channel)
Protect from light. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 4–5 days, with gentle rocking, foil-wrapped)
4.2 Wash in PTwH buffer, 5 × 1 hour washes with rocking, protected from light. (Temperature: RT, Time: 5 hours total)

---

### 5 Nuclear Counterstain (DAPI)
5.1 Incubation with DAPI (5 µg/mL in PBS). (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours, protected from light)
5.2 Rinse 3× in 1× PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 15 min per wash)

---

### 6 Dehydration (tert-Butanol gradient, PEGASOS step 1)
6.1 Incubation in 30% (vol/vol) tert-butanol (tB) in ddH₂O. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 4 hours)
6.2 Incubation in 50% (vol/vol) tert-butanol in ddH₂O. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 4 hours)
6.3 Incubation in 70% (vol/vol) tert-butanol in ddH₂O. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 8 hours)
6.4 Incubation in 80% (vol/vol) tert-butanol in ddH₂O. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 8 hours)
6.5 Incubation in 90% (vol/vol) tert-butanol in ddH₂O. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 8 hours)
6.6 Incubation in 96% (vol/vol) tert-butanol in ddH₂O. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 8 hours)
6.7 Incubation in 100% tert-butanol (anhydrous). (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 8 hours)
6.8 Repeat 100% tert-butanol incubation (fresh solution). (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 8 hours)

---

### 7 Delipidation (PEGASOS clearing solution)
7.1 Prepare PEGASOS clearing solution: PEG-associated solvent (BB-PEG solution): mix 75 g polyethylene glycol diacrylate (PEG-DA, MW 250) + 25 g Quadrol (N,N,N′,N′-tetrakis(2-hydroxypropyl)ethylenediamine) + 0.4 g diphenyl ether (DPE) per 100 g total; adjust to RI = 1.52 using refractometer. Warm to 37 ℃ before use.
7.2 Incubation in PEGASOS clearing solution (first exchange). (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours, with gentle rocking, protected from light)
7.3 Incubation in fresh PEGASOS clearing solution (second exchange). (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours, with gentle rocking, protected from light)
7.4 Incubation in fresh PEGASOS clearing solution (third exchange) until tissue becomes visually transparent. For femur cortical bone, extend to additional 24–48 hours as needed. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24–48 hours, protected from light)

---

### 8 Refractive Index Matching and Final Equilibration
8.1 Transfer cleared samples into PEGASOS RI-matching solution (same BB-PEG formulation, RI = 1.52, confirmed by refractometer). Incubate until no further optical change is observed (tissue appears uniformly transparent). (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours, protected from light)
8.2 Replace with fresh RI-matching solution and confirm RI = 1.52 ± 0.005 with refractometer. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours, protected from light)

---

### 9 Sample Mounting for 3D Imaging
9.1 Mount cleared samples in custom imaging chambers (e.g., FEP tube or glass-bottom dish) filled with PEGASOS RI-matching solution (RI = 1.52). Seal with optical adhesive or vacuum grease to prevent evaporation and bubble formation. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 min)
9.2 Allow sample to settle and equilibrate in mounting medium before imaging. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours, protected from light)

---

### 10 Imaging Parameters (Guidance)
10.1 Acquire on light-sheet fluorescence microscope (LSFM) or confocal microscope equipped with an objective compatible with RI = 1.52 immersion medium (e.g., CLARITY/PEGASOS-compatible 10× or 25× objective). Use the following channel assignments:
- DAPI channel (405 nm excitation): nuclear/structural reference for bone sutures, foramina, marrow, meninges
- Alexa Fluor 555 channel (561 nm excitation): TUJ1/β-III Tubulin — coarse axon trunks and nerve bundles
- Alexa Fluor 647 channel (638 nm excitation): PGP9.5 — pan-neuronal fine fiber network including sensory fibers
(Temperature: RT, Time: per imaging session)
10.2 For long-term storage prior to imaging, keep samples in sealed containers with PEGASOS RI-matching solution at 4 ℃, protected from light. Stable for up to 4 weeks. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: up to 4 weeks)

model_response:
**Chosen Method:** BoneClear
**Chosen Labeling:** [TH (酪氨酸羟化酶) + Alexa Fluor 488, NPY + Alexa Fluor 647, CD31 (PECAM1) + Alexa Fluor 568, DAPI]

**Justification:** BoneClear is specifically designed for hard mineralized tissues (bone), incorporating a decalcification step that renders dense cortical and trabecular bone optically transparent while preserving antigenicity and fluorescence signals within the marrow cavity. This makes it uniquely suited for femur, tibia, and calvaria samples. For the scientific goal of mapping sympathetic innervation in the bone marrow niche: (1) **TH (tyrosine hydroxylase)** is the canonical marker for noradrenergic sympathetic nerve terminals and fibers — it directly identifies the norepinephrine-synthesizing sympathetic endings that regulate the hematopoietic microenvironment; (2) **NPY (neuropeptide Y)** labels peptidergic sympathetic fibers that co-transmit with norepinephrine, enabling discrimination of noradrenergic vs. peptidergic sympathetic fiber subtypes; (3) **CD31 (PECAM-1)** labels the sinusoidal and arterial vasculature, providing the perivascular spatial reference frame essential for analyzing nerve–vessel relationships in the endosteal and perivascular niches; (4) **DAPI** labels nuclei to delineate the overall marrow cellularity and hematopoietic cell-rich zones. This four-channel strategy directly addresses all spatial relationship questions (marrow cavity, endosteum, perivascular, hematopoietic zones) without substituting vascular or nuclear markers for nerve identity.

---

**Protocol Steps:**

**1 Post-fixation Verification and Pre-treatment**
1.1 Confirm samples (intact femur, tibia, calvaria) have been post-fixed in 4% (wt/vol) paraformaldehyde (PFA) in 0.01 M PBS (pH 7.4). If not, immerse in 4% PFA/PBS. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 24 hours)
1.2 Wash samples 3× in 0.01 M PBS (pH 7.4) with gentle rocking to remove residual PFA. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 × 30 minutes)

**2 Decalcification**
2.1 Immerse samples in 10% (wt/vol) EDTA (ethylenediaminetetraacetic acid, disodium salt) in 0.01 M PBS (pH 7.4), with gentle rocking on an orbital shaker. Change EDTA solution every 2 days. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 14 days for femur/tibia; 7 days for calvaria)
2.2 Monitor decalcification completion by needle-penetration test or X-ray verification. Bone should be pliable and translucent at the cortex.
2.3 Wash samples 3× in 0.01 M PBS (pH 7.4) with gentle rocking. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 × 1 hour)

**3 Delipidation and Permeabilization**
3.1 Incubate samples in BoneClear delipidation solution: 25% (vol/vol) N,N,N′,N′-tetrakis(2-hydroxypropyl)ethylenediamine (Quadrol) in ddH₂O, with gentle shaking. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)
3.2 Replace with fresh BoneClear delipidation solution (25% Quadrol in ddH₂O). (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)
3.3 Wash samples 3× in 0.01 M PBS (pH 7.4) with gentle rocking. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 × 1 hour)
3.4 Incubate samples in permeabilization/blocking buffer: 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100, 10% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum (NDS), 0.01% (wt/vol) sodium azide in 0.01 M PBS (pH 7.4), with gentle rocking. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)

**4 Primary Antibody Labeling**
4.1 Prepare primary antibody cocktail in antibody incubation buffer [0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100, 5% (vol/vol) NDS, 0.01% (wt/vol) sodium azide in 0.01 M PBS (pH 7.4)]:
- Rabbit anti-TH (tyrosine hydroxylase): 1:500 dilution
- Sheep anti-NPY (neuropeptide Y): 1:400 dilution
- Rat anti-CD31 (PECAM-1, clone MEC13.3): 1:300 dilution
4.2 Immerse decalcified samples fully in primary antibody cocktail solution with gentle rocking. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 7 days for femur/tibia; 5 days for calvaria)
4.3 Wash samples 5× in 0.01 M PBS containing 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (PBST) with gentle rocking. (Temperature: RT, Time: 5 × 2 hours)

**5 Secondary Antibody Labeling**
5.1 Prepare secondary antibody cocktail in antibody incubation buffer [0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100, 5% (vol/vol) NDS, 0.01% (wt/vol) sodium azide in 0.01 M PBS (pH 7.4)]:
- Donkey anti-rabbit IgG conjugated to Alexa Fluor 488: 1:500 dilution (for TH)
- Donkey anti-sheep IgG conjugated to Alexa Fluor 647: 1:500 dilution (for NPY)
- Donkey anti-rat IgG conjugated to Alexa Fluor 568: 1:500 dilution (for CD31)
5.2 Immerse samples in secondary antibody cocktail with gentle rocking, protected from light. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 5 days for femur/tibia; 3 days for calvaria)
5.3 Wash samples 5× in PBST (0.2% Triton X-100 in 0.01 M PBS) with gentle rocking, protected from light. (Temperature: RT, Time: 5 × 2 hours)

**6 Nuclear Counterstaining**
6.1 Incubate samples in DAPI solution [5 μg/mL DAPI in 0.01 M PBS] with gentle rocking, protected from light. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)
6.2 Wash samples 3× in 0.01 M PBS with gentle rocking, protected from light. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 × 1 hour)

**7 Dehydration**
7.1 Incubate samples in 30% (vol/vol) tetrahydrofuran (THF) in ddH₂O (freshly prepared, stabilizer-free THF), with gentle shaking, protected from light. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)
7.2 Incubate samples in 50% (vol/vol) THF in ddH₂O, with gentle shaking, protected from light. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)
7.3 Incubate samples in 70% (vol/vol) THF in ddH₂O, with gentle shaking, protected from light. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)
7.4 Incubate samples in 80% (vol/vol) THF in ddH₂O, with gentle shaking, protected from light. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)
7.5 Incubate samples in 100% (vol/vol) THF (anhydrous), with gentle shaking, protected from light. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)
7.6 Repeat incubation in fresh 100% (vol/vol) THF (anhydrous), with gentle shaking, protected from light. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)

**8 Optical Clearing and Refractive Index Matching**
8.1 Transfer samples from 100% THF directly into BoneClear clearing/RI-matching solution: 75% (vol/vol) benzyl benzoate (BB) / 25% (vol/vol) benzyl alcohol (BA) (BABB, RI ≈ 1.559), with gentle shaking, protected from light. (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours)
8.2 Replace with fresh BABB (75% BB / 25% BA) solution and continue incubation until samples are fully transparent (visually confirmed), protected from light. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12–24 hours)
8.3 Verify optical transparency: samples should appear fully clear with no visible opaque regions in the marrow cavity or cortical bone.

**9 Storage and Pre-imaging Preparation**
9.1 Transfer cleared samples into fresh BABB (75% BB / 25% BA, RI ≈ 1.559) in a sealed glass vial or imaging chamber, protected from light. Store at RT until imaging. (Temperature: RT, Time: up to 4 weeks)
9.2 For light-sheet fluorescence microscopy (LSFM): mount samples in BABB-compatible glass-bottom imaging chambers or custom 3D-printed holders filled with BABB. Ensure the sample is fully submerged and immobilized with no air bubbles.
9.3 For confocal microscopy: mount samples on glass slides with BABB as the mounting medium, apply a coverslip sealed with two-component epoxy glue, and allow to cure before imaging. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours curing)
9.4 Use BABB-compatible objectives (e.g., CLARITY/LSFM objectives with RI correction collar set to 1.56, or dipping objectives compatible with organic solvents). Acquire 3D z-stacks with the following channel assignments:
- DAPI: 405 nm excitation (nuclear counterstain, marrow cellularity reference)
- Alexa Fluor 488 (TH): 488 nm excitation (noradrenergic sympathetic terminals)
- Alexa Fluor 568 (CD31): 561 nm excitation (vasculature, perivascular niche reference)
- Alexa Fluor 647 (NPY): 638 nm excitation (peptidergic sympathetic fibers)

**Chosen Method:** BoneClear
**Chosen Labeling:** [TH (酪氨酸羟化酶) + Alexa Fluor 647, NPY + Alexa Fluor 568, CD31 (PECAM1) + Alexa Fluor 488, DAPI]

**Justification:** BoneClear is specifically designed for decalcification-integrated optical clearing of intact bone tissues (femur, tibia, calvaria), enabling whole-mount immunolabeling and clearing of mineralized tissues without destroying bone marrow architecture. It combines EDTA-based decalcification with a CUBIC-derivative aqueous clearing pipeline optimized for bone, preserving antigenicity for immunofluorescence. For the scientific goal of simultaneously visualizing catecholaminergic (TH) and peptidergic (NPY) sympathetic nerve terminals in bone marrow, TH antibody (Alexa Fluor 647) serves as the catecholaminergic marker and NPY antibody (Alexa Fluor 568) serves as the peptidergic marker — both are well-validated sympathetic nerve terminal markers in bone marrow. CD31 (Alexa Fluor 488) labels sinusoidal vasculature as a structural reference for spatial distance analysis. DAPI labels nuclei to delineate hematopoietic cell-rich zones and endosteal regions. This multi-channel strategy enables quantitative analysis of nerve fiber density, branching complexity, terminal coverage, and spatial relationships with vasculature, endosteum, and hematopoietic niches across femur, tibia, and calvaria bone marrow compartments.

---

**Protocol Steps:**

**1 Post-fixation Wash**
1.1 Wash fixed bone samples (femur, tibia, calvaria; already PFA-fixed) with 1× PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 × 30 minutes)

**2 Decalcification**
2.1 Incubation with 10% (wt/vol) EDTA in PBS (pH 7.4) with gentle rocking to decalcify bone. Replace EDTA solution every 2 days. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 14 days for femur/tibia; 7 days for calvaria)
2.2 Verify decalcification completion by X-ray or needle-penetration test. Wash with 1× PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 × 1 hour)

**3 Permeabilization and Blocking**
3.1 Incubation with permeabilization/blocking solution: 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100, 10% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum, 0.1% (wt/vol) sodium azide, 0.2% (wt/vol) BSA in PBS (PTwH-based blocking buffer). (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 48 hours)

**4 Primary Antibody Labeling**
4.1 Incubation with primary antibody cocktail in antibody diluent (0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100, 5% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum, 0.1% (wt/vol) sodium azide in PBS):
- Anti-TH (rabbit polyclonal, 1:500; catecholaminergic sympathetic marker)
- Anti-NPY (goat polyclonal, 1:400; peptidergic sympathetic marker)
- Anti-CD31/PECAM1 (rat monoclonal, 1:300; vascular reference)
with gentle rocking. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days)
4.2 Wash with PTwH (0.2% (vol/vol) Tween-20, 0.1% (wt/vol) heparin in PBS). (Temperature: RT, Time: 5 × 2 hours)

**5 Secondary Antibody Labeling**
5.1 Incubation with secondary antibody cocktail in antibody diluent (same as 4.1):
- Donkey anti-rabbit Alexa Fluor 647 (1:500; for TH)
- Donkey anti-goat Alexa Fluor 568 (1:500; for NPY)
- Donkey anti-rat Alexa Fluor 488 (1:500; for CD31)
with gentle rocking, protected from light. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 5 days)
5.2 Wash with PTwH, protected from light. (Temperature: RT, Time: 5 × 2 hours)

**6 Nuclear Counterstain**
6.1 Incubation with DAPI (5 µg/mL in PBS) to label nuclei for delineation of hematopoietic cell-rich zones and endosteal regions, protected from light. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)
6.2 Wash with 1× PBS, protected from light. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 × 30 minutes)

**7 Tissue Delipidation and Clearing (BoneClear aqueous clearing)**
7.1 Incubation with BoneClear Reagent B1: 25% (wt/vol) N-butyldiethanolamine (BDEA), 15% (wt/vol) Triton X-100 in distilled water (pH adjusted to 9.0 with HCl), with gentle shaking, protected from light. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 2 days)
7.2 Replace with fresh BoneClear Reagent B1. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 2 days)
7.3 Wash with 1× PBS, protected from light. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 × 1 hour)
7.4 Incubation with BoneClear Reagent B2: 25% (wt/vol) BDEA, 50% (wt/vol) sucrose in distilled water (pH 9.0), with gentle shaking, protected from light. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 2 days)
7.5 Replace with fresh BoneClear Reagent B2. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 2 days)
7.6 Wash with 1× PBS, protected from light. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 × 1 hour)

**8 Refractive Index (RI) Matching**
8.1 Incubation with BoneClear RI matching solution (RIMS): 40% (wt/vol) sucrose, 20% (wt/vol) urea, 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS (RI ≈ 1.46–1.48), with gentle shaking, protected from light. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)
8.2 Replace with fresh RIMS and continue incubation until samples are fully transparent, protected from light. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24–48 hours)

**9 Sample Mounting and Imaging Preparation**
9.1 Transfer cleared bone samples into glass-bottom imaging chambers or custom 3D-printed holders filled with RIMS (RI ≈ 1.46–1.48). Orient femur/tibia longitudinally and calvaria flat for optimal light-sheet or confocal access. Seal with optical adhesive, protected from light. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1–2 hours)
9.2 Allow samples to equilibrate in final RIMS within sealed chamber before imaging, protected from light. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)
9.3 Image using light-sheet fluorescence microscopy (LSFM) or confocal microscopy with appropriate laser lines: 405 nm (DAPI), 488 nm (Alexa Fluor 488 / CD31), 561 nm (Alexa Fluor 568 / NPY), 647 nm (Alexa Fluor 647 / TH). Use 10× or 25× water/glycerol-immersion objectives matched to RIMS RI for whole-bone tile scanning and high-resolution nerve terminal imaging.

**10 Post-imaging Storage**
10.1 Store cleared and imaged samples in RIMS in sealed containers, protected from light. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: up to 3 months)

**Chosen Method:** BoneClear
**Chosen Labeling:** [TH + Alexa Fluor 647, NPY + Alexa Fluor 555, Lectin + Alexa Fluor 488, DAPI]

**Justification:** BoneClear is specifically engineered for mineralized bone tissues (femur, tibia, calvaria) and combines a mild decalcification step with a detergent/urea-based clearing pipeline that preserves antigenicity in hard tissue. Unlike iDISCO+ or uDISCO (which use organic solvents incompatible with prolonged antibody epitope retention in dense bone matrix), BoneClear maintains aqueous conditions throughout, enabling whole-mount immunolabeling of deep bone marrow targets. TH (tyrosine hydroxylase) marks noradrenergic sympathetic terminals; NPY marks sympathetic/peptidergic fibers; Lectin (vascular perfusion or post-fixation luminal labeling) delineates the sinusoidal/arterial vasculature as a reference channel; DAPI provides nuclear counterstain for hematopoietic cell density mapping. The four-channel design (488/555/647/DAPI) is fully compatible with light-sheet fluorescence microscopy (LSFM) and confocal imaging, and the refractive index (RI) matching solution used in BoneClear (fructose/urea-based, RI ≈ 1.48) is well-suited for both bone cortex and marrow cavity.

---

**Protocol Steps:**

**1 Pre-clearing Decalcification**
1.1 Immerse fixed bone samples (femur, tibia, calvaria; post-fixed in 4% PFA) in 10% (wt/vol) EDTA (pH 7.4) in PBS with gentle rocking. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 7 days for femur/tibia; 3 days for calvaria; replace EDTA solution every 2 days)
1.2 Verify decalcification completion by X-ray or needle-penetration test. Rinse samples 3 × 30 min in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 min per wash × 3)

**2 Permeabilization and Pre-treatment**
2.1 Incubation in BoneClear Permeabilization Buffer: 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100, 0.5% (wt/vol) sodium deoxycholate, 0.2% (wt/vol) sodium azide in PBS. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours, gentle shaking)
2.2 Incubation in BoneClear Delipidation Solution: 10% (wt/vol) urea, 1% (vol/vol) Triton X-100, 10% (vol/vol) N-butyldiethanolamine (BDEA) in ddH₂O. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 48 hours, gentle shaking; replace solution at 24 h)
2.3 Wash 3 × 1 hour in PBS + 0.1% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (PBST). (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour per wash × 3)

**3 Endogenous Peroxidase Quenching (optional, for signal background reduction)**
3.1 Incubation in 1% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in PBST to quench autofluorescence from bone matrix. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours, gentle rocking)
3.2 Wash 3 × 30 min in PBST. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 min per wash × 3)

**4 Blocking**
4.1 Incubation in Blocking Buffer: 5% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum (NDS) + 0.5% (wt/vol) bovine serum albumin (BSA) + 0.2% (wt/vol) sodium azide + 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours, gentle rocking)

**5 Vascular Labeling with Lectin (Primary Vascular Channel)**
5.1 Incubation with Lectin conjugated to Alexa Fluor 488 (e.g., Lycopersicon esculentum lectin–Alexa Fluor 488, Vector Labs; 50 µg/mL) in Blocking Buffer. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours, gentle rocking)
5.2 Wash 5 × 2 hours in PBST. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours per wash × 5)

**6 Primary Antibody Immunolabeling (TH and NPY)**
6.1 Incubation with primary antibody cocktail in Antibody Diluent Buffer (1% NDS + 0.5% BSA + 0.2% sodium azide + 0.5% Triton X-100 in PBS):
- Rabbit anti-TH (1:500; e.g., Millipore AB152)
- Sheep anti-NPY (1:400; e.g., Abcam ab36985)
(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 5 days for femur/tibia; 3 days for calvaria; gentle rocking; replace antibody solution at day 3 for long incubations)

8.2 Wash 3 × 1 hour in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour per wash × 3)

9.1 Incubation in BoneClear Clearing Solution A: 20% (wt/vol) urea + 5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 + 10% (vol/vol) BDEA in ddH₂O (RI ≈ 1.42). (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours, gentle shaking, protected from light)

10.2 Replace with fresh RIMS and incubate until samples are fully transparent and equilibrated. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12–24 hours, protected from light)
10.3 Verify RI of RIMS with a refractometer before imaging; adjust fructose concentration if needed to reach RI = 1.48 ± 0.005.

**11 Sample Mounting and Imaging Preparation**
11.1 Mount cleared bone samples in RIMS within a custom 3D-printed or glass-bottom imaging chamber; orient femur/tibia longitudinally and calvaria flat to allow full marrow cavity access by the light sheet. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 min equilibration after mounting)
11.2 Seal chamber edges with silicone grease or UV-curable optical adhesive to prevent evaporation and RI drift during imaging. (Temperature: RT, Time: 15 min curing)
11.3 Image using light-sheet fluorescence microscopy (LSFM) with the following channel assignments:
- 405 nm excitation → DAPI (hematopoietic cell nuclei / cell density reference)
- 488 nm excitation → Lectin–Alexa Fluor 488 (vascular lumen)
- 561 nm excitation → Alexa Fluor 555 (NPY, sympathetic/peptidergic fibers)
- 638 nm excitation → Alexa Fluor 647 (TH, noradrenergic terminals)
Use a 4× or 10× objective with RI-matched immersion medium (RIMS) for whole-bone overview; switch to 25× for high-resolution marrow cavity analysis. (Temperature: RT)

**12 Post-imaging Storage**
12.1 Store cleared, imaged samples in fresh RIMS in sealed tubes wrapped in aluminum foil. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: up to 4 weeks; re-equilibrate in fresh RIMS if RI drift is observed)

**Chosen Method:** BoneClear
**Chosen Labeling:** [TH + Alexa Fluor (546 or 555, anti-rabbit), NPY + Alexa Fluor (647, anti-rabbit or anti-goat), CD31 + Alexa Fluor (488, anti-rat or anti-rabbit), DAPI]

**Justification:**
BoneClear is specifically designed for mineralized bone tissues (femur, tibia, calvaria) and integrates EDTA-based decalcification with a lipid-clearing pipeline optimized for preserving bone marrow architecture and antigenicity. Unlike standard SWITCH (which uses SDS-based delipidation without dedicated decalcification and RI matching for bone), BoneClear achieves high transparency in dense cortical and trabecular bone while maintaining marrow cavity structure. It is compatible with immunolabeling of neural markers (TH, NPY) and vascular markers (CD31), supports deep antibody penetration via active staining steps, and uses a final RI-matching solution (BABB-D4 or equivalent) suitable for light-sheet microscopy. The combination of TH (catecholaminergic marker, sympathetic fibers) + NPY (peptidergic co-transmitter in sympathetic fibers) + CD31 (vascular/endosteal reference) + DAPI (nuclear/marrow architecture) directly addresses the scientific goal of mapping sympathetic innervation in the bone marrow niche without introducing any targets outside the permitted lists.

---

**Protocol Steps:**

**1 Post-fixation Verification and Pre-treatment**
1.1 Confirm samples (femur, tibia, calvaria) are post-fixed in 4% PFA in 0.1 M PBS at 4 °C for 24 hours; if not completed, perform this step now. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 24 hours)
1.2 Wash samples 3× with 0.1 M PBS to remove residual PFA. (Temperature: RT, Time: 10 minutes per wash)
1.3 Trim excess soft tissue from bone surfaces under a dissecting microscope; for femur and tibia, cut epiphyses to expose marrow cavity at both ends to facilitate reagent penetration. (Temperature: RT, Time: as needed)

**2 Decalcification (EDTA-based)**
2.1 Immerse samples in 10% (wt/vol) EDTA (disodium salt, pH 7.4 in 0.1 M PBS) with gentle rocking. Change EDTA solution every 2 days. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 14 days for femur/tibia; 7 days for calvaria)
2.2 Monitor decalcification progress by flexibility test (bone should bend without cracking) and/or X-ray verification. Continue EDTA treatment until fully decalcified. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: as needed)
2.3 Wash samples 3× with 0.1 M PBS to remove EDTA. (Temperature: RT, Time: 15 minutes per wash)

**3 Delipidation and Tissue Clearing (BoneClear pipeline)**
3.1 Incubate samples in BoneClear Clearing Solution A: 25% (vol/vol) N,N,N′,N′-tetrakis(2-hydroxypropyl)ethylenediamine (Quadrol) in distilled water, pH adjusted to 9.0 with HCl, with gentle shaking. (Temperature: 37 °C, Time: 24 hours)
3.2 Replace with fresh BoneClear Clearing Solution A (25% Quadrol, pH 9.0). (Temperature: 37 °C, Time: 24 hours)
3.3 Incubate samples in BoneClear Clearing Solution B: 25% (vol/vol) Quadrol + 25% (wt/vol) urea in distilled water, pH 9.0, with gentle shaking. (Temperature: 37 °C, Time: 24 hours)
3.4 Replace with fresh Clearing Solution B. (Temperature: 37 °C, Time: 24 hours)
3.5 Wash samples 3× with 0.1 M PBS + 0.1% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (PBST). (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes per wash)
3.6 Assess transparency visually; if tissue remains opaque, repeat steps 3.3–3.4 for an additional 24–48 hours. (Temperature: 37 °C, Time: 24–48 hours additional if needed)

**4 Permeabilization and Blocking**
4.1 Incubate samples in permeabilization buffer: 0.1 M PBS + 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 + 20% (vol/vol) DMSO + 0.3 M glycine, with gentle rocking. (Temperature: 37 °C, Time: 48 hours)
4.2 Wash 2× with PBST (0.1 M PBS + 0.2% Triton X-100). (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes per wash)
4.3 Incubate in blocking buffer: 0.1 M PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 + 10% (vol/vol) DMSO + 6% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum (NDS) + 0.5% (wt/vol) casein, with gentle rocking. (Temperature: 37 °C, Time: 48 hours)

**5 Primary Antibody Immunolabeling**
5.1 Prepare primary antibody cocktail in antibody incubation buffer (0.1 M PBS + 0.2% Triton X-100 + 5% DMSO + 3% NDS + 0.5% casein):
- Anti-TH (rabbit polyclonal or monoclonal, e.g., Millipore AB152 or Abcam ab112), 1:400 dilution
- Anti-NPY (rabbit polyclonal or goat polyclonal, e.g., ImmunoStar 22940 or Abcam ab30914), 1:400 dilution
- Anti-CD31/PECAM-1 (rat monoclonal, e.g., BD Biosciences 550274), 1:300 dilution
(Temperature: 37 °C, Time: 7 days with gentle rocking; for calvaria 5 days sufficient)
5.2 Wash samples 5× with PBST (0.1 M PBS + 0.2% Triton X-100) to remove unbound primary antibodies. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour per wash)
5.3 Perform additional overnight wash in PBST with gentle rocking to minimize background. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)

**6 Secondary Antibody Immunolabeling**
6.1 Prepare secondary antibody cocktail in antibody incubation buffer (0.1 M PBS + 0.2% Triton X-100 + 3% NDS):
- Donkey anti-rabbit Alexa Fluor 546 (or 555), 1:500 dilution → labels TH
- Donkey anti-rabbit Alexa Fluor 647 (if NPY primary is rabbit; if goat: donkey anti-goat Alexa Fluor 647), 1:500 dilution → labels NPY
- Donkey anti-rat Alexa Fluor 488, 1:500 dilution → labels CD31
Note: If both TH and NPY primaries are rabbit, use sequential labeling (see step 6.1a–6.1b below) or select primaries from different host species.
6.1a [If sequential labeling required] First incubate with anti-TH (rabbit) primary alone (step 5.1 conditions), wash, then apply donkey anti-rabbit Alexa Fluor 546 secondary alone. (Temperature: 37 °C, Time: 5 days primary; 3 days secondary)
6.1b After washing (5× PBST, 1 hour each), incubate with anti-NPY (goat) primary + anti-CD31 (rat) primary cocktail, wash, then apply donkey anti-goat Alexa Fluor 647 + donkey anti-rat Alexa Fluor 488 secondary cocktail. (Temperature: 37 °C, Time: 5 days primary; 3 days secondary)
6.2 Incubate samples with secondary antibody cocktail (or sequential secondaries as above) in antibody incubation buffer with gentle rocking. (Temperature: 37 °C, Time: 5 days)
6.3 Wash samples 5× with PBST. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour per wash)
6.4 Perform overnight wash in PBST. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)

**7 Nuclear Counterstaining**
7.1 Incubate samples in DAPI solution (5 µg/mL in 0.1 M PBS + 0.2% Triton X-100) with gentle rocking. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)
7.2 Wash 3× with PBST to remove excess DAPI. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes per wash)

**8 Refractive Index Matching**
8.1 Incubate samples in 25% (vol/vol) BABB-D4 [benzyl alcohol : benzyl benzoate : diphenyl ether = 1:2:1 (vol/vol/vol), diluted 1:3 in ethanol] as a graded step. Note: BABB-D4 is the RI-matching solution used in the original BoneClear protocol (RI ≈ 1.52). (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)
8.2 Transfer samples to 50% (vol/vol) BABB-D4 in ethanol. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)
8.3 Transfer samples to 100% BABB-D4 (benzyl alcohol : benzyl benzoate : diphenyl ether = 1:2:1, RI ≈ 1.52) until fully transparent. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12–24 hours)
8.4 Verify optical transparency visually; samples should appear glass-like. If residual opacity remains, continue incubation in fresh 100% BABB-D4. (Temperature: RT, Time: up to additional 12 hours)

**9 Sample Mounting and Imaging Preparation**
9.1 Transfer cleared samples into a glass-bottom imaging chamber or custom 3D-printed holder filled with 100% BABB-D4 for light-sheet fluorescence microscopy (LSFM) or confocal microscopy. (Temperature: RT, Time: as needed for mounting)
9.2 Seal chamber with optical-grade silicone or UV-curable adhesive compatible with BABB-D4 to prevent evaporation and refractive index drift. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes curing)
9.3 Allow samples to equilibrate in imaging medium (BABB-D4) before acquisition to minimize drift. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
9.4 Image using light-sheet fluorescence microscope (e.g., LaVision BioTec Ultramicroscope, Zeiss Lightsheet Z.1, or Miltenyi UltraMicroscope Blaze) with objectives compatible with RI 1.52 immersion medium. Recommended channels: 405 nm (DAPI), 488 nm (CD31/Alexa Fluor 488), 546/561 nm (TH/Alexa Fluor 546), 647 nm (NPY/Alexa Fluor 647). (Temperature: RT, Time: as required per sample)
